## What

The `/admin` platform portal CSS-hides the global nav's middle links (`:root:has([data-admin-sidebar]) [data-global-nav]`, #481), so the only way back to the customer-facing site was the easily-missed Kuruma logo. A platform admin — e.g. the owner previewing hidden beta features (#1161 admin bypass) — gets visually trapped in the dashboard; clicking the view-switch only flips a cookie and re-renders `/admin`, so it feels stuck.

## Fix

Add a discoverable **"← Back to site"** link as the first item in `AdminSidebar`, linking to the locale home (`/$locale`). i18n'd in en/ja/zh (`admin.nav.backToSite`). Visually separated from the portal nav items with a back-arrow icon + divider.

author: blokzdev
body:
## Loop Hardening LH-6 — say-do consistency gate (F3) · closes the phase

The final Loop Hardening PR. The model sometimes narrates one target (e.g. tap "Submit") but its `element_index` resolves to another (e.g. "Cancel") — the **Execution Gap**, which persists even in the largest models and is *the lie a user would authorize* (arXiv:2510.02204). This adds a **deterministic, zero-extra-model-call** gate (on-device-safe) that routes a clear contradiction through the **existing** confirmation sheet.

### What
- **`SayDoCheck`** (pure, JVM-tested) — `CONTRADICTS` iff an element_index-targeted tool, a non-blank resolved name, a **quoted** target in the narration, and **no** quoted target `consistent` (exact / containment / token-set Jaccard / edit-distance≤1, after normalization) with it. `narrationBefore()` scopes to "since the previous ToolUse" by **referential identity** (multi-tool batches can't cross-contaminate).
- **`ActionSummary.targetLabel`** — the bare `element.name` only, **null when blank** (never value/controlType/resourceId): the key FP fix, so an icon button with no a11y name never gates a *correct* tap.
- **Wire-in** — `riskGatePasses` OR-s the say-do term in; the normal call site passes the narration; a contradiction logs `agent_note_saydo_confirm` and routes through `ConfirmationSheet`; deny → `deniedResult` (**no history mutation** → replay byte-exactness preserved).
- **SYSTEM_PROMPT** — name the acted-on control in single quotes (a checkable contract that lifts recall on the on-device tier, no added FP). `agent_note_saydo_confirm` (en + zh).

### Research-grounded (9-agent Ultracode workflow)
Cited: arXiv:2510.02204 (Execution Gap keystone), 2503.18492 VeriSafe Agent (deterministic > LLM-reflection on FP/latency), 2605.01208 Faithful Agent (neutral-on-vacuous = primary FP guard), 2509.21799 D-Artemis (pre-execution placement; we reject its model-based auto-correct to stay replay-safe/on-device), 2509.07553 VeriOS (query-the-human routing), 2503.08679 (verify the quotable token, not the chain), 2503.15937 V-Droid. **Two adversarial `safe=False` findings folded in:** the `targetLabel` FP fix and quoted-only + per-action narration.

### Verification
- **JVM:** `SayDoCheckTest` (16 — match/mismatch/confusable, scroll+set_value, the four FP guards incl. icon-button-null-target, containment/case/punct/token-set, non-targeted-tool skip, `narrationBefore` referential-identity on value-equal ToolUses) + `ActionSummaryTargetLabelTest` (4 — bare name, **null when name blank**).
- `:app:testDebugUnitTest :app:assembleDebug :app:assembleRelease` green, R8 clean, `lintVitalRelease` accepts the new string (zh present).
- **Instrumented on emulator-5556 — 2/2:** `AgentLoopEmulatorTest` (no spurious gate on the normal path). 5554 untouched.
- On-device feel → `VERIFICATION.md` `V-LH-6` (gate fires on a real contradiction; never on correct icon taps).

PR 6 of 6 — **Loop Hardening COMPLETE**; exec-plan moved to `completed/`. (LH-5b streaming-hoist remains in BACKLOG.)

A polished `EmptyState` primitive already existed (`src/components/shared.tsx` — team-logo watermark → glyph fallback, title, body, optional CTA) but only 3 screens used it; the rest hand-rolled their own `text-center py-* … ⚾ … No X Yet` blocks. ## 관련 이슈

close #959

## 작업 배경

관리자 목록 화면마다 page, size, filter query 보존 방식이 달라 목록 경계와 접근성 검증 기준이 흔들릴 수 있었다. eGovFrame `PaginationInfo` 기반의 기존 `EgovPaginationView`를 공통으로 쓰고, 운영성 실행 로그는 `LIMIT/OFFSET` 조회로 page 이동을 처리한다.

## 작업 내용

- `AdminPageRequest`를 추가해 관리자 목록의 page 기본값, size 상한, offset overflow 방지를 공통화했다.
- `EgovPaginationView`에 slice 조회, 현재 page 항목 선택, filter query를 보존하는 링크 생성을 추가했다.
- 공통 Thymeleaf pagination fragment를 만들고 신고, 역, 시설 상태, 현장 검증, 데이터 수집 실행, 배치 실행, 감사 로그, 개인정보 조회 로그, 공통코드, incident 목록에 적용했다.
- 데이터 수집 실행, 배치 실행, 감사 로그, incident는 저장소/서비스에 offset 조회를 추가해 다음 page 판단용 `size + 1` 조회를 사용한다.
- slice 기반 목록의 범위 밖 빈 page에서도 요청 page와 pager 상태가 어긋나지 않도록 보정했다.
- pagination href 생성 시 filter query 값을 URL encode해 역 검색어의 공백, 한글, `&`를 유지한다.
- 현재 저장소에 별도 관리자 사용자 목록과 역할·권한 목록 화면은 없어 신규 화면을 만들지 않았다.

  - `cd backend && ./gradlew test --rerun-tasks --tests 'com.easysubway.common.web.pagination.EgovPaginationViewTest' --tests 'com.easysubway.report.adapter.in.web.FacilityReportAdminPageControllerTest' --tests 'com.easysubway.collection.adapter.in.web.DataCollectionAdminPageControllerTest' --tests 'com.easysubway.admin.batch.adapter.in.web.AdminBatchPageControllerTest' --tests 'com.easysubway.admin.audit.adapter.in.web.AdminAuditPageControllerTest' --tests 'com.easysubway.admin.operations.adapter.in.web.AdminOperationsPageControllerTest' --tests 'com.easysubway.transit.adapter.in.web.TransitMasterControllerTest' --tests 'com.easysubway.transit.adapter.in.web.TransitFacilityAdminPageControllerTest' --tests 'com.easysubway.transit.adapter.in.web.TransitReadOnlyAdminPageModelTest' --tests 'com.easysubway.field.adapter.in.web.FieldVerificationAdminControllerTest' --tests 'com.easysubway.collection.application.service.DataCollectionRunRecorderTest' --tests 'com.easysubway.collection.adapter.out.persistence.JdbcDataCollectionRunRepositoryTest'`: BUILD SUCCESSFUL
  - `cd backend && ./gradlew test`: BUILD SUCCESSFUL
  - `cd backend && ./gradlew clean test --no-daemon`: BUILD SUCCESSFUL

  - `codex review --base origin/main --title "[Feat] 관리자 목록과 검색 PaginationInfo 표준화"`: 최종 re-review actionable 0건

Implements Phase B of #1154 — wires `@lore-vcs/sdk` into the upload path behind a `BlobStore` interface.

Spike verdict: **✅ GO** — see [`spike/1154-lore-verdict.md`](../../blob/main/spike/1154-lore-verdict.md) for full measured evidence.

## Strategy: additive, not replacement

The read path is **unchanged** — `readFile(storagePath)` keeps working because Lore leaves the working copy on disk after commit. No changes to `GET /api/assets/[id]`, range serving, video transcode, or markdown render.

Write flow:
```
writeFile(storagePath, buffer)        ← unchanged
writeFile(fairPath, manifest)         ← unchanged
blobStore.put(ownerDid, storagePath)  ← NEW (non-fatal: upload succeeds even if Lore fails)
```

## Changes

- **`blob-store.ts`** — `BlobStore` interface + `BlobRef` type (storage abstraction seam for #1122 to extend)
- **`blob-store-lore.ts`** — `LoreBlobStore`: per-DID `PQueue` (concurrency=1 for file-lock safety), idempotent `ensureRepo`, koffi FFI via `@lore-vcs/sdk`, process-lifetime `lore.shutdown()` handler
- **`route.ts`** — `blobStore.put()` called after `writeFile`; `loreRef` stored on asset row (nullable)
- **`media.ts` + `migrations/0046_lore_blob_ref.sql`** — nullable `lore_ref TEXT` column
- **`next.config.js`** — `@lore-vcs/sdk` and `koffi` added to `serverComponentsExternalPackages`
- **`package.json`** — `@lore-vcs/sdk@^0.8.3` + `p-queue@^8.0.1`
- **`blob-store-lore.test.ts`** — 11 unit tests (all passing, no live Lore installation required)

## Key design decisions (from spike)

- One Lore repo per DID at `{MEDIA_ROOT}/{didPath}/` — fits existing directory structure with no new paths
- `loreRef` (64-char SHA-256 hex) is the Lore-internal storage pointer — distinct from the DFOS CID that #1122 will add
- Lore failure is non-fatal: upload still succeeds, `loreRef` is null, asset served from working copy
- `@lore-vcs/sdk` uses koffi FFI + pre-built platform DLLs — no node-gyp, one `npm install`

## What this does NOT change

- Any read path in the codebase
- Existing hash-based owner-scoped dedup (line 180-184 of upload route)
- Any `storagePath` reference anywhere
- CID identity, content chains, alias→HEAD — that is #1122 (stacks on this)

## Acceptance

- [ ] Upload succeeds and `assets.lore_ref` is populated with 64-char hex
- [ ] Upload succeeds even when Lore errors (working copy served normally, `lore_ref` is null)
- [ ] `bash scripts/check-schema-migration-sync.sh origin/main` passes
- [ ] All existing upload/serve tests pass unchanged
- [ ] `blob-store-lore.test.ts`: 11/11 passing

body: ## Summary Introduces a pure **`TokenWeighting`** module that normalizes raw input/output tokens to **output-equivalent tokens** via a per-model weight table (reference model = 1.0, unknown model → safe default = the reference weight). Agent-step accounting now records the weighted value alongside raw tokens, and period-usage summation + budget enforcement denominate in output-equivalent tokens — making the advertised "model-aware budget" literally true. (WS2 of #3984.) - **Pure module** `lib/billing/token-weighting.ts` — `MODEL_WEIGHTS` (haiku 1/3, sonnet 1.0 = reference, opus 5.0), `INPUT_WEIGHT` (1/5, the input:output list-price ratio), `resolveModelWeight()` (substring family match, `known` flag), `toOutputEquivalentTokens()` (clamped, total, integer). Unknown model → `DEFAULT_WEIGHT` (= reference, never free, never punitive). Exhaustive table-driven tests. - **Migration 0152** adds `usage_events.weighted_quantity` (nullable integer); Drizzle schema mirror (`usageEvents.weightedQuantity`) in the **same PR** (schema-drift clean). author: jt-mchorse
body:
## Summary
`_split_then` splits a sequential query on `_THEN_SPLIT` (lookahead `then\b` — a **word boundary**), but the per-part cleanup only stripped the connective when it was followed by a literal space (`startswith("then ")`). So a connective followed by punctuation — `Then, ...`, `Then; ...`, `Then- ...` — still split but **leaked** the `Then,` token into the sub-query, contradicting the docstring (*"reads as an independent question"*) and polluting the downstream BM25/dense retrieval query.

Reproduced on main: `_split_then("Do A. Then, do B.")` → `['Do A.', 'Then, do B.']`.

The fix adds `_THEN_PREFIX = re.compile(r"^then\b\W*", re.IGNORECASE)` next to `_THEN_SPLIT` and replaces the `startswith` strip with `_THEN_PREFIX.sub("", s)`, so the cleanup mirrors exactly what the split fires on. `then\b` leaves a content word like "thence" untouched (no boundary), consistent with the split itself.

## Tests (3 new; suite 431 → 435, ruff clean)
- end-to-end `TemplateRewriter` strips `Then,`/`Then;`/`Then-`
- direct `_split_then` leak cases + the plain-space case still works
- "thence" is not false-split (guard on the word-boundary semantics)

Closes #92

No decisions made; memory updated in a separate commit.

body:
## 問題

`OllamaClient.list_vision_models()` 原本靠**寫死的模型名稱關鍵字清單**(`llava`、`qwen2.5-vl`、`vision` 等)判斷哪些是視覺模型。

新版多模態模型(如 **gemma3 / gemma4**)名稱不含這些關鍵字,即使實際支援 vision 也會被漏判,造成:
- `/api/ai/models` 的 `vision_models` 回空陣列
- 「AI 引擎」設定頁的審查模型下拉選不到任何視覺模型
- 「AI 審查」功能形同無法使用本機 Ollama 視覺模型

實測 `gemma4:12b/26b/31b` 經 `ollama show` 確認都具備 `vision` 能力,卻被漏判。

## 修改

改以 Ollama **`/api/show` 回報的 `capabilities`** 為判斷依據(含 `"vision"` 才視為視覺模型),這是官方權威來源。查詢失敗時**退回原本的名稱關鍵字判斷**以維持相容,不會比現況更差。

- 新增 `capabilities(model)`:呼叫 `/api/show` 取得真實能力清單
- 新增 `_looks_vision_by_name(model)`:保留舊的名稱關鍵字判斷作為 fallback
- `list_vision_models()` 改用上述邏輯

## 影響範圍

- 僅動 `backend/app/agent/llm/ollama.py`,1 檔。
- 對既有以名稱命中的視覺模型(llava 等)行為不變(capabilities 也會含 vision)。
- `/api/ai/models` 每次呼叫會對每個模型多打一次 `/api/show`;模型數通常個位數,延遲可接受,未來可再加快取。

## 驗證

重啟後端後 `/api/ai/models` 回傳:

```
vision_models: [gemma4:12b, gemma4:26b, gemma4:31b, qwen2.5vl:7b]
```

author: matt0x6f
body:
## Cascade Scripting v1 — PR10 (stacks on `cascade-scripting`, after PR9 #91)

The React **Scripts** management panel consuming the frozen PR9 backend API, plus one small additive backend change so the panel stays live.

### What's here
- **Backend (additive):** the script `Manager` emits a `script-lifecycle` runtime Wails event on every status transition — enable/disable/reload/unload, watchdog **runaway auto-disable**, and hot-reload of a new script dir — via a new nil-safe `Host.Notify` callback wired in `app.go` to `app.emit(...)`. Mirrors the existing `plugin-lifecycle` pattern. **No new bound methods, no binding regeneration.**
- **Store:** `frontend/src/stores/scripts.ts` — Zustand store (`fetch`/`enable`/`disable`/`reload`/`create`/`openDir`/`clearCreated`, per-row `busy` set, `lastCreatedPath`, `error`) with `initScripts()` that does an initial fetch and subscribes to `script-lifecycle` to refetch. Wired into `main.tsx`.
- **Component:** `frontend/src/components/scripts-panel.tsx` — inventory rows (name, status badge, description, perms, error), enable/disable toggle, reload, a "New script" name input + create, "Open scripts folder", and a created-path reveal.
- **Nav:** new "Scripts" section wired into the settings window (`settings-panel.tsx` type + guard + render case + nav item).

### Design decisions
1. **Extracted component + store** (not inlined like the Plugins pane).
2. **Live status via `script-lifecycle` event** — so a watchdog runaway auto-disable flips the row to red with no user action.
3. **New script → show path + manual "Reveal in folder"** (no auto-popping Finder/Explorer).

### Testing
- Backend: `internal/script` passes with `-race`; `gofmt`/`go vet` clean.
- Frontend: full vitest suite **201/201**; `tsc --noEmit` clean.

### Process
Built via subagent-driven development: per-task implement + spec/quality review, then a whole-branch review (verdict: ready to merge). A final-review pass folded in two store-polish fixes (clear stale error on successful fetch; suppress the empty-state flash while loading), re-reviewed clean.

The plan doc (`docs/plans/2026-06-26-cascade-scripting-v1-pr10.md`) is committed here per the stacked-integration workflow and is `git rm`'d before the integration branch squash-merges to `main`.

### Remaining (post-PR10)
- PR11: public docs (`docs/public/developers/`).

author: anchildress1
body:
## What

Makes Multivert findable by search engines and AI answer engines, without touching the quiz's client-only render path or the Lighthouse perf floor.

> [!NOTE]
> **Deploy was already done.** `release-please.yml` → `deploy-pages.yml` already ships every release to Cloudflare Pages project `multivert` (→ multivert.pages.dev). `v1.2.1` is live. Merging this PR cuts a release-please PR; merging *that* deploys. No pipeline changes needed.

## Changes

- **robots.txt** — split AI crawlers into *retrieval* (allowed: PerplexityBot, OAI-SearchBot, ChatGPT-User, Claude-User/SearchBot, Google-Extended) vs *training* (still blocked: GPTBot, ClaudeBot, CCBot, Bytespider, …). Honors the original "not your training data" stance while opening the surfaces that drive AI citations.
- **llms.txt** — concise, citable summary (quiz pitch, five vert definitions, scoring model, cited sources) for non-JS AI crawlers.
- **app.html** — added `author` (`sameAs`) to the `Quiz` JSON-LD, plus a `WebSite` + `DefinedTermSet` graph defining each vert. Targets "what is an otrovert / omnivert vs ambivert" queries.
- **smoke.spec.ts** — asserts both JSON-LD blocks and their `@type`s.

## Decision: SSR stays off

Tried `ssr=true` to put the full body in the prerendered HTML. It dropped the **mobile Lighthouse perf gate to 0.92** (FCP 1.5s → 2.6s) — below the hard 0.95 floor — because the route CSS lands in the critical path. Inlining and DOM-trimming both still landed at 0.92. Per the "lhci always" rule, kept `ssr=false`. Findability instead rides on meta tags + JSON-LD + llms.txt; Googlebot renders JS for the rest.

## Off-page (manual, can't be done in code)

"Top 10" needs more than markup:
- [ ] Verify the site in **Google Search Console** + submit the sitemap
- [ ] Same in **Bing Webmaster Tools**
- [ ] Earn a few inbound links (the dev.to writeup, GitHub README, anchildress1.dev)
- [ ] Give it 2–4 weeks to index; recheck Search Console coverage

format · lint · typecheck · 252 unit · build · 56 e2e · Lighthouse mobile 0.96 / desktop 100 — all green locally (pre-push gate passed).

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body:
## Summary

Agent-authored PRs (Devin, Copilot) currently sit open waiting for a human to click merge, even when all required checks are green and the ruleset requires 0 approvals — agents aren't permitted to merge into `main` directly. This adds a lean `auto-merge` workflow that squash-merges agent PRs once they're ready.

It does **not** bypass any gate. The merge is attempted via the REST API, so GitHub enforces the full ruleset server-side (required status checks + conversation resolution). A PR that is red, has unresolved threads, or is otherwise blocked returns `405` and is skipped, to be retried on a later run.

```
check_suite completed / schedule (*/5m) / manual dispatch
  └─ list open non-draft PRs → main authored by an allowlisted agent bot
       └─ pulls.merge(squash)   // GitHub enforces checks + thread resolution
            └─ on success: delete head branch
            └─ on 405/409: skip quietly, retry next run
```

Allowlist (humans are never auto-merged): `devin-ai-integration[bot]`, `copilot-swe-agent[bot]`, `Copilot`.

Modeled on the `anokye-labs/plugins` Auto-Flow pattern, intentionally simplified (no merge queue / Copilot dispatch machinery) to fit this repo's lighter check set.

## Related Issue

Closes #365

## Changes

- `.github/workflows/auto-merge.yml` — new workflow (`check_suite` + `schedule` + `workflow_dispatch`) that squash-merges ready agent PRs and cleans up the merged branch.

## Verification

- [x] Build/tests run (if applicable) — n/a, CI-only workflow; no source changed.
- [x] Manual or API verification completed
- Evidence:
  - Ruleset confirmed: `required_approving_review_count = 0`, required checks `dependency-review` / `check-linked-issue` / `pr-title`, conversation resolution required — all enforced server-side at merge, so the workflow can only ever merge an already-green PR.
  - Bootstrap note: this PR itself needs one human merge; once on `main`, the scheduled sweep will auto-merge subsequent green agent PRs.

## Checklist

- [x] Linked issue referenced
- [x] Documentation updated if needed (n/a)

## Summary

- fixes #3145
- batches the primary typed-row compatibility asset through the existing regular column-asset append writer instead of writing it with its own open/sync/close cycle
- lets non-direct-view typed-column part assets use the same regular append queue while preserving direct-view typed-column segment file IDs and alignment
- adds mixed regular-asset append coverage and updates the typed-storage legacy-name allowlist for the new test references

## Scope Boundary

This is an insert/load and column asset publication PR under #3099/#3067. It is not evidence that TreeDB SQL is broadly faster than ClickHouse.

Effect classification:

| area | status |
|---|---|
| insert/load | improved |
| one-shot query execution | regression context only |
| hot prepared execution | not targeted |
| metadata storage/write cost | accounting unchanged; insert-cost upper-bound timer moves with asset preparation |
| general no-metadata scan performance | not targeted |
| storage bytes | unchanged in current evidence |

Direct-view typed-column part assets still use generation-specific direct-view segment IDs. This PR changes batching of writes, not the persisted asset/ref format.

author: scrutineerhq
body:
Edge cases in `QueryReducer::reduce()` where it under-reported tables or risked emitting a non-table token. All "reduce more / leak no more than verb+table".

| input | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `FROM a, b, c` | `SELECT a` | `SELECT a, b, c` |
| `FROM users u, posts p` | `SELECT users` | `SELECT users, posts` |
| `FROM a STRAIGHT_JOIN b` | `SELECT a` | `SELECT a, b` |
| `FROM mydb.wp_posts` | `SELECT mydb` (schema!) | `SELECT wp_posts` |
| `... INTO OUTFILE '/tmp/x'` | `SELECT OUTFILE` | `SELECT <table>` |
| `... INTO @var FROM wp_x` | `SELECT var` | `SELECT wp_x` |

## How
- Tokenizer keeps `.` as a token (so `db.table` resolves to the trailing segment instead of being mistaken for "schema + alias") and collapses `@var`/`@@global` into one token.
- `STRAIGHT_JOIN` added to the table-preceding set; `OUTFILE`/`DUMPFILE` added to the skip-keyword set.
- `extract_tables` resolves qualified refs (`read_table_ref`), captures comma-separated tables, and steps over optional aliases (`skip_alias`).

## Verification
- `php -l` clean (7.4); `phpcs` exit 0.
- Ran the real reducer against **23 cases** (all the above + regression coverage: aliases, JOINs, subqueries, CTEs, INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE, FOUND_ROWS, SHOW, `t.*`) — all green.

Note: the INVARIANTS verification regex is updated to include the DDL verbs the reducer legitimately emits in the docs PR.

## What & why
Makes a board ticket a **durable, reviewable record of an autopilot run** so you can intervene early *and* come back later to diagnose where an agent went wrong. Closes board item `960de3bf` ("Surface autopilot assumptions & direction while it works a ticket").

Previously the plan only lived in a board modal and `agent_notes` only showed on a *failed* board row — there was no single place to see what an agent is assuming/doing while it works.

## Changes
- **`app/views/tasks/show.html.erb`**
  - **Plan & direction** card: `agent_role` label + `board_state` pill, the plan rendered as markdown, and "plan updated <ago>".
  - **Latest agent status**: renders `agent_notes` inline so the agent's last note is visible without opening the board.
  - **Watch live session** link to the task's session conversation (which already streams live), shown only when one exists.
  - Relabel **Comments → Activity & decisions log** (the append-only assumptions/direction trail).
  - Subscribe to a `[@task, :activity]` turbo stream for live page-refresh.
- **`app/models/task_comment.rb`** — `after_create_commit` broadcasts a refresh to `[task, :activity]` so new worklog entries appear live.
- **`app/models/task.rb`** — `after_update_commit` broadcasts to `[self, :activity]`, gated on `plan` / `agent_notes` / `board_state` changes so unrelated saves (e.g. drag reorder) don't refresh. Errors rescued/logged like `broadcast_board`.
- **Tests** — model broadcast tests (TaskComment + Task, incl. a no-broadcast case for unrelated saves) and a new integration test (`test/integration/task_activity_log_test.rb`) covering the new cards, the stream source, the live-session link, the worklog, and graceful fallbacks. Updated one existing board test for the renamed heading.

### Agent write-back discipline (outside this repo)
Part B of the plan adds the prompts that make agents *populate* the trail. These live in global command files (`~/.claude/commands/board-{plan,engineer,debug}.md`), not in this repo, so they are **not in this diff** — they were edited in place to POST a `planner`/`engineer`/`debugger` worklog comment stating key assumptions + direction at the start of work (and a closing note at finish).

## Testing
- Repo suite: `bin/rails test` → **211 runs, 766 assertions, 0 failures**. Rubocop clean on the Ruby files.
- Headless Playwright test leg: **5 cases blocked (0 failed)** — the runner's Chromium failed to launch in-container (`browserType.launch: Target page, context or browser has been closed`), an environment issue unrelated to this change. The equivalent acceptance checks are covered by the new Minitest integration test.

body:
All changes complete. Let me provide the PR description.

## Summary

修复实时对话三处问题：

1. **桌面端 "claude 未正常完成本轮"**：执行失败的错误文案不区分根因，难以诊断。现把 `spawnClaude` reject 的原因（脱敏 + 截断后）回填到 `failConversationTurn`，并区分两类失败：①进程异常退出/超时 → `claude 进程异常退出：<截断 stderr>`；②退出 0 但无完整 assistant 文本 → `claude 退出了但本轮无完整结果（...）`。Web/桌面端直接展示该文案。

2. **Web 端消息始终为空 / 切换页面后自己发送的消息也消失**：原 `chat-thread.tsx` 只渲染 jsonl 解析结果 + 本地 `pending` 乐观气泡。jsonl 在 worker 落地前为空，`pending` 在切换会话/重挂载时被清空——任一发生就看不到消息，claude 失败时也无可见提示。改为同步拉取 `dbMessages`（同 3s 节奏轮询），新增 `dbExtras` 兜底渲染：jsonl 未收录的 user 消息 + 失败 assistant 的 `error_message`。`pending` 增加按 DB 内容去重，避免双显示。

3. **Web 端发送按钮点击后 1-2 秒无响应**：原 `send()` 在 `await postJson` 返回后才 `setInput("")` / `setPending([...])`，造成体感卡顿。改为「先落乐观状态（清输入 + 加 pending），再发请求」；失败时回滚（恢复输入、移除该 pending）。发送成功后立刻 `refreshMeta()` 拉一次 DB 让 `dbExtras` 接管。

## Changes

- `apps/console/app/ui/chat-thread.tsx:54-56` — 新增 `dbMessages` state，承载来自 `/api/conversations/[id]` 的全量消息，jsonl 兜底渲染的数据源
- `apps/console/app/ui/chat-thread.tsx:85-108` — `refreshMeta` 同步写入 `dbMessages`；轮询间隔由 15s 缩到 3s 与 jsonl 同节奏，避免「pending 已清/db 还没来」的空白窗
- `apps/console/app/ui/chat-thread.tsx:146-164` — `pending` 去重新增「textInDb」判定，DB 已有正文即清掉乐观气泡
- `apps/console/app/ui/chat-thread.tsx:181-204` — 新增 `dbExtras`：按 `seq` 升序整理 DB 里 jsonl 未收录的 user 消息 + 失败 assistant，逐条决定是否补显示
- `apps/console/app/ui/chat-thread.tsx:208,459,464-482` — 渲染管线插入 `dbExtras`（在 TranscriptView 后、pending 前），并参与空态判断
- `apps/console/app/ui/chat-thread.tsx:235-273` — `send()` 把 `setInput("")`/`setPending(...)`/`setDraftAtts([])` 全部前置到 `await postJson` 之前；catch 回滚现场；成功后 `void refreshMeta()` 立刻拉取 DB 状态
- `apps/console/app/globals.css:4563-4581` — 新增 `.tx-msg.asst.chat-msg-failed` 失败气泡样式（边框 + 软背景 + 80% 宽度，特异性高于默认 .tx-msg.asst）
- `apps/worker/src/executor.ts:1558-1606` — 捕获 `spawnClaude` 错误到 `spawnError`（截断 500 字），区分两类失败给出更具体的 `errorMessage`，方便 Web/桌面 UI 直接展示根因

author: paddione
body:
## Problem

`gh pr merge --auto` returns immediately — the actual merge happens asynchronously in the background. Previously, Schritt 6.5 of `dev-flow-execute` closed the ticket to `done` right after `--auto`, causing drift: ticket shows `done/shipped` but the PR is still OPEN (often CONFLICTING, with failed CI). This is the same pattern that hit T001140/T001141 and now T001145 / PR #2101 (Mishap T001149-M1).

## Fix

Add a new **Schritt 6.4** between 6 (auto-merge) and 6.5 (close ticket) that polls `gh pr view --json state,mergeStateStatus` until the PR is actually `MERGED`, with a timeout (`MAX_MERGE_WAIT_MIN=15` by default). On `CLOSED` (no merge) or timeout, abort with a clear error so a human can investigate branch-protection or CI failures instead of silently closing a stuck ticket.

Schritt 6.5 is updated to use the already-determined `PR_NUM` from 6.4 (still re-derives it if the step is run standalone), and the inline comment now correctly says "Schritt 6.4 hat bestätigt, dass der PR gemergt ist" instead of the misleading "grüner Auto-Merge nach main schließt das Ticket direkt".

author: riasc
body:
## Why

Two issues with the per-topic C++/Python guide tabs:
1. **Every page reopened on C++.** sphinx-design selects the first tab by default and there were no `:sync:` keys, so a reader's "Python" choice never persisted — making the guide *look* C++-only.
2. **No version signal** that the C++ tabs track genogrove (0.24.7) while the Python tabs track pygenogrove (0.5.0), which lags.

(The recent "no tabs at all" on the live site was a separate, already-fixed issue — RTD builds had been failing since #171; build is green again as of #173.)

## Changes

- `:sync: cpp` / `:sync: py` on all 12 guide tab-sets — pick a language once, it follows across every page.
- Tab labels show their version: **C++ · genogrove 0.24.7** / **Python · pygenogrove 0.5.0**, sourced centrally from `conf.py` (`myst_substitutions`) so a version bump updates all pages at once.

Borrows three process improvements from the ai-website-cloner-template
reference, mapped onto our deterministic-script pipeline:

- State capture: clone-extract.js harvests non-default state rules

author: lance0
body:
## Summary

Completes the #12 send-path work on the IPv6 side. IPv4 is already race-free via `IP_HDRINCL` (#97); this extends the per-probe send-socket strategy — previously macOS-only — to **FreeBSD and NetBSD** for IPv6, so a fast BSD host can no longer collapse an IPv6 trace to a single hop. There is no IPv4-style `IP_HDRINCL` for IPv6, so sending each probe from a fresh socket (one datagram, one hop limit) is the deterministic fix.

With this, **every send path is deterministic by construction** — IPv4 via `IP_HDRINCL`, IPv6 via per-probe sockets on all BSD-derived platforms — so the interim 500µs delay is removed.

## What changed

- **`build.rs` defines a `per_probe_send` cfg** (macOS/FreeBSD/NetBSD) as the single source of truth for "platforms whose async `sendto` needs a fresh socket per probe." It replaces the scattered `cfg(target_os = "macos")` gates in `run_icmp`/`run_udp`/`run_tcp` and the UDP `SO_REUSEADDR` gate. Linux is excluded — its `sendto` never exhibited the race — and keeps one shared socket.
- **IPv6 on FreeBSD/NetBSD now uses per-probe sockets** (the same proven path macOS already used): ICMP/TCP via a fresh raw socket per probe, UDP via a fresh socket re-bound to the flow's source port (with `SO_REUSEADDR` for rapid re-bind).
- **Removed the 500µs `apply_rate_limit` floor.** No path needs it anymore; only the explicit `--rate` delay remains. `apply_rate_limit_explicit` is folded back into `apply_rate_limit`.
- Comments/CHANGELOG/ROADMAP updated; the `--source-ip` fail-fast bind and correlation behavior are unchanged.

## Validation

- ✅ Linux (`per_probe_send` off → shared path, unchanged): build, `clippy --all-targets -D warnings`, fmt, 227 tests.
- ✅ **BSD path type-checked locally** by forcing `RUSTFLAGS='--cfg per_probe_send'` — the FreeBSD/NetBSD per-probe blocks compile and lint clean against the cross-platform socket APIs.
- ✅ CI build/clippy on macOS + FreeBSD compiles and lints the `per_probe_send` path on those real toolchains; the FreeBSD job also runs the existing privileged raw-socket runtime test, confirming raw sends work in that environment.
- ⏳ **Recommended pre-merge check:** a live IPv6 trace on a FreeBSD (and ideally NetBSD) host — the per-probe IPv6 path is a `cfg` extension of the proven macOS path, but a real IPv6 trace is the final confirmation. I couldn't runtime-test IPv6 loopback reliably in CI VMs without risking false failures.

## Notes

## Why

`apps/lantern-garage/lib/tool-logger.js` resolved the repo root one level short:
`path.resolve(__dirname, "..", "..")` from `apps/lantern-garage/lib/` lands in
**`apps/`**, not the repo root (needs three `..`). Every tool-execution log was
written to `apps/data/tool-logs/` instead of the canonical root `data/tool-logs/`,
and the WIP-committing automation then committed a whole stray `apps/data/` tree
duplicating `data/`. This finishes the deferred half of #1296.

## What changed

**Fixes (the two writers that actually produced the *tracked* stray tree):**
- `lib/tool-logger.js` — `REPO` now uses three `..` → writes land in root
  `data/tool-logs/`. The reader (`routes/api-tools-log.js`, the `/api/tools/log/*`
  API) `require`s this same module, so **writer + reader move together**. Added a
  **transitional read-only fallback** to the legacy `apps/data/tool-logs/` path so
  the tool-history API doesn't go blank after the move — historical days still
  read from the old location while new logs accrue at the canonical path. Writes
  always target the canonical dir.
- `lib/dream-chat.js:70` — same off-by-one loading agent personas. It read the
  stale stray `apps/data/contexts/personas.json` (1978 B) instead of the canonical
  root `data/contexts/personas.json` (4265 B, identical schema — same 6 personas
  `lantern,keystone,blinkbug,waterfall,xenon,founder`, fuller prompts). Repointed
  to root. (`lib/mcp-resource-client.js` already read the root copy.)

**Stray tree reconciliation:**
- `git rm --cached` (kept on disk) the 6 remaining stray tracked files:
  `apps/data/contexts/personas.json`, `apps/data/convergence/{records,canary-events}.jsonl`,
  `apps/data/conversations/garage-conversations.jsonl`,
  `apps/data/dreamer/notebooks/orion.jsonl`, `apps/data/tool-logs/2026-06-26.jsonl`.
  Each was verified to be either a duplicate of a canonical root `data/` file or
  pure runtime state, and **the current writers for convergence/canary/conversations/dreamer
  already use the correct three-`..` root path** — so nothing reads these stray
  copies once the two fixed writers stop targeting `apps/data/`.
- `.gitignore`: ignore the whole `apps/data/` tree (so the automation can never
  re-commit it) and the canonical `data/tool-logs/` (now that the logger targets
  it). Removed the now-redundant single-file `apps/data/conversations/...` entry.

## Verification

- `node --check` passes on `server.js` + `cloud-server.js`.
- Logger writes then reads back from root `data/tool-logs/<date>.jsonl` (confirmed
  the self-test landed at repo root, not `apps/data/`).
- Drove the **real `api-tools-log` route handler**: `query` → 200/count, `health`
  → 200/`ok`/`latest_log_exists:true`, `stats` → 200/total. Writer side is
  `lib/tool-runner.js:881`.
- **Fallback proven:** `logger.query({date:'2026-06-26'})` — a day that exists only
  in legacy `apps/data/tool-logs/` — returns its 5 entries via the fallback, so the
  history API stays populated across the transition.
- `dream-chat` personas resolve to `data/contexts/personas.json` and load all 6.
- `git check-ignore` confirms `apps/data/**` and `data/tool-logs/**` are ignored.

There is no dedicated tool-history HTML page; the feature is the `/api/tools/log/*`
API, which the verification above exercises directly.

## Audit of the rest of `lib/*.js` (same off-by-one) — left for a focused follow-up

The grep found ~10 other modules with the same pattern. They're **not** producers
of the tracked stray tree (no data exists at either location on a fresh checkout),
and each one relocates where a *live* deployment reads/writes runtime data — so they
deserve their own verified PR rather than riding along here.

**Self-contained log/metric sinks** (one-line fix each; const is module-local):
- `provider-router.js:14` → `apps/data/provider-calls.jsonl` (feeds router calibration — verify continuity)
- `trading-history-logger.js:22-23` → `apps/data/trading/{trades,signals}.jsonl` (docstring already says the intended path is root `data/trading/...`)

author: brrritscold
body:
Implements **#5** (ADR-0007 ingest authentication) as a shared library adapter consumed by ingest-service (#6) and query-service (#8). No HTTP server here — this is the auth core both services import.

## Module layout
Two new `go.work` modules (KISS, no framework), both depending on `pkg/kernel`:

- **`pkg/platform`** — tiny shared constructors every Go service needs:
  - `NewPool(ctx, dsn)` (pgx/v5 pool, pings) + `AppDatabaseURL()` reading `LOGALOT_APP_DATABASE_URL`
  - `NewRedisClient(ctx, cfg)` (go-redis/v9, pings) + `RedisConfigFromEnv()` reading `REDIS_*`
  - Created now because #6/#7/#8 all need pool+redis; avoids each service re-inlining it (DRY).
- **`pkg/auth`** — the ingest API-key adapter:
  - `Authenticator` (kernel.Authenticator) — full ADR-0007 resolution
  - `KeyStore` (kernel.KeyStore) — tenant-scoped `Lookup` + `Revoke` (busts cache)
  - `IssueKey(...)` — minimal programmatic mint+insert (hashed) for the slice/tests; **full CRUD is wave 2, intentionally not built**

Both kernel ports are satisfied via compile-time `var _ kernel.X = (*T)(nil)` assertions.

## Resolution flow (model.md §4.5 — RLS-safe)
Key format `lgk_<publicId>_<keyId>_<secret>` (confirmed against the dev seed `lgk_dev_devkey001_devsecret0123456789` → publicId=`dev`, keyId=`devkey001`, secret hashed → `api_keys.key_hash`):

1. Parse the key (shape only — no DB) and `SHA-256` the secret. Malformed → reject before any DB work.
2. **Redis cache hit (60s TTL):** constant-time re-verify the presented secret against the cached hash, then return. A cache hit skips Postgres but **never** the secret check.
3. **Cache miss:** resolve tenant slug → `tenant_id` (`tenants`, no RLS — this is the step that *produces* the tenant scope) → **arm RLS** (`SET LOCAL app.tenant_id` via the kernel `WithTenantScope`/`ArmTenant` convention) → tenant-scoped `SELECT … WHERE id = keyId` in the same tx → `subtle.ConstantTimeCompare(sha256(secret), key_hash)` → reject `revoked_at`/`expires_at` → build `kernel.TenantContext{TenantID, PrincipalID=keyId, Scopes}`.

Because RLS is armed for the slug's tenant *before* the lookup, a key id owned by another tenant returns **zero rows** — auth itself runs inside the tenant boundary. `Role` is left empty on purpose: an ingest key is a machine principal authorized by **scope** (`ingest:write`), not an RBAC role.

## Cache semantics
- Key `auth:key:<keyId>` → `{tenant_id, principal_id, scopes, key_hash}`, TTL **60s**.
- **Only successful validations are cached** (no negative caching) so the cache can't confirm the existence of an unknown/invalid key id (enumeration defense).
- `key_hash` is cached so the secret is **re-verified in constant time on every hit** — the hash is `SHA-256` of a high-entropy secret (irreversible), so caching it is not a secret disclosure.
- **Revocation:** `KeyStore.Revoke` deletes the cache entry, so a revoked key stops authenticating immediately. Worst case (cache-bust fails) the row is still revoked and the entry expires within the **60s TTL bound** — the documented, acceptable lag (ADR-0007).

## Security notes (load-bearing)
- Constant-time compare (`crypto/subtle`); length mismatch is a safe non-match.
- Plaintext secret is **never logged or stored** — only its `SHA-256` ever leaves the parse boundary.
- Key lookup runs **inside RLS**; services connect as the **NOSUPERUSER `logalot_app`** role so `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` actually governs the lookup.
- All SQL is parameterized; the GUC is set via the parameterized `set_config(...)` kernel helper.
- Auth errors collapse to "deny" at the edge (distinct sentinels exist for server logs/tests only — no client-facing oracle).

## Test evidence

**Unit** (`go test ./...`, fast, Docker-free) — all green:
- key parsing valid / secret-with-separator / 8 malformed variants
- `SecretHash`↔`hashSecret` agreement; constant-time compare incl. length mismatch
- cache hit skips resolver; cache expiry refetches after TTL (fake clock); cache hit still verifies secret
- wrong-secret / revoked / unknown **not cached**; expired vs not-yet-expired; malformed never touches resolver

**Integration** (`go test -tags=integration ./...`, testcontainers Postgres 16 + Redis 7, random ports for hermeticity) — all green:
```
--- PASS: TestIntegration_Auth (38.21s)
    --- PASS: .../valid_key_resolves_to_correct_TenantContext
    --- PASS: .../cross-tenant_key_id_is_invisible_under_RLS
    --- PASS: .../revoked_key_is_rejected_and_cache_busted
    --- PASS: .../cache_hit_skips_Postgres
    --- PASS: .../expired_key_is_rejected
    --- PASS: .../KeyStore.Lookup_is_tenant-scoped
```
- **Cross-tenant RLS proof:** mint key for tenant A, then present `lgk_<bravo>_<A.keyId>_<A.secret>` (B's slug + A's key id). Resolution arms RLS for B → scoped SELECT of A's key id returns zero rows → rejected. B's own key still authenticates.
- **Cache-hit-skips-DB proof:** authenticate (miss → DB → cache), `DELETE` the row via a superuser pool, authenticate again within TTL → **still succeeds** (served from cache); then bust the cache and confirm it now fails (proves the cache, not a DB fallback, served it).
- Migrations applied into the container via golang-migrate; the app pool connects as `logalot_app` so RLS is real.

## CI
CI stays **unit-only / Docker-free** (integration tests gated behind `//go:build integration`). `make go-fmt` clean, `go vet` clean, `golangci-lint` (v2.12.2, incl. `--build-tags=integration`) reports 0 issues, `go work sync` clean.

## Deferred (out of scope, by design)
JWT/UI sessions, RBAC enforcement, user/tenant CRUD, full key CRUD + HTTP — wave 2 / consumed by #6/#8.

Closes #5

## M1 — YouTube ingestion (resolve → download → play)

Stacked on #1 (M0). Adds the pipeline that turns a pasted YouTube link into a downloaded, playable track — replacing the M0 synth as the audio source.

### M1A — ContinuityCore (pure, unit-tested)
- `YouTubeURL` — parse video/playlist IDs from watch / youtu.be / shorts / embed / music / bare-ID forms
- `AudioStreamSelector` — choose the best audio-only **AAC** stream (AVAudioFile-decodable), highest bitrate
- **39 tests pass** — `cd Packages/ContinuityCore && swift test`

### M1B — iOS pipeline (`App/Continuity/Ingest/`)
- `YouTubeStreamResolver` — wraps **alexeichhorn/YouTubeKit**, maps streams onto the tested selector
- `AudioDownloader` + `AudioCache` — cache-first, atomic publish, temp-file cleanup
- `PreparationQueue` — `@MainActor` queue driving `prepState` (pending → ready/failed)
- `Player` — plays the real downloaded file (reconnects to its format; frame-accurate seek)
- **Add from YouTube** sheet (toolbar +) and per-track prep badges

### Quality — adversarial review
A 5-reviewer workflow flagged candidates; verifiers rejected ~14 speculative ones and confirmed **5 real bugs, all fixed**: real-file seek desync, download race, temp-file leak, `isNativelyPlayable` mis-flag, engine-start fake-playing.

### Live verification (iOS 26 simulator)
Pasted `youtu.be/dQw4w9WgXcQ` → parsed → resolved (selected **AAC itag 140**) → downloaded ~82% → the YouTube `googlevideo` connection throttled to 0 kbps and dropped, and the track correctly transitioned to **`.failed`**. The whole pipeline executes correctly end-to-end; the only gap is YouTube's anti-scraping **download throttling**.

**Next:** ranged/chunked download (HTTP `Range`) to defeat the full-file throttling and complete real playback.

author: montfort
body:
Implements the architecture decision in #332, registered after the Sentinel adopter calibration ([#331](https://github.com/StrangeDaysTech/straymark/pull/331)). The Baton-side prototype.

## What

The declared **`work_verb`** (+ `design_provenance`), captured at authoring, becomes the **sole authoritative classification signal**. Title-scan is removed from the classification path entirely. A unit with **no declared verb is unclassifiable** → routed up to frontier conservatively, with a nudge to declare the verb. Never guessed.

- `signals.rs` — removed `Cue`/`scan_cues`/`CUE_TABLE`/`matches_at_word_start`; added `WorkVerb` (design/implement/audit/operate) + `DesignProvenance` (new/upstream), controlled-vocabulary.
- `classify.rs` — `class: Option<TaskClass>`; verb→class with `implement` + `design_provenance=upstream` → `operator` (residual-cognitive-load); undeclared → `None`. Declared = High confidence.
- `route.rs` — undeclared → frontier (conservative, R1).
- `telemetry.rs` — `conflict_fraction` → `undeclared_fraction` (the actionable nudge); saving now provably rests on declared units (`low_confidence_savings_fraction` → 0).
- `units.rs` — harvest `work_verb`/`design_provenance` from charter frontmatter + follow-up lines.

## Why (adopter evidence)

The Sentinel calibration proved title-substring classification **unsafe**: high+medium precision **0.57** with **4 errors *downward***, all from object-vs-verb collisions (a module *named* `Audit`), incidental tokens (`*.go` filenames, commit hashes, make-target names). The title is unconstrained, schema-less, often-bilingual free text; reinforcing the scan per adopter is an unbounded keyword treadmill (the #321 anti-pattern). Fake savings are worse than an honest gap.

## Verification

- `cargo test -p straymark-baton` ✓ — 78 tests (suite rewritten for the declared-verb model); `clippy` clean; no trace of `scan_cues`/`Cue` left.
- **Sentinel dogfood** (`route --dry-run`, read-only, `git status` intact): the legacy corpus declares no verbs → **100% undeclared → all frontier → 0 saving → "not routable" + "declare a work_verb" nudge.** The truthful clean-cut behaviour — the gap is an action, not a fake number.

## Scope boundary (deferred on purpose)

- **Framework graduation** — `work_verb`/`design_provenance` as first-class governance fields (schemas, templates, validator nudge) is a `fw-X.Y.Z` change, gated on schema ratification (the adopter asked not to instrument against an unratified schema).
- Finer-grained declaration (batch/task have no frontmatter slot), **forward-validation** (StrayMark's job, varied corpus), and B2 auto-assist for `design_provenance` are tracked under #332.

Closes the prototype step of #332.

## What

`aida ps`'s "Orphaned In-Progress specs" pass listed every In-Progress spec with no live session. Since BUG-626 made an epic's status a child-rollup, In-Progress **epics** are common — and they never hold a spec-scoped lease, so they *all* read as "orphaned" = noise.

## Fix

Skip rollup / stateless requirement types (`Epic`, `Folder`, `Meta`) in the orphan walk in `handle_ps`, via a new pure, unit-testable predicate `ps_orphan_excluded_type`. Only real work-item In-Progress specs (task/story/bug/functional/…) without a live session now surface.

## Summary

- **SKILL.md** — comprehensive rewrite of `b20-factory-indexer` spec:
  - Confirmed addresses: Factory (`0xB20f…`), Activation Registry (`0x8453…0001`), Policy Registry (`0x8453…0002`)
  - 5-step detection flow: prefix → `isB20()` → `isB20Initialized()` → metadata → manual review. Prefix alone is not sufficient.
  - Activation Registry gate: check before any mainnet discovery run — if B20 not yet active, return `b20_mainnet_active: false` and exit cleanly without indexing
  - Factory helper interfaces documented (`isB20`, `isB20Initialized`, `getB20Address`) — selectors marked as needing on-chain ABI verification before hardcoding
  - Testnet demo note: Base Sepolia proves the full pipeline; Zetta is mainnet-ready when real activated tokens appear

- **`b20-client.ts`** — constants and infrastructure guard:
  - `B20_FACTORY`, `B20_ACTIVATION_REGISTRY`, `B20_POLICY_REGISTRY` exported constants
  - `B20_INFRASTRUCTURE_ADDRESSES` — a `Set` of all three addresses lowercase; prevents factory/registry from ever being treated as indexable tokens
  - `fetchB20FactoryLogs` filters infrastructure addresses out of extracted candidates

- **`index-b20` route** — runtime guard:
  - Hard 400 if the requested `address` is a factory or registry precompile — the B20 factory cannot be accidentally indexed as a token

author: robobun
body:
Bun's `TextDecoder` diverges from the [Encoding Standard](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/) in several places:

```js
new TextDecoder("iso-8859-5")
// RangeError: Unsupported encoding label "iso-8859-5"

new TextDecoder("replacement")
// succeeds; the spec, Node, and every browser require a RangeError here

[...new TextDecoder("euc-jp").decode(Uint8Array.of(0x8f, 0xa1, 0x61, 0xa1, 0xa1))]
// ["\ufffd", "a", "\ufffd"]   spec: ["\ufffd", "a", "\u3000"]

[...new TextDecoder("big5").decode(Uint8Array.of(0x81, 0x40, 0x41))]
// ["\ufffd", "A"]             spec: ["\ufffd", "@", "A"]

const d = new TextDecoder();
d.decode(Uint8Array.of(0xef), { stream: true }) + d.decode(Uint8Array.of(0xbb, 0xbf, 0x41))
// "\ufeffA"                   spec: "A"
```

### Cause

- 16 of the standard's single-byte encodings have no decode table. WebKit gets them from `TextCodecICU`, which Bun does not build, and `TextCodecSingleByte.cpp` only had tables for the other ten. The `TextDecoder` label table in `EncodingLabel.rs` is also incomplete: 97 of the standard's 228 labels are rejected, the non-standard `iso_8859-11` is accepted, and the `replacement` encoding (which the constructor must reject) is constructible.
- Bun's `TextCodecCJK.cpp` is a fork that predates several upstream WebKit spec fixes. EUC-JP clears its `jis0212` flag only on the in-range path, so an aborted JIS X 0212 sequence makes the next, valid JIS X 0208 pair decode through the wrong index (silent mojibake, not a U+FFFD). Big5 does not restore the ASCII trail byte of an unmapped pair. ISO-2022-JP misses a replacement character for an error from the second restored escape byte in non-fatal mode, and appends the escape lead verbatim at end of stream instead of reprocessing it through the decoder output state.
- The Rust UTF-8 and UTF-16 paths strip the BOM by checking the first bytes of each chunk. Per the spec the BOM is the stream's first output code point, so a BOM split across `{stream: true}` chunks was not stripped and BOM-shaped bytes at the start of a later chunk were wrongly stripped (#25495).

### Fix

- `TextCodecSingleByte.cpp`: add the 16 decode tables, generated from the spec's index files. The generator reproduces Bun's ten existing tables byte for byte, which is how I validated it.
- `EncodingLabel.rs`: rebuild the label table from the spec's `encodings.json` so it carries exactly the 228 standard labels. The `TextDecoder` constructor now rejects the `replacement` encoding.
- `TextCodecCJK.cpp`: port the four upstream WebKit fixes (the EUC-JP `jis0212` hoist, the Big5 trail-byte restore, the two ISO-2022-JP changes, and the `decodeCommon` prepended-byte cleanup on the fatal early return).
- `TextDecoder.rs`: track `BOM seen` and `do not flush` per the spec and suppress only the stream's first `U+FEFF`, at the code point level.

### Verification

`test/js/web/encoding/text-decoder-wpt.test.ts` is now a faithful port of WPT's `single-byte-decoder.window.js` (all 28 single-byte encodings, every byte), `textdecoder-labels.any.js` (all 228 labels), and `api-replacement-encodings.any.js`. Regression tests for the CJK and BOM bugs sit next to the existing coverage in `text-decoder-cjk.test.ts` and `text-decoder.test.js`. 134 of them fail on `main`.

Beyond the committed tests, I ran a differential sweep of Bun against `encoding_rs` 0.8.35 (Firefox's Encoding Standard implementation) and found zero divergences after this change. Node's built-in `TextDecoder` is not a reliable oracle here: it delegates the legacy encodings to ICU, which is itself off-spec on Big5 and on EUC-JP error recovery.

<details>
<summary>Differential sweep details</summary>

For each of the 38 constructible encodings: every 1- and 2-byte sequence, 3- to 5-byte sequences over an alphabet of the decoder-state boundary bytes, two-chunk streaming splits of the 5-byte set, the fatal-mode 2-byte set, and the BOM/chunking permutations. About 13.5 million cases in total, all byte-for-byte equal to `encoding_rs`. The same sweep on `main`, over the 23 encodings it can construct, diverges on 39,625 big5 cases, 162 euc-jp cases, 858 iso-2022-jp cases, and the split-BOM handling of utf-8, utf-16le, and utf-16be; the other 16 encodings cannot be constructed at all.

</details>

Two existing tests asserted the pre-spec behavior of `new TextDecoder("replacement")` succeeding; they now assert the `RangeError` the spec requires.

#31726 adds the same 16 single-byte tables. This change additionally covers the label table, the `replacement` rejection, the CJK decoder fixes, and the BOM handling, but I am happy to rebase on top of that PR if landing it first is preferred.

Fixes #6084
Fixes #20683
Fixes #25495

body:
## Problem

Login POST requests from `web-production-40d5e.up.railway.app` fail with a 403 CSRF verification error. Django's CSRF middleware validates the `Origin` header against `CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS`, which is separate from `ALLOWED_HOSTS` — so even though the Railway domain was listed in `ALLOWED_HOSTS`, Django still rejected the form submission.

## Solution

Added `CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS` to `portfolio_project/settings.py` with wildcard entries for `https://*.up.railway.app` and `https://*.railway.app`. This explicitly tells Django's CSRF middleware to accept POST requests originating from Railway domains, resolving the 403 on login.

### Changes
- **Modified** `portfolio_project/settings.py`

author: stlim0727
body:
## Follow-up to #241

After #241 wired ccache for real, the first **warm** APK build (run `28281642054`, same commit as the seed) only hit **29%**:

```
Cacheable calls:  286 / 290 (98.62%)
  Hits:            84 / 286 (29.37%)   ← Direct 84/84, Preprocessed 0
  Misses:         202 / 286 (70.63%)
```

`Direct 29% / Preprocessed 0%` on an identical commit + prebuild is the classic **"cwd is in the hash"** miss: Gradle/NDK compiles each module from a per-run `android/.cxx/<hash>/<abi>` directory, so the same source keys differently run-over-run. `CCACHE_BASEDIR` relativized paths in the command line but not the build cwd.

Build-step timing so far: original ~9 min → seed (cold) 10m49s → warm 7m10s. The drop to 7 min is mostly the removed release-lint (~2 min); ccache was only half-pulling its weight.

## Change

Add to the build env on **both** `android-apk.yml` and `android-screenshots.yml`:
- `CCACHE_NOHASHDIR=true` — drop the build dir from the hash. Only affects debug-symbol paths (irrelevant for an internal debug-signed APK).
- `locale` added to `CCACHE_SLOPPINESS` — a runner locale change can't bust the cache.

## Expected impact

Warm-build ccache hit rate should climb toward ~90%, so the ~70% of native compiles that still ran cold become cache hits and the `Build release APK` step should drop from ~7 min toward ~4 min.

## Verification

Will run a seed + warm build pair after merge and confirm via the `ccache stats` step that the hit rate jumped. (The seed run is needed because NOHASHDIR changes the cache keys, so the existing ccache entries won't match.)

author: martingale42
body:
## Summary

Fix `VerticalHorizontalFilter` to respect its `period` window.

The `prices` deque is declared with a fixed `MAX_PERIOD` (1024) capacity, but the
window was never bounded to `period`. As a result the `max`/`min` used in the VHF
calculation folded over every retained price (up to 1024) instead of the last
`period` bars, so the value diverged once more than `period` inputs were seen.

This mirrors the fix applied to `DonchianChannel` in #4239: evict the oldest price
once the window reaches `period` before pushing, matching the Cython reference
which uses `deque(maxlen=period)`.

## Tests

- Added `test_value_respects_period_window` (an early spike must leave the window;
  buggy result = 33.0, fixed = 2/3).
- Existing tests pass unchanged. `test_value_with_ten_inputs` did not catch the bug
  because its min value appeared at both an evicted and a retained position.

```

author: aloyshf
body:
## Summary

Closes #83.

本 PR 为全部 26 款游戏的人机模式增加统一的四档 AI 难度调节：**简单、普通、困难、大师**。普通档以改造前的 AI 能力为基准；玩家可在对局过程中修改难度，新的档位从 AI 的下一次决策开始生效，不需要重开对局。

## Problem

改造前各游戏的 AI 强度参数分散且写死在实现中：

- 搜索型游戏固定搜索深度或时间预算；
- 围棋固定蒙特卡洛模拟次数；
- 卡牌和部分棋盘游戏固定使用单步启发式；
- 飞行棋虽然展示了三档难度，但该值没有进入 AI 决策，电脑实际始终随机选择飞机；
- 所有游戏都缺少对局中的统一难度入口。

因此玩家无法根据自身水平调整电脑强度，各游戏未来调整难度时也容易出现重复 UI 和不一致的交互。

## UX and runtime behavior

### Unified control

新增 `apps/common/ai-difficulty.js` 作为全站共享组件：

- 统一等级值：`easy`、`normal`、`hard`、`master`；
- 统一中文文案：简单、普通、困难、大师；
- 默认档位为普通；
- 仅在人机模式显示，双人和联网模式隐藏；
- 所有 26 个游戏页面复用同一个控件、样式和状态 API；
- 飞行棋原有未生效的三档控件已移除，改为使用共享组件。

### Live switching semantics

难度是运行时全局状态。每个 AI 在开始一次决策时读取当前等级，因此：

1. 玩家修改档位后不重置棋盘、回合或玩家身份；
2. 新档位从 AI 下一次决策开始生效；
3. 已经开始执行的当前 AI 动作不被取消；
4. 无需引入 Web Worker 或可中断搜索，避免扩大并发状态管理复杂度。

组件会派发 `ai-difficulty-change` 事件，并提供 `getLevel()`、`setLevel()`、`setMode()`、`getProfile()` 等公共 API，便于后续扩展持久化或设置面板。

## Difficulty design

四档不是单纯修改动画等待时间，而是按不同 AI 类型调整实际决策质量。

| AI 类型 | 简单 | 普通 | 困难 | 大师 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Alpha-Beta / Minimax | 随机合法动作 | 原搜索深度 | 增加搜索深度 | 最高深度或更长时间预算 |
| 迭代加深搜索 | 随机合法动作 | 原时间和深度上限 | 提高时间/深度预算 | 使用最高预算 |
| 围棋蒙特卡洛 | 随机合法落子 | 每候选 20 次模拟 | 每候选 50 次模拟 | 每候选 100 次模拟 |
| 单步启发式棋类 | 随机合法动作 | 原评分策略 | 增强位置/推进评分 | 增加后续局面或对手行动评估 |
| 卡牌游戏 | 候选动作随机化 | 原单步风险策略 | 避免明显亏损交换 | 更严格规避负收益交换 |
| 飞行棋 | 偏向较差候选 | 保持原随机水平 | 从前两名候选中选择 | 选择最高进度候选 |
| 大富翁 | 高现金储备、保守投资 | 原资金阈值 | 更积极购买和升级 | 最积极的资金使用策略 |

### Search-based games

中国象棋、国际象棋、国际跳棋、斗兽棋、将棋以及多个童年棋盘游戏根据档位调整搜索深度、迭代上限或搜索时间。普通档保留原参数，困难和大师逐级提高预算。

### Heuristic games

黑白棋、五子棋、中国跳棋和军棋在原有评分基础上增加边角价值、中心控制、后续移动潜力、推进方向等档位差异。简单档使用合法候选随机化，普通档保持原决策路径。

### Solved/small games

井字棋原 AI 已经使用完整 Minimax，无法在普通档之上继续获得理论强度。为保持四档可辨识度：

- 简单：随机合法动作；
- 普通：约 8% 可控失误率；
- 困难：约 2% 可控失误率；
- 大师：0% 失误，保持完整 Minimax。

测试环境未挂载运行时难度组件时仍保持原有确定性，避免随机行为破坏规则回归测试。

### Card games

六款卡牌游戏复用 `apps/common/card-game-core.js` 的难度参数。共享的吃子、翻牌和移动选择器统一处理随机化与风险阈值；军师旅团营和刀杀鸡继续保留各自的夺旗、武器协同等专有策略。

### Dice games

- 飞行棋现在会把可选飞机的状态和进度传给 AI，困难/大师不再纯随机；
- 大富翁的购买和升级逻辑改为调用统一的 NPC 决策入口，并按档位使用不同现金储备阈值。

## Changes

- `apps/common/ai-difficulty.js` — 统一难度枚举、控件、样式、模式显隐和运行时 API；
- `apps/common/card-game-core.js` — 卡牌 AI 共享难度策略；
- `apps/*/*/ai.js` — 26 款游戏分别接入搜索深度、模拟次数、评分、随机度或资金策略；
- `apps/*/*/index.html` — 全部游戏加载共享组件；
- `apps/dice-game/flying-chess/*` — 删除无效旧控件并接入真实飞机评分；
- `apps/dice-game/monopoly/*` — 购买/升级接入分档 NPC 策略；
- `apps/common/ai-difficulty.test.js` — 共享 API 单元测试；
- `apps/common/ai-difficulty-coverage.test.js` — 自动验证 26 个页面和 26 个 AI 文件均完成接入；
- `README.md` / `index.html` — 同步四档能力说明，并修正实际游戏数量为 26。

## Verification

- `npm test` ✓ — 33 个测试文件、1808 个测试全部通过；
- `npm run lint` ✓ — 0 errors（保留仓库现有 warnings）；
- `npm run build:dist` ✓ — Web/Tauri 前端分发资源构建成功；
- `git diff --check` ✓；
- 覆盖检查 ✓ — 26/26 游戏页面加载共享组件，26/26 AI 实现读取难度；
- `npx vitest run --coverage` 未执行：仓库当前未安装 `@vitest/coverage-v8`，现有 CI 也未配置覆盖率门禁。

## Trade-offs

- 搜索仍在浏览器主线程中同步执行。困难和大师档可能比普通档有更长思考时间，但都设置了受控的深度或时间上限；
- 本 PR 的“随时切换”明确为下一次 AI 决策生效，不取消已经开始的当前决策；
- 普通档优先保持现有玩家体验，困难和大师在现有算法框架内增强，不引入外部棋力引擎或服务端依赖。

## Notes for reviewer

建议重点检查：

1. 任意人机游戏开始后，右下角显示统一难度控件；
2. 双人和联网入口不会显示控件；
3. 对局中切换难度不会重置当前局面；
4. 飞行棋不再显示旧的三档设置；
5. 搜索型游戏的大师档思考时间是否符合期望。
## Sonar follow-up

| --- | --- | --- |
| `69a26a1` | `javascript:S3776` | Extracted capture/move candidate collection and scoring helpers to reduce cognitive complexity without changing card AI scoring behavior. |

body:
## Summary

Adds **template mode** to the AI site generator (creative mode preserved), with two big additions in the latest commit: **AI smart template matching** and **10 new >10k-star enterprise templates** (library is now **18**).

### 1. AI smart template matching
Users no longer have to pick a template. The form now defaults to **「✨ AI 智能匹配」**; the agent reads the brief (+ any product images) and auto-selects the best-fit template, falling back to the default if the reply is unusable. Manual selection is still available.

```ts
// site-templates.ts — compact, LLM-friendly catalog used for matching
landingTemplateCatalogForPrompt() // "- <id> — "<name>" (<category>): <intent>" per line

// generate.ts — runTemplateGeneration()
const wantsAutoMatch = !merchant.landingTemplateId
  || merchant.landingTemplateId === AUTO_LANDING_TEMPLATE_ID // 'auto'
const template = wantsAutoMatch
  ? await pickTemplateForBrief(merchant, imageDataUrls, emit) // LLM -> {"id","reason"}
  : getLandingTemplate(merchant.landingTemplateId) ?? getLandingTemplate(DEFAULT_LANDING_TEMPLATE_ID)
```

`pickTemplateForBrief()` emits a `match` step + a Chinese log line with the chosen template and the model's one-sentence reason, then `fill` runs as before.

Verified end-to-end against the live relay — 8/8 briefs matched to the right template:

| brief | picked |
|---|---|
| 高端野山参抗老护肤品牌 | `d2c-brand` |
| scheduling SaaS, book via shared link | `cal-booking` |
| 开源 Postgres 平台（auth/storage/edge） | `supabase-dev` |
| 极简潮流男装独立站，大图选品 | `medusa-store` |
| personal finance / net-worth app | `maybe-fintech` |
| e-signature for legal teams | `documenso-trust` |

body:
## Summary

Phase 3 — Docker + CI/CD. Full containerization + automated deployment pipeline.

## What's included

### 1. Multi-stage Dockerfile
- **3 targets**: `app`, `worker`, `realtime` (single Dockerfile, multiple images)
- Stage 1 (deps): `bun install --frozen-lockfile`
- Stage 2 (builder): `prisma generate` + `next build` (standalone)
- Stage 3 (runner): `oven/bun:1.2-slim`, **non-root user** (`nextjs:nodejs`)
- Health checks on all 3 targets
- Size target: <500MB per image

### 2. `docker-compose.yml` (dev)
- `app` (:3000), `worker` (:3002), `realtime` (:3003), `redis` (:6379)
- PostgreSQL commented out (enable in Phase 4)
- Health checks on all services
- Volume for SQLite DB (`app-db`)

### 3. `compose.production.yaml`
- **Immutable images** (no source bind mounts)
- **Internal-only Redis network** (not exposed externally)
- **Caddy reverse proxy** with auto-TLS
- **Migration runner** (one-shot, runs `prisma db push` before app starts)
- **Resource limits** (app: 1G/1CPU, worker: 512M/0.5CPU)
- **app replicas: 2** (horizontal scaling)
- `restart: always`

### 4. `Caddyfile.prod`
- Automatic HTTPS (Let's Encrypt)
- Security headers (HSTS, X-Frame-Options, CSP)
- WebSocket upgrade for `/socket.io/` → `realtime:3003`
- Reverse proxy `/` → `app:3000`
- JSON access logs + gzip/zstd compression

### 5. Scripts
- `scripts/backup.sh` — SQLite/PostgreSQL backup + .env encryption + S3 upload + 30-day retention
- `scripts/restore.sh` — restore from backup (with confirmation prompt)
- `scripts/rollback.sh` — re-deploy previous Docker image tag

### 6. CI/CD
- **`.github/workflows/ci.yml`**: Docker Build job **ENABLED** (was `if: false`)
  - Builds all 3 targets (app, worker, realtime) on every PR
  - GHA cache for faster rebuilds
- **`.github/workflows/deploy.yml`**: build + push to GHCR + SSH deploy
  - Triggers on push to `main`
  - Builds 3 images, pushes with commit SHA tag + `latest`
  - SSH to production server, `docker compose pull && up -d`
  - Health check after deploy

### 7. `.dockerignore`
- Excludes `node_modules`, `.next`, tests, research, screenshots, `.env`, `db`
- Smaller build context = faster builds

### 8. `docs/STAGING_ACCEPTANCE.md`
- Pre-deploy checklist
- Docker Compose validation
- Smoke tests (all views)
- Security checks (headers, auth, SSL)
- Observability checks (metrics, health, Sentry)

- Rollback readiness
- Sign-off section

`AgentService.ChatStreamWithTools` 演示设计文档 5.5 的完整装配：

```go
all, _   := agent.LoadAllSkills(s.SkillsDir)
enabled  := agent.FilterEnabled(all, req.Skills)
tools    := MCP工具(转 agent.Tool, 按 req.MCPTools 过滤) + agent.SkillTools(enabled)  // L2
runner   := agent.NewSkillRunner(enabled, s.SkillBuilder, s.SkillTimeout)
dispatch := agent.CombinedDispatcher(runner, s.Tools.CallTool)   // skill.* 走脚本，其余走 MCP
history  := [system: BuildSystemPromptWithSkills(req.Mode, enabled)] + [user]  // L1，统一注入
return agent.RunReActLoop(ctx, req.Provider, tools, nil /*skills 已注入*/, history, 8, s.Transport, dispatch, onDelta)
```

- `ToolSource` 接口抽象 MCP 来源，`var _ ToolSource = (*mcpconn.Manager)(nil)` 编译期断言 SDK 薄封装满足它（单测可注入内存假实现）。

author: milderdb
body:
Refactor only — no behaviour change in the default build.

## What
- Move the startup logic out of `main()` into an importable `app.Run()`.
- `main.go` now just calls `app.SetVersion(version)` + `app.Run()`.
- Add a generic `app.RegisterService(func(context.Context))` hook. Registered funcs are started as goroutines bound to the run context, run alongside the web UI and marge listeners, and keep the process alive via the same WaitGroup.

## Why
It lets the exact same binary be composed from an external wrapper that registers extra long-running tasks, so an add-on can share this one Go runtime instead of running a second process (the speakers are RAM-tight). `app` has no knowledge of what registers; nothing is registered by default, so the stock `retouch` build is byte-for-behaviour identical.

## Notes
- Pure refactor: `go build ./...` and `go vet ./app/ .` pass (frontend `dist` embed unchanged).
- No new dependencies.

author: kushaldas
body:
Fixes #12, an inline <xs:simpleType> whose <xs:restriction base="..."> points at a named list type never inherited is_list, so an xs:length facet counted characters instead of list items. A 3-item list constrained to length 3 was rejected because the validator saw the character count, not the item count.

The parser leaves is_list=false for a restriction over a user-defined base (it only records the base local name), and the existing list- inheritance pass in builder.rs only propagated is_list between named types in validator.types -- it never reached the anonymous inline type embedded in an element declaration.

- builder.rs: build a list_bases map (named simple types that are list types, with their resolved item type/facets) and thread it into the inline list-resolution pass.
- facet_resolution.rs: resolve_inline_list_item_facets now inherits is_list/item_type/item_facets from a named base list type before resolving item facets, covering anonymous inline types in element declarations and complex-type particles.
- tests: add xsd_list_inheritance regression test.

## 🧠 Peer · Daily Maintenance Report — Run 2

**Saturday, 2026-06-27 · GMT+2 · 2 days tracked**

**Health: 9/10** — Codebase is healthy and stable; the last open reliability gap from Run 1 (mid-stream SSE error swallowing) is now closed on both providers. No new issues introduced since Run 1's merge.

---

### ✅ Fixed (2)

**HIGH · `server/handleChat.js` · `streamAnthropic` · lines ~88–105**
- **Problem:** The Anthropic SSE parse loop ran `JSON.parse` inside a `catch {}` and only handled `content_block_delta`. A mid-stream `{"type":"error",...}` event (e.g. `overloaded_error`) was silently swallowed, so the user received a truncated answer ending with `done:true` and **no error surfaced**.
- **Fix:** Restructured the loop — `JSON.parse` now sits in its own try/catch that only `continue`s on malformed JSON. A parsed `event.type === "error"` throws `apiError(502, ...)` **outside** that catch, propagating to `handleChatRequest`'s catch, which emits `sendEvent(res, { error })` + `res.end()`. No double `res.end()` (the throw precedes the loop's own end).
- **Verified:** Confirmed the Anthropic SSE error-event shape (`data: {"type":"error","error":{"type","message"}}`) against the claude-api skill docs before fixing. `vite build` PASS · 17/17 tests · server boots + HTTP 200.

**HIGH · `server/handleChat.js` · `streamOpenAI` · lines ~155–172**
- **Problem:** Same gap on the OpenAI path (mid-stream errors arrive as `{"error":{...}}`).
- **Fix:** Symmetric restructure — parse in its own try/catch, throw `apiError(502, event.error.message)` on a detected error object. `[DONE]` handling unchanged (still checked before parse).
- **Verified:** Same suite as above.

### ⚠️ Flagged (0)
The sole open flag from Run 1 (this SSE gap) is resolved. Nothing new held back.

body:
This pull request refactors the home page to use a server component for authentication and role detection, and moves the main UI logic into a new client component. It also updates how user roles are passed to the `LoginButton` and removes the `role` field from certain API responses and types. These changes improve the separation of server/client logic and streamline role handling throughout the codebase.

**Home page refactor and role handling:**

* The main page (`page.tsx`) is now a server component that reads and verifies the user token from cookies, extracts the user role, and passes it as a prop to a new `HomeClient` component. (`prsweb/src/app/page.tsx` [prsweb/src/app/page.tsxL1-R20](diffhunk://#diff-687261a5286e37524098f4b3374d91e45b6e267b8469934f4b8583b2b94c8851L1-R20))
* The main UI logic previously in `page.tsx` is moved to `HomeClient.tsx`, which is a client component that receives the `role` prop and renders the homepage. (`prsweb/src/components/HomeClient.tsx` [prsweb/src/components/HomeClient.tsxR1-R117](diffhunk://#diff-c5f06af67d986633bcfa4249d8244a8d2a9e92a9ee1bf47869631be10e012b63R1-R117))
* The `LoginButton` component is updated to accept the `role` prop directly, instead of reading it from the user store, ensuring it always reflects the server-authenticated role. (`prsweb/src/components/LoginButton.tsx` [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-47406bfa746ac6c8f583e2d513b339a23513697376b7fc9270558892ee3732a3L8-R8) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-47406bfa746ac6c8f583e2d513b339a23513697376b7fc9270558892ee3732a3L44-L45)

**API and type changes:**

* The `role` field is removed from the responses of the `/api/auth/me` endpoint for both mentors and mentees, as the role is now handled elsewhere. (`prsweb/src/app/api/auth/me/route.ts` [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-fb3439a7c66cb4c4c2190200f6b3056a3db0a535fafbce93119ab24137b2f173L60) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-fb3439a7c66cb4c4c2190200f6b3056a3db0a535fafbce93119ab24137b2f173L106)

**Other improvements:**

author: albertdobmeyer
body:
## What

`govulncheck` on `infra/proxy/goproxy/` found **24 source-reachable** stdlib advisories (the repo had guessed "9") — every one a patched-toolchain fix, because the goproxy built on **go 1.23.0**. `vault-proxy` is the L7 chokepoint and **Tier-2 release-gating** ([`known-advisories.md`](../blob/main/docs/known-advisories.md)), so it must stay advisory-clean.

## Fix (at the root, not per-CVE)

| Change | From → To | Clears |
|---|---|---|
| `go.mod` `go` | `1.23.0` → **`1.25.11`** | all 24 reachable stdlib advisories (max "Fixed in": GO-2026-5039/5037) |
| `golang.org/x/net` | `v0.43.0` → **`v0.56.0`** | the one reachable *module* vuln, GO-2026-4918 (`x/text` → v0.38.0 alongside) |
| Containerfile builder | `golang:1.23-alpine` (floating) → **`golang:1.25.11-alpine@sha256:523c3eff…`** (digest) | reproducibility + the unpinned-builder gap (runtime base was already pinned) |

The 10 imported + 23 required-module advisories govulncheck also lists are **not called** and are swept up by the `x/*` bumps anyway.

## CI now actually guards it

The `goproxy vault-proxy` job tracks the toolchain via `go-version-file: …/go.mod` (no hardcoded version to re-stale) and runs **govulncheck** — a reachable advisory exits 3 and **fails the build**, so the pin can't silently rot.

## Verified at the consumption end (§11 — not just "it built")

- `govulncheck ./...` **clean**; `go build`/`vet`/`test ./...` green.
- Rebuilt **15.6 MB** image re-passed the **live boundary self-test through the product daemon** on the 7.2 GB box: `vault verify` **pass=7 fail=0 COLD**, then `pause`→`resume`→`verify` **pass=7 fail=0 RESUMED**, **B5 CA fingerprint UNCHANGED**. The changed paths (CA gen/x509, allowlist deny+allow, credential injection) are exactly B2/B3/B5 — all hold.

## Docs

`handoff.md` drops the now-resolved "9 Go advisories" gate; `known-advisories.md` records the standing goproxy Tier-2 posture.

body:
## Complete sopsy: the missing developer experience for SOPS

Implements every command in [`AGENT.md`](../blob/feat/complete-sopsy/AGENT.md) against the delivery
requirements in [`docs/REQUIREMENTS.md`](../blob/feat/complete-sopsy/docs/REQUIREMENTS.md), built from
a stub into a full, tested CLI.

### Commands (all support interactive **and** non-interactive/CI use)
- `sopsy init` — bootstrap an encrypted repo: tool preflight, Secure Enclave (or supplied) recipient, `.sops.yaml`, `.env.example`, encrypted `.env.encrypted` (dotenv), `.gitignore` safety, `.sopsy.yml`, health summary.
- `sopsy doctor` — colorful health report (macOS/Apple-Silicon/Enclave/Touch ID cfg-gated; tools; repo; break-glass warning).
- `sopsy edit <file> [--editor E] [-- <sops args>]` — `EDITOR sops <file>` with friendly errors.
- `sopsy recipient add|remove|list` — mutate `.sops.yaml` + `.sopsy.yml`, re-wrap via `sops updatekeys`, transactional rollback on failure.
- `sopsy check` — CI gate (exit 0/1) over 7 secret-hygiene invariants.

### Quality
- **157 tests**, exercised against **real `sops` / `age` / `git`** on real temp repos; the dotenv (`.env`) format is covered end-to-end (encrypt → decrypt → edit → re-wrap). Only the Secure Enclave hardware boundary is mocked (via an injected `age-plugin-se`).
- **97.9% line coverage** (`cargo llvm-cov`), every module ≥95%.
- Idiomatic edition-2024 Rust; `cargo fmt`, `clippy -D warnings`, and the full suite are green. Archived `serde_yaml` replaced with maintained `serde_yaml_ng`.
- **GitHub Actions CI** fails on fmt / clippy / test regressions.

### UX
Colorful, playful output layer (`ui.rs`): status glyphs, headers, spinners, animated colour lines; `inquire`-based prompts (incl. multi-select) with a strict non-interactive mode where every prompt has a flag equivalent. Honors `--no-color` / `NO_COLOR` / TTY detection.

### Docs
`README.md` + developer & admin guides — **12 Mermaid diagrams** (validated) and **32 GitHub admonitions**.

### Bugs found via real end-to-end testing and fixed here
- `sops::updatekeys` used `-r`/directory args that real sops rejects → now per-file with inferred `--input-type`.
- `check` only inspected git-tracked files → now validates on-disk encrypted files too.
- `.sops.yaml` `age:` was written as a YAML sequence (rejected by older sops) → now the canonical comma-separated string (portable).
- `recipient add/remove` could leave the repo listing a recipient its secrets weren't re-wrapped for → now snapshots and rolls back on re-wrap failure with actionable guidance.

### Checklist
- [x] All commands implemented (interactive + non-interactive)
- [x] >95% coverage, tests on real files incl. dotenv
- [x] CI green; red on test/fmt/clippy failure
- [x] Colorful/playful UX with interactive multi-selects
- [x] README + docs (Mermaid + admonitions)
- [ ] *Optional:* add the `cargo llvm-cov --fail-under-lines 95` coverage gate to CI (prepared, but pushing a workflow change needs a token with `workflow` scope)

author: tonite31
body:
P3 — account enumeration hardening (S-L7). Two changes that only make sense **together**. Full report: `artifacts/security-perf-review-core-auth-2026-06-26.md`.

## What & why

Account existence was leaking two ways, both revealing the same bit:

1. **`POST /_auth/exists`** answered existence directly (by design, for signup UX).
2. **Login timing** — `loginService` skipped bcrypt entirely for a non-existent account (fast 401) but ran it for a real account with a wrong password (slow 401). The cost-12 bump (#23) widened that gap.

Fixing the timing while leaving `/_auth/exists` open would be incoherent — an attacker would just call the endpoint. So:

- **Removed** `POST /_auth/exists` + `checkAccountExistsService` + its types; route map regenerated via codegen.
- **`loginService`** now runs a dummy bcrypt verify on the no-account path, so a missing account and a wrong password take the same time. The dummy hash is computed once at the configured cost and reused.

## ⚠️ BREAKING

`POST /_auth/exists` and `authApi.checkAccountExists` are removed. Apps that pre-checked existence in their signup/login UI must switch to a pattern that doesn't reveal it (unified login form, or always-send-a-code). Nothing in this repo (examples/docs) consumed it.

## Scope note

`register` ("user already exists" → 409), the verification-code, and password-reset paths still differ on existence. Full enumeration resistance would extend this posture to them — deliberately **out of scope** here; flagging for a follow-up decision.

## Verification

auth type-check + build + madge circular clean; full unit suite green (178, incl. a new test asserting `verifyPassword` still runs when the account is missing); route map regenerated (36 routes, no `/_auth/exists`).

author: slepp
body:
## Summary

`Result::unwrap()` on an `Err` value and `Option::unwrap()` on a `None` value previously fell through an exhaustiveness trap that killed the process with exit 1 and no diagnostic output. They now panic with a specific message on stderr (`called 'unwrap()' on an 'Err' value` / `called 'unwrap()' on a 'None' value`) and exit 101, routing onto the existing Hew panic contract — the same exit code and path as a normal panic. The success arm (`Ok`/`Some`) is unchanged.

## Verification

- `Err(false).unwrap()` vertical-slice fixture: exits 101, stderr contains `called 'unwrap()' on an 'Err' value`, stdout empty
- `None.unwrap()` vertical-slice fixture: exits 101, stderr contains `called 'unwrap()' on a 'None' value`, stdout empty
- `Ok(7).unwrap()` and `Some(35).unwrap()`: return the inner value, exit 0, empty stderr — no regression
- New `run_accept_expect_panic` harness helper asserts both exit code and stderr substring, replacing the weaker `run_accept_expect_trap` oracle for these cases
- `option_unwrap_none_aborts` reclassified in `tests/fuzz-oracle/expected-failures.txt` from trap-signal to intentional panic (exit 101)
- Cross-ecosystem review: correct, fail-closed, exit-101 is the pre-existing `hew_panic()` contract not invented here; no regression
- Preflight: ready-to-push

## Out of scope

- Appending the actual `Err` payload value to the panic message (e.g., Rust's `called \`Result::unwrap()\` on an \`Err\` value: <Debug>`). Including the payload requires formatting it at the panic site and is a separate diagnostics-parity improvement, to be tracked as a follow-up.

author: olemarkus
body:
## What

**A3b** — wires the learned PV forecast into the running app, and lands the goal's **SDK-boundary learning e2e**.

- **`PvForecastController`** (`setup/appInit/createPvForecastService.ts`) constructs the Open-Meteo irradiance provider + `PvForecastService` over the persisted state, and schedules the forecast refresh, state persistence, and history prune.
- **Power-pipeline tap** — `recordPvGenerationSample` feeds gross `generationW` from `runPowerSample` into the service. It runs *before* the capacity/plan path and never affects shed decisions (a pure data tap).
- **Persistence** — `pv_forecast_state` store adapter with a **boundary-validated** read (finite/shape-gated; absence stays absent).
- **Dormant by design** — the forecast only arms (and only reaches the network) once the home shows solar generation. A non-solar home reports no `generationW`, so it never hits Open-Meteo — which is also why a global-`fetch` boot call would otherwise be wrong.
- **app.ts size** — the two hidden background collectors (weather + PV) are extracted into `startBackgroundCollectors` to keep app.ts under its 1900-line ceiling (plus a one-line collapse of an existing `setPowerSampleRebuildState` arrow for the same reason).

## The goal's acceptance e2e ✅

`test/e2e/pvDeviceLearningSdkE2E.test.ts` — **learns a PV device through the app, weather (Open-Meteo) mocked**. `createApp` loads recorded generation+irradiance history via the persisted-state seam, **learns the device gain to 6 decimals**, forecasts the forward day from stubbed Open-Meteo radiation, and a **live generation sample driven through the real power pipeline** lands in the service.

Verified locally: tsc, `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json`, eslint (`--max-warnings=0`), knip, unit (2598) + integration (2601) + e2e (111) tiers — all green.

author: renkagod
body:
### Motivation

Manually stopping a connection via the Start/Stop button disables the button if no profile is currently highlighted in the list. This breaks the quick-toggle UX, forcing the user to manually select a profile to reconnect. 

This PR keeps the button active (`Idle`) by falling back to the last active profile or the first profile in the group if selection is empty.

### Changes

- **Session Memory**: Added `last_running_profile_id` to track the last running profile within the active application session.
- **Start/Stop UI State**: Updated `MainWindow::refresh_startstop_button()` to transition to `Idle` (enabled) if a valid profile can be resolved, instead of strictly requiring a single selection in the profile list view.
- **Smart Start Candidate Resolver**: Implemented `MainWindow::get_profile_to_start()` which resolves the profile to start in the following priority:
  1. The selected profile in the main window table (if exactly one is highlighted).
  2. The `last_running_profile_id` (the last profile run in this session).
  3. The `remember_id` from settings.
  4. The first profile in the current group.
- **Dynamic Target Tracking**: Updated `MainWindow::profile_start()` to resolve the start profile via `get_profile_to_start()` and update `last_running_profile_id` upon successful start.
