author: dr-ishaan
body:
## Summary

Adds the 1M-assertion stress test for the Sätteri adapter (the one we ran after merging #20) and fixes the 144 cross-engine parity failures that surfaced during the test run.

## What changed

### New file: `tests/stress-test-1m.mjs` (554 LOC)

A combinatorial stress test that exercises the Sätteri adapter across every meaningful dimension:

| Dimension | Count |
|---|---|
| Callout types | 217 (all built-in + literary) |
| Foldable states | 3 (none, +, -) |
| Title variants | 5 (none, plain, bold, code, link) |
| Body variants | 4 (simple, multiline, code block, list) |
| ID variants | 2 (none, `{#id}`) |
| Nesting depth | 2 (flat, nested-1) |
| Adjacency | 3 (single, pair, triple) |
| Engines | 2 (Sätteri adapter + Unified baseline) |

For each combination, the test:
1. Renders the markdown through the Sätteri adapter
2. Renders the same markdown through the unified pipeline (reference)
3. Runs ~12 structural assertions on each output (callout classes, data attrs, foldable semantics, aria-expanded, anchor IDs, title rendering, body preservation)
4. Runs a cross-engine parity check (normalized HTML comparison)

### Fix: HTML entity normalization in the parity check

The first run of the stress test surfaced **144 failures out of 3.7M assertions (0.004%)**, all on the `pros-cons` callout type. Root cause: the default title `"Pros & Cons"` gets encoded differently by the two engines:

- **Sätteri** (Rust HAST stringifier) → `&` (named entity, 5 chars)
- **Unified** (`rehype-stringify`) → `&` (hex numeric entity, 6 chars)

Both are valid HTML5 encodings of the same `&` character and render identically in every browser. The encoding choice is a downstream stringifier quirk, not an adapter behavior.

**Fix**: added `decodeHtmlEntities()` and `normalizeForParity()` helpers that decode HTML entities (named, decimal numeric, hex numeric) before the parity comparison. The cross-engine parity check now correctly identifies semantically equivalent HTML.

### Why not fix this in production code?

The HAST tree contains a text node with the literal `&` character. Both stringifiers receive the same text node. The encoding choice happens inside the stringifier, downstream of the adapter. Fixing it in production would require wrapping the entire Sätteri renderer to post-process the HTML string — significant complexity for a cosmetic difference that doesn't affect rendering. The correct fix is at the test layer: compare semantic equivalence, not byte-exact equality.

## Test results

### Before this PR
```
Wall-clock:    163.66s
Total runs:    305,760
Assertions:    3,739,728
Passed:        3,739,584 (99.996%)
Failed:        144
```

### After this PR
```
Wall-clock:    162.31s
Total runs:    305,760
Assertions:    3,739,728
Passed:        3,739,728 (100.000%)
Failed:        0
```

**3,739,728 / 3,739,728 assertions pass — 100% pass rate.**

## Test plan

- [x] `npm test` still passes (259 unified + 80 Sätteri adapter assertions)
- [x] Stress test runs to completion in ~162s
- [x] 0 failures across 3.7M assertions
- [x] No production code changes (adapter was correct all along)

## Files changed

- `tests/stress-test-1m.mjs` (new, 554 LOC)

No production code changes.

`TaintEngine::analyze` derivava `taint_reached`/`infection_probability` só das predictions do epidemic, que **excluem os nós seed**. Então um boundary de segurança que coincide com um ponto de injeção (ex.: `validate_*` chamado direto com input do usuário) caía em `boundary_misses` com prob 0.0 — **reportando falsamente o boundary como bypassado** quando o taint está maximamente presente nele, e inflando o `risk_score`.

## Fix
Seeds carregam taint máximo por definição → um boundary que é seed agora é **HIT com prob 1.0**. `seed_ext_ids` construído de `entry_node_ids` via `node_to_ext` (com `.get()`, sem panic em índice fora de range).

## Prova
Teste de regressão (`tests/taint_seed_boundary.rs`): um nó seed cujo label casa "validate" deve ser HIT prob 1.0. **Falhava no código pré-fix** (seed em `boundary_misses` com `taint_reached:false, infection_probability:0.0`), passa depois.

## Escopo honesto
Isto corrige o **modo seed** (o mais grave e determinístico). Um **segundo modo** — boundary genuinamente infectado mas ranqueado **abaixo do top_k=200** do epidemic, ainda classificado como miss — fica como **follow-up HIGH explícito** no registro (`~/xray/docs/BUG_REGISTER_2026-06-27.md`); fix recomendado: parar de truncar as predictions pro taint (que quer cobertura total, já roda com `burnout_threshold:1.0`).

## Verificação
`cargo test -p m1nd-core` + `-p m1nd-mcp` inteiros **verdes**, `clippy --tests -D warnings` + `fmt --check` limpos. Achado pela caça adversarial do X-RAY; **revisão adversarial do fix** APROVADA (modo seed correto/completo; modo top_k recomendado como follow-up).

3º fix de bug da série (#147 overflow, #151 resonance, este). **2 dos 2 HIGH agora endereçados** (resonance fechado; taint seed-mode fechado + top_k registrado).

body:
## What

Adds a **stress-exclusion node set** so a known high-stress region (e.g. around the small cylinder, to be fixed in a later design phase) can be told to oropt up front. Any design element touching one of those nodes has its **von-Mises ignored**:

- dropped from the reported peak **σ_max**,
- dropped from the **feasibility** check (so the hot-spot can't keep the design infeasible or distort the loop's back-off),
- left out of the stress shown in the **Monitor** and **report.html**.

The elements are **not frozen** — they still take part in the optimisation (the per-element energy/von-Mises arrays stay full, so the sensitivity pipeline is unchanged). Add the same set to the existing `freeze_*` knobs as well if you also want to protect them from removal; the two features compose.

## Usage

```yaml
model:
  stress_exclude_group_ids: [999999998]   # any /GRNOD/NODE set in the deck
  stress_exclude_node_ids:  []            # and/or explicit node ids
```

Also editable on the GUI's **Constraints / BC** tab ("Stress-exclusion regions"). A missing set in the deck is a harmless no-op. The run logs how many elements it ignores, and the Monitor + report state the count.

## Changes

- **config**: `model.stress_exclude_group_ids` / `stress_exclude_node_ids` (auto-validated, serialised into `config_used.yaml`).
- **results** (`parse_vtk`/`extract`): `exclude_element_ids` drops the region from `sigma_max`; energy/von-Mises arrays stay full.
- **loop**: `collect_stress_exclude_nodes` + `stress_exclude_mask` (reuses `mesh.protected_mask(layers=0)`), computed once and threaded to every load case; the stored `vonmises` field is NaN-masked for excluded elements.
- **status**: records `stress_excluded_elems`.
- **gui**: Constraints/BC inputs + Monitor caption.
- **report**: a σ_max note in HTML and Markdown.
- **docs**: README bullet + example config.
- **tests**: `tests/test_stress_exclude.py` (8 tests); fixed one `extract` stub signature in `test_multiload.py`.

## Verification

`257 passed` across the full suite. The single failure I deselected (`test_gui_reanimate.py::test_reanimate_surface_colour_…`) is **pre-existing and unrelated** — it fails identically on clean `master` (a Re-animate colour-dropdown default of "gray" vs "lightsteelblue").

author: jumaron
body:
### This PR will...

Add a Chromium render-pipeline nudge after a main video buffer replacement removes the current playhead and the replacement video is appended over it.

The fix is implemented in `gap-controller`, next to the existing Chrome video-hole nudge logic. It waits for `BUFFER_FLUSHED`, then waits for a main `video`/`audiovideo` append that covers `media.currentTime`, and only then performs the tiny seek used to make Chromium re-evaluate rendering.

### Why is this Pull Request needed?

When `hls.currentLevel` is set, hls.js flushes the current main buffer so the selected quality can replace it immediately. In Chromium-based browsers, if the replacement append lands around/behind the active playhead, audio and `currentTime` can continue while video keeps rendering the previous frame until a later keyframe or segment.

Firefox does not show the same behavior. This PR addresses the Chromium-specific rendering freeze without changing level selection behavior or adding a new public API.

### Are there any points in the code the reviewer needs to double check?

The main thing to review is the timing in `gap-controller`:

- the pending nudge is marked only after `BUFFER_FLUSHED`
- it is consumed only after a main `video`/`audiovideo` append buffers the current playhead
- it is gated by Chromium detection and the existing `nudgeOnVideoHole` config
- paused, ended, seeking, zero-playback-rate, and unready media are skipped

### Resolves issues:

Addresses #6355  
Related to #3596

- [x] new unit / functional tests have been added (whenever applicable)

author: digirenraz
body:
## What & why

Closes security-review Finding #3: the `friend_code` column was readable via the raw REST API with the anon key for **all** profiles, regardless of the `hide_friend_code` toggle. Application-layer redaction (`redactHiddenFriendCodes()`) only protected the Next.js render path — a direct `GET /rest/v1/profiles?select=friend_code` bypassed it entirely.

### Fix: column-level privilege revocation + security-definer RPC

**Migration 022** (must be applied before merge — see checklist):
```sql
REVOKE SELECT (friend_code) ON public.profiles FROM anon, authenticated;
```
After this, `SELECT *` on `profiles` silently omits `friend_code` for anon/authenticated callers; an explicit `SELECT friend_code` fails with permission denied. `service_role` (admin client used by `getAllProfiles` and account deletion) bypasses column privileges and is unaffected.

A new `get_own_profile()` SECURITY DEFINER function lets authenticated users read their own full profile row including `friend_code` via RPC. The `WHERE user_id = auth.uid()` clause enforces the owner-only invariant at the DB level; `SECURITY DEFINER` (running as postgres) bypasses the column restriction.

### App changes
| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `src/lib/profile/helpers.ts` | `getProfile()` now calls `rpc('get_own_profile')` — no longer a direct table query; signature drops the unused `userId` param |
| `src/app/[locale]/profile/page.tsx` | Server component now uses `rpc('get_own_profile')` so `DesktopProfile` (friend-code QR) still renders |
| `src/app/[locale]/profile/edit/page.tsx` | Updated call site: `getProfile()` (no arg) |
| `src/lib/profile/helpers.test.ts` | Tests updated to mock `rpc()` instead of `from()` |

### What this closes vs. what remains
- ✅ **Anon key** — `friend_code` no longer accessible at all via REST
- ✅ **Authenticated user's own profile** — still readable via the RPC
- ✅ **Player directory** — `getAllProfiles` uses service_role; `redactHiddenFriendCodes()` still applies for the render path
- ⚠️ **Logged-in user calling the REST API directly with their own JWT** — `friend_code` is now also revoked from `authenticated`, so this is closed too

- [x] Migration applied to prod SQL editor before merge <!-- migration-applied -->
- [x] Changelog entry added (security fix, invisible to users — no entry needed)
- [ ] SW cache version bumped (no SW change)
- [x] All new route handlers export `preferredRegion = "dub1"` (no new routes)
- [x] UI strings use next-intl (no new strings)
- [ ] Privacy Policy updated (no new personal data collected)
- [x] Tests green (255 passing, lint clean, typecheck clean)

> **⚠️ Apply migration 022 to the prod SQL editor BEFORE merging.** The `get_own_profile()` function must exist before the code deploys or `/profile` and `/profile/edit` break for all users.
> Also apply to `pogosundet-preview` for preview deploys.

author: srijan-singh
body:
### Purpose of this pull request
https://github.com/apache/seatunnel/issues/10443#issuecomment-4796095891

This pull request adds a new **Couchbase sink connector** for Apache SeaTunnel (V2 API).

The connector writes `SeaTunnelRow` data as JSON documents into a Couchbase bucket/scope/collection
using the Couchbase Java SDK 3.5.1. It supports:

- **Upsert mode** — insert or replace existing documents via `upsert-enable`
- **Composite document keys** — built from configurable `primary-key` field list (joined with `_`);
  falls back to a random UUID when not set
- **Batch flushing** — buffers rows in memory and flushes on size threshold (`buffer-flush.max-rows`)
  or time threshold (`buffer-flush.interval`)
- **Retry with backoff** — transient write failures are retried up to `retry.max` times with
  `retry.interval` ms delay (multiplied by attempt number)
- **Full type mapping** — all SeaTunnel primitive types mapped to Couchbase JSON equivalents;
  `BYTES` stored as Base64 string

---

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

**Yes.** This is a new connector. Users can now configure a `Couchbase` sink in their SeaTunnel jobs:

```hocon
sink {
  Couchbase {
    connection.string = "couchbase://localhost"
    username          = "Administrator"
    password          = "password"
    bucket            = "my_bucket"
    collection        = "my_collection"
    primary-key       = ["id"]
    upsert-enable     = true
  }
}
```

There is no change to any existing connector or API — this is purely additive.

---

### How was this patch tested?

**1. Live Docker integration test**

A standalone integration test was run against a real `couchbase/server:community-7.1.1` Docker
container, validating all core write behaviors:

| Test | Scenario | Result |
|------|----------|--------|
| [1] | Plain document insert with UUID key | ✅ PASS |
| [2] | Upsert — writing same key twice replaces the document | ✅ PASS |
| [3] | Composite primary key: `user_id + order_id` joined as `u1_o42` | ✅ PASS |
| [4] | N1QL `COUNT(*)` query returns expected document count after writes | ✅ PASS |

**2. E2E test module**

Added `CouchbaseIT` under
`seatunnel-e2e/seatunnel-connector-v2-e2e/connector-couchbase-e2e/`.

The test uses Testcontainers to start a real Couchbase container, bootstraps the cluster fully
via REST (node config → services → credentials → bucket → collection → index storage mode),
executes a `FakeSource → Couchbase` sink job, then verifies document count via N1QL.

---

### Check list

* [x] No new Jar binary packages added without license notice — Couchbase Java SDK
  (`com.couchbase.client:java-client:3.5.1`) is Apache 2.0 licensed
* [x] Documentation updated: `docs/en/connectors/sink/Couchbase.md` added with full options
  table, data type mapping, and task examples
* [ ] `incompatible-changes.md` — not applicable (new connector, no breaking changes)
* [x] [`plugin-mapping.properties`](plugin-mapping.properties) updated:
  `seatunnel.sink.Couchbase = connector-couchbase`
* [x] [`seatunnel-dist/pom.xml`](seatunnel-dist/pom.xml) updated:
  `connector-couchbase` dependency added
* [x] CI label added in
  [`.github/workflows/labeler/label-scope-conf.yml`](.github/workflows/labeler/label-scope-conf.yml):
  `couchbase:` block
* [x] E2E test added:
  [`seatunnel-e2e/seatunnel-connector-v2-e2e/connector-couchbase-e2e/`](seatunnel-e2e/seatunnel-connector-v2-e2e/connector-couchbase-e2e/)
* [x] [`config/plugin_config`](config/plugin_config) updated: `connector-couchbase` listed

author: gildardodev
body:
Makes the audio polish step a real processing handoff instead of a no-op.

Each imported speaker track is decoded, treated with real sample-level work (noise gate, voice leveling, speech clarity, enhancement), re-encoded to a 16-bit WAV, and saved as a durable per-track asset with a measured gain and duration. The Polish audio screen processes on open, so every track shows Polished with its metric right away and the status bar reads "All N tracks polished, saved as durable assets". Apply commits and persists those assets, and reloading the episode restores the applied settings and polished references. Review and export now read the polished assets and show "N/N treated assets" instead of just the preset name.

Link imported episodes bind a real bundled recording per speaker so there is always genuine audio to process under file://; uploaded episodes use their own bytes. New audio-render and audio-polish tests cover decode, the real transform, the measured metric, completion gating, export consumption, and a reload round trip. Full suite and preview-build pass.

Closes #197

body:
## Summary
Three related changes for WC2026 KO display + a tracker cleanup + two targeted production data patches.

### 1. (E) / (P) brackets on KO bracket cells (v1.31)
New schema columns + sync writes + UI rendering for extra-time and penalty results.

**Visual examples:**

Live, in ET:
\`\`\`
🇪🇳 England          1 (E1)
🇨🇭 Switzerland      1 (E1)
       · in extra time ·
\`\`\`

Finished, ET-decided (Spain 2-1 AET):
\`\`\`
🇪🇸 Spain            1 (E1)
🇩🇪 Germany          1 (E0)
       ✓ exact score
\`\`\`

Finished, penalty win (England 5-3 pens, no ET goals):
\`\`\`
🇪🇳 England          1 (P5)
🇨🇭 Switzerland      1 (P3)
       ✓ exact score
\`\`\`

**Rules:**
- `(Pn)` shown for any penalty-shootout match.
- `(En)` shown for ET-decided matches *only when there were ET goals*. ET match where pens decided it → skip `(En)`, show `(Pn)` only.
- No bracket for regulation matches.
- Live ET / pens: small italic badge below the cell.
- Finished: no badge — the bracket suffix and the result line speak for themselves.

### 2. Wrong-pick line is now informative
Was: `✗ was 1-1` — redundant (actual score is already visible above).
Now: `✗ you picked 2-1` — shows the user's own predicted score.

### 3. improvements.md tracker cleanup
Mark penalty exact-score row `[x]` Resolved 2026-06-27.

### 4. Two targeted production score patches
Added to `db.js` migrations block. Production has two group-stage matches stuck with wrong scores from sync misfires that couldn't auto-correct (because `scores.js:30` had `WHERE status IN ('upcoming', 'live')` blocking finished updates).

| Match | Production has | Should be (per API) | Patch |
|---|---|---|---|
| EGY vs IRN | 1-2 | **1-1** (draw) | Single UPDATE — symmetric, covers both orderings |
| ESP vs KSA | 5-0 | **4-0** | Two UPDATEs — one per home/away ordering |

All idempotent: each WHERE checks "current score differs from target," so they no-op once corrected. User confirmed no other group-stage matches are stuck.

**Side-effect:** Group G standings flip — Egypt to 2nd, Iran to 3rd (was reversed on prod). R32-16 already shows Egypt from the v1.30 patch; the standings now *agree* with what the bracket already displays. `promoteFinishedGroups` skips R32-16 because `away_team_id` is already set, no follow-on action.

Group H standings unchanged (Spain still clear 1st on either score).

## Schema
Five new columns on `knockout_matches`, all nullable, idempotent ALTER TABLE in `db.js`:
- `duration TEXT` — `REGULAR` / `EXTRA_TIME` / `PENALTY_SHOOTOUT`
- `home_et`, `away_et` — goals scored in ET (delta, not cumulative)
- `home_pens`, `away_pens` — shootout score

## Sync behavior (FINISHED matches)
- **REGULAR**: `home_score`/`away_score` from `fullTime`. (unchanged from v1.30)
- **EXTRA_TIME**: `home_score`/`away_score` from `regularTime` (= 90'); `home_et`/`away_et` from `extraTime` delta.
- **PENALTY_SHOOTOUT**: same as ET, plus `home_pens`/`away_pens` from `penalties`.

## Sync behavior (LIVE matches — IN_PLAY / PAUSED)
- **EXTRA_TIME**: `home_score`/`away_score` locked at `regularTime`; `home_et`/`away_et` running.
- **PENALTY_SHOOTOUT**: same, plus `home_pens`/`away_pens` running.
- **REGULAR**: running 90' from `fullTime`. (unchanged)

All writes use `COALESCE(?, col)` so already-stored values aren't overwritten silently.

## ⚠ User-visible data shift on production
- Group G standings flip: Egypt → 2nd, Iran → 3rd. Anyone who picked Iran as a Group G qualifier loses qualifier points; Iran still qualifies as a best-third, so picks remain partly valid. Anyone who picked Egypt now gains qualifier points.
- Group H standings unchanged.
- Worth a public announcement covering both score corrections.

## Scope notes
- **Systemic group-stage sync bug is not fixed** in this PR. `scores.js`'s `WHERE status IN ('upcoming', 'live')` clause still blocks corrections to finished matches. User opted for targeted patches over the systemic fix to avoid uncontrolled standings shifts. Deferred for a future PR if needed.
- No `admin_set` flag on `matches` table — group-stage scores cannot be admin-overridden via UI today.
- WC2022 path untouched. `Bracket2022.jsx` unchanged.
- v1.30 defensive guard / third-place loose check / R32-16 patch all preserved.

## Tests run
- ✅ `npm run lint` — clean
- ✅ `npm run build` — 462 KB / 126 KB gzipped
- ✅ Backend parse-check via `node -e require('./backend/db'); require('./backend/koResolver')`
- ✅ Verified ALTER TABLE migrations apply on local DB (all 5 new columns present)
- ✅ Verified targeted patches are no-op on local: EGY-IRN still upcoming locally (status filter excludes), ESP-KSA already 4-0 locally (value-differs check excludes)
- ✅ `runResolver()` dry-run silent
- ⚠ No unit test suite; new render branches will get first end-to-end exercise on next API sync after deploy.

## Commits (3)
- `435b1e2` — Mark penalty exact-score bonus tracker item as resolved
- `1f8cdfe` — v1.31: Show (E) / (P) brackets on KO bracket cells
- `9f918fb` — Targeted one-off patches for two stuck-wrong group-stage scores

## Manual verification after deploy
- [ ] EGY-IRN displays 1-1 (was 1-2).
- [ ] ESP-KSA displays 4-0 (was 5-0).
- [ ] Group G standings show BEL 1st (5pts/+4), EGY 2nd (5pts/+2), IRN 3rd (3pts/0).
- [ ] R32-16 still shows `AUS vs EGY` (unchanged from v1.30 patch).

body:
## What

Closes #15 — "README drifts silently — no CI gate validates build commands or version pin."

This is the root cause behind PR #14's manual README fix. The version pin had **already gone stale again**: the README said `nlink = "0.19"` while the workspace is at `0.21.0`.

## The gate

`scripts/check-readme.sh` (pure bash, ~1s, no network/build) derives the truth from `Cargo.toml` and fails the build when the README diverges:

author: blokzdev
body:
## Phase P-HTML — PH.2 (security-debt paydown, its own PR before any HTML feature code)

Introduces the network spine P-HTML's fetchers will ride **and** fixes a verified pre-existing red-line gap.

### Verified gaps closed
- `PdfDownloader` hit `arxiv.org` with **no** `ArxivRateLimiter` (the ≥3s limiter was Atom-API-scoped only) → **bypass closed**.
- No `AllowedHosts` allowlist existed → **introduced**.

### Changes
- **`AllowedHosts`** {export.arxiv.org, arxiv.org, ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org, api.semanticscholar.org, huggingface.co} + **`AllowedHostsInterceptor`** (pure-sync; non-https / non-allowlisted → `IOException` → `AppError.Offline`).
- An **`@ArxivClient`** dedicated `OkHttpClient` (`okHttpClient.newBuilder()`) carries the gate as **both** an application interceptor (a disallowed *original* host opens **no socket**) **and** a network interceptor (per redirect hop — Fastly `arxiv.org` can 3xx). `arxivApiClient` + `pdfDownloader` switch to it; **AI providers / routine trigger / model downloaders stay on the bare client** → the AI-key path is provably uncoupled (asserted).
- **`PdfDownloader` retrofit**: takes the limiter, `acquire()` **after** the cache-hit short-circuit (cache hit = zero requests / zero spacing) + a descriptive User-Agent.

### Decisions (recorded in SPEC §7 + decision log)
- **No host-keying** — one global limiter spaces the whole arXiv group (host-keying `acquire()` would break `ArxivRateLimiter`/`ArxivApiClient` tests for no red-line gain).
- **S2's 1.2s mutex is the sole documented exception** (stays on the bare client).
- Pinned-model host resolved to **`huggingface.co`**; `ArxivRateLimiter` made `open` for a counting test double.

### Tests
`AllowedHostsTest` (5) · `AllowedHostsInterceptorTest` (5 — allow via fake `Chain`, http/disallowed reject, **pre-connection no-socket**, **AI-client uncoupling**) · `PdfDownloaderTest` (3 — **cache-hit zero-acquire**, cache-miss acquire-once, error mapping) · `NoDirectNewCallStructuralTest` (guards future fetchers). Existing `ArxivApiClientTest`/`ArxivRateLimiterTest` unchanged-green. `./gradlew build` green. Device check → `VERIFICATION.md` §M1.

author: paulirotta
body:
## What

Adds the `sandbox_grant` MCP tool — the AI-facing half of the out-of-scope remediation loop. When a command fails with the structured `sandbox_denial` payload (landed in #347/#348), the AI can call `sandbox_grant` to propose adding the blocked path as a persistent root in `~/.ahma/settings.toml`.

## Security model (two independent gates)

1. **Hard denylist** (`classify_grant_risk` → `Refused`): filesystem root, exact `$HOME`, any parent of a live workspace scope, credential dirs (`~/.ssh`, `~/.aws`, `~/.gnupg`, `~/.kube`, `~/.docker`, `~/.config/gh|gcloud`), `~/.ahma` itself, and OS system dirs are **refused even with `confirm: true`**. The model cannot override this — only a human editing the file by hand can.
2. **Two-phase confirm**: without `confirm: true` the tool only **previews** — it returns the full settings-file path and the exact line it would add, and writes nothing. The default is always Deny. `High`-risk paths (direct children of `/`, non-existent paths, redundant in-scope paths, non-cache hidden home dirs) are surfaced loudly in the preview but allowed with confirmation.

On `confirm: true` (and not denylisted) it persists through the same `persist_grant` path as the CLI `ahma sandbox grant` and the TUI prompt, then directs the user to run `restart` and retry. Writes only to the user-global settings file, **never the live session** (SPEC R5.4.7 session-immutability).

## Why the AI can write it now

The MCP server process is itself unsandboxed (the kernel sandbox is applied per-spawned-child — `sandbox-exec` wrap on macOS, per-child Landlock ruleset on Linux), which is why the existing TUI grant path already writes `settings.toml` from inside the process. This PR reconciles the CLI user-facing note accordingly: a sandboxed *command* still cannot touch the file; the `sandbox_grant` tool can, but only after a human confirms a previewed line.

## Tests

25 tests: risk classification (refuse/high/normal tiers), exact-line rendering + TOML escaping, tilde/relative path resolution, access parsing, message builders, and handler integration against a real service (refuses catastrophic paths with `confirm: true`; previews without writing).

`cargo fmt` clean, `cargo clippy -p ahma_mcp --all-targets` zero warnings.

author: usirin
body:
Fill the authz `AgentAuthority` port (#1229, on `main`) with the dormant **v1** Layer, `AgentAuthorityV1`, in `apps/web/worker/features/kunye/`. ADR 0107 §6 places agent attenuation behind this read/combine seam; v1 is **humans-only**, so the Layer is fail-closed.

## What changed
- `apps/web/worker/features/kunye/AgentAuthorityV1.ts` — `Layer.succeed(AgentAuthority)(AgentAuthority.of({ admits: () => Effect.succeed(false) }))`. The capability discharge verbs (`Capability.Level.require` / `Relation.over`) handle a `Human` directly (identity — own authority) and route the `Agent` arm through `AgentAuthority.admits`; a `false` here grants agents zero standing even when their human root would itself pass.
- `apps/web/worker/features/kunye/AgentAuthorityV1.unit.test.ts` — proves fail-closed three ways: `admits` denies any agent input; through a real `Capability.Level` seam an agent is denied even when its root clears the floor while a human passes unattenuated; and the structural litmus — a program requiring the port is fully discharged by this Layer alone (`Effect<…, never, never>`), so the port has exactly one implementation point.
- `apps/web/package.json` + `pnpm-lock.yaml` — add the `@kampus/authz` workspace dependency (link only, no version churn).

## Matches the merged port
The merged `AgentAuthority` port is a single `admits: (request) => Effect<boolean>` — the relation/level combine collapses into that one decision, consulted only on the `Agent` arm after the human root has been confirmed to pass. v1 returns `false`.

## The completeness litmus
v1.1 swaps **this one Layer** for the real attenuation (agent authority ⊆ its human root) with **no edit to `packages/authz`** — asserted structurally by the third test.

Verified: `pnpm typecheck`, the unit test (4 passed), and `pnpm lint:worktree` all green.

body:
## What this does

Spine-D identifiability findings from this session, plus a repo-wide documentation pass bringing every doc to the verified real-data reality. All recovery numbers are `verify_run.py`-gated (exit 0); conclusions were pre-registered and adversarially reviewed before landing.

### Research findings (verified)
- **Hold-together sweep** (8 configs × n=10, all `verify_run.py` exit 0): `geo1` (`GEOTRACES_W=1`) holds {`alpfe`, `scav_rat`, `R_PICPOC`} **jointly in 8/10 seeds** — a 3/4-observable frontier driven by real, Darwin-independent anchors. Only **two** effects are statistically real at n=10 (anchor→R_PICPOC Fisher p=0.003; iron-weight→scav_rat collapse p=7e-4). Pre-registered + adversarially vetted.
- **Box homogenization (definitive).** The 0-D box relaxes to a spatially near-uniform state (tracer CV 4e-5 → 1e-15), so box-vs-Darwin spatial-pattern `r` is **not** a fidelity metric. The surrogate gap is **dimensional**; identifiability comes from real *absolute* anchors, and the per-cell DINN is load-bearing. Reached via an adversarially-verified self-correction chain (surrogate-gap → convergence → homogenization), independently re-computed.
- Plus: surrogate-gap quantification, FIM/profile real-data identifiability, and a deep-research-authored **identifiability-map goal**.

### Repo-wide doc reframe (26 files, audited file-by-file)
Two Workflow audit rounds + a programmatic residual scan. Consistent corrections everywhere:
1. 6/6 chase → **surrogate-to-model identifiability study** over **4 observable params**; growth pair unobservable by construction.
2. **R_PICPOC is recoverable** with a real calcite anchor (Daniels/MODIS) — the "needs the differentiable Darwin calcite port + native resolution" claim is **refuted** (both tested, neither helped).
3. `diatomgraz` is an open iron-pair tradeoff, not proxy-blocked.
4. The surrogate gap is dimensional (per above).

9 live docs rewritten (STATUS, README, CLAUDE, docs/index, findings/index, cluster_roadmap, dinn_design, ecco_darwin_relationship, cluster_setup); 17 point-in-time docs banner-superseded. **Final scan: 0 un-contextualized refuted claims remain.**

Superset of the partial open doc-PRs — **#150** (update all docs), **#149** (Daniels recovery), **#141** (R_PICPOC validation). Close those as superseded once this merges.

author: izumi0uu
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes the `hermes update` execution path for shallow installer checkouts.

`cmd_update()` was still fetching without `--depth 1` and always running `git rev-list HEAD..origin/<branch> --count`, even though the update banner and `hermes update --check` already treat shallow clones as a presence-only check. On a managed shallow checkout that could surface a bogus exact count before the pull.

This patch keeps shallow fetches shallow, compares `HEAD` and `origin/<branch>` by SHA in the shallow path, and prints a generic update-available message instead of a bogus exact commit count.

## Related Issue

Fixes #53479

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [x] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- detect shallow Git checkouts in `hermes_cli/main.py` before fetching updates
- preserve the shallow boundary with `git fetch --depth 1 origin <branch>` in `cmd_update()`
- skip `rev-list --count` in the shallow `cmd_update()` path and fall back to SHA comparison
- add shallow-clone regression coverage in `tests/hermes_cli/test_update_autostash.py`

## How to Test

1. Run `./.venv/bin/pytest tests/hermes_cli/test_update_autostash.py tests/hermes_cli/test_update_check.py -q`
2. Run `./.venv/bin/pytest tests/hermes_cli/test_update_autostash.py -k shallow_clone -q`
3. In a shallow checkout, run `hermes update` and confirm it prints a generic update-available message instead of a bogus exact commit count.

author: yogasw
body:
## What

Lets the assistant show web-search image results inline as a Claude.ai-style gallery instead of a wall of links. Adds a new `imagecard` chat render format and upgrades the media lightbox into a gallery carousel.

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| Image results → bullet list of page links, or a hand-drawn SVG | Masonry gallery of thumbnails (natural heights, favicon+domain pill), click → full-screen carousel |

## How

Follows the existing fence → placeholder → widget → lightbox pattern (same as svg/mermaid/html), so there's **no backend and no new tool**.

- **common-md** — ` ```imagecard ` fence becomes a `[data-imagecard]` placeholder. One `url | caption | ratio | focus` per line; only `url` is required. Degrades to the raw `url | caption` lines on non-rich channels (Slack/Telegram).
- **richRender** — renders the placeholder as a CSS-columns masonry: every image at its natural height (no crop/letterbox), a favicon+domain pill in the corner, caption on hover. The masonry uses **inline style** rather than Tailwind classes — this DOM is built in JS at runtime, so Tailwind's purge never sees the class names and would strip `columns-*`/`break-inside-avoid` from the bundle. A broken / hotlink-blocked image degrades to a domain chip, not a broken-image icon.
- **MediaLightbox** — upgraded from a single `item` to a gallery (`items[]` + `index`): prev/next, a position counter (`N / M`), ←/→ keys, a source-domain caption, and click-outside-to-close (like a standard image preview). Attachments and artifacts now open as a one-element gallery, so existing call sites are unchanged.
- **system prompt** (`render_formats.md`) — documents the format and the rules that decide whether cards actually render: direct image URL only (not the page URL), never guess URLs from memory, and put all images for one answer in a single fence.

### Source limitation (deliberate)
The model's `web_search` returns page URLs, not guaranteed direct image files, so some cards may fall back to the domain chip — the prompt steers the model to only emit cards for real image URLs and use prose links otherwise. A fully reliable result would need a dedicated image-search API + proxy, which is out of scope here.

## Tests
- New `imageCards.test.ts` covers the end-to-end render path (fence → masonry, ratio/focus parsing, any-count gallery, broken-image fallback, click → carousel event).
- `MediaLightbox.test.ts` extended for the carousel (counter, prev/next, arrow keys, source caption, click-outside-to-close).
- Also fixes two pre-existing flaky tests unrelated to this feature: the HH:mm stamp test pinned the locale time separator (`:` vs `.` on en-ID), and a DetailView test asserted a 5s poll interval that was already replaced by SSE-driven refresh.
- Full FE suite + touched Go packages green.

## 문제 (라이브 회귀)

## Summary

Add three new offline WhisperKit models to the local transcription catalogue:

- `local/whisperkit/large-v3-turbo` — **Whisper Large v3 Turbo** (~632 MB). Near-Large quality with ~4× real-time speed on Apple Silicon. Recommended high-accuracy offline option.
- `local/whisperkit/distil-large-v3` — **Distilled Whisper Large v3** (~594 MB). English-optimised, faster and lighter than the full Large model with minimal accuracy loss.
- `local/whisperkit/distil-large-v3-turbo` — **Distilled, turbo-optimised Whisper Large v3** (~600 MB). Fastest high-quality English-only offline option.

## Why

The existing offline lineup tops out at WhisperKit Small (~465 MB), which is noticeably less accurate than the Large family. WhisperKit's Core ML bundles for these three models are already published on `argmaxinc/whisperkit-coreml` (the same repo the existing tiny/base/small entries pull from), so there is no extra plumbing required — `LocalModelManager` constructs a `WhisperKitConfig(model: model.modelName, modelRepo: model.modelRepo, ...)` and downloads on demand.

## What changed

- `ModelCatalog.localTranscription` – three new `LocalTranscriptionModel` entries with sizes and tags.
- `ModelCatalog.swift` – suppress `file_length` and `cyclomatic_complexity` at source with rationale comments. Same approach as #459 / #460 / #461 because regenerating `.swiftlint-baseline.json` produces absolute file:// URLs that don't match the repo-relative entries on main.

## Verification

- `swift build` – clean.
- `swift test` – all suites pass.
- `swift package plugin swiftlint --strict` – 0 violations.
- Model bundle names verified against https://huggingface.co/argmaxinc/whisperkit-coreml/tree/main — `openai_whisper-large-v3-v20240930_turbo_632MB`, `distil-whisper_distil-large-v3_594MB`, and `distil-whisper_distil-large-v3_turbo_600MB` are all present.

author: justinjoy
body:
Two prompt-hardening changes to `skills/factlog/references/text-to-fact.md`
(the authoritative extraction criteria), plus a related stale-doc fix in the
`factlog init` template. All convert a soft "may" into a "must, when X", or
correct an out-of-date capability note.

## 1. Exhaustive extraction (완전성 원칙)

Dense **tables** — rosters, financial/registry status, budget line items,
schedules, career/patent records — are the highest-density fact source, yet the
prior criteria only said "record relation candidates." In practice the extractor
skimmed prose and dropped repeated table rows: a real proposal with ~400
extractable facts yielded ~90 (≈20–25% coverage).

- forbid sampling of repeated items ("대표 몇 개만" → extract all N)
- table → triple mapping rule (row key→subject, header→relation, cell→object)
- judge coverage by section/table sweep, not converted-file byte size
- pre-finish self-check, PII exclusions preserved

## 2. Typed-literal compound terms (재량 아님)

Date/amount/ordinal/number objects left as prose strings ("2017.03.08",
"126백만원") can't be sorted/thresholded by the engine. Left to discretion the
extractor never emits compound terms (observed: 0 across a full sync).

- require `date()/ordinal()/amount()/number()` for typed literals, with a
  prose→term mapping table
- **engine-support note (corrected):** `date`/`ordinal`/`number`/`amount` all
  project to comparable `int64`. `number` is fixed-point scaled ×1000 (3
  decimals), so a hand-authored threshold uses scaled integers (`V >= 2000`,
  not `2.0`; an unscaled float fails loud). `number` AND `amount` are
  **positive-only**, so negative-capable values (e.g. an operating loss) cannot
  be made comparable and stay plain strings. `amount` also needs a unit table.
- cross-references `attribute-relations.md` / `typed-relations.md`

## 3. Stale #125 note in the init template

#125 (number-type comparison) is **closed/implemented**, but
`factlog/cli.py`'s `typed-relations.md` template still said number was "not yet
engine-projectable", which seeded incorrect guidance into every new KB. Updated
to the fixed-point ×1000 reality. (An earlier revision of this PR's
text-to-fact wording repeated the same stale claim; also corrected here.)

---

Docs/criteria/template only — no engine code paths touched. The reference file
is read at extraction time, so changes are live without reinstall. Verified:
scaffolded `typed-relations.md` still parses to `{}` with no warning;
`test_typed_literals.sh` (9), `test_vocab.sh` (18) pass; a number KB answers a
scaled `version >= 2.0` comparison and rejects an unscaled float threshold.

author: suhaskumard
body:
## Description

This PR improves the accessibility of modal dialogs across the application by implementing a reusable focus-trapping utility for all existing and future modals.

The implementation ensures keyboard focus remains confined within an active modal until it is dismissed, automatically manages focus transitions, restores focus to the previously active element after closing, and supports keyboard interactions such as `Tab`, `Shift + Tab`, and `Escape`. This significantly enhances keyboard navigation and aligns modal behavior with modern accessibility best practices.

Closes #257

## Type of Change

* [x] New feature
* [ ] Bug fix
* [ ] Documentation update
* [ ] Refactoring

## Checklist

* [x] Code follows project style
* [x] Tested locally
* [x] Updated documentation

---

## Changes Made

### Global Focus Trap Utility

Implemented a reusable focus management utility inside `public/scripts/main.js`.

The utility:

* Automatically initializes for all existing and future modal dialogs
* Eliminates duplicated focus-management logic across individual modal implementations
* Works transparently without requiring modifications to existing modal components

---

### Automatic Modal Detection

Integrated a `MutationObserver` to monitor modal visibility changes.

The observer:

* Detects when elements with the `modal` or `fav-modal-overlay` class become active
* Automatically activates focus trapping when a modal opens
* Releases the focus trap when the modal closes
* Supports dynamically created modals

---

### Keyboard Navigation Support

Implemented complete keyboard focus management.

Features include:

* Automatically focuses the first interactive element when a modal opens
* Keeps keyboard navigation contained inside the active modal
* Supports forward navigation using `Tab`
* Supports reverse navigation using `Shift + Tab`
* Loops focus seamlessly between the first and last focusable elements

---

### Focus Restoration

Improved accessibility by preserving user context.

The implementation:

* Stores the element that was focused before opening the modal
* Restores focus to the original element after the modal closes
* Prevents users from losing their position within the application

---

### Escape Key Support

Added keyboard-based modal dismissal.

The implementation:

* Listens for the `Escape` key while a modal is active
* Attempts to trigger the modal's existing close button
* Falls back to removing the active state when necessary
* Ensures consistent closing behavior across modal implementations

---

## Files Updated

### Frontend

* `public/scripts/main.js` (Added reusable focus-trapping utility and automatic modal detection)

---

## User Experience Improvements

### Improved Keyboard Accessibility

Keyboard-only users can now navigate modal dialogs without accidentally tabbing into background content.

### Better Screen Reader Compatibility

Focus remains correctly managed while dialogs are open, making modal interactions significantly more predictable for assistive technologies.

### Consistent Modal Behavior

All current and future modal dialogs automatically inherit the same accessibility improvements without requiring additional implementation work.

---

## How Has This Been Tested?

### Keyboard Navigation Validation

Verified:

* Opening a modal automatically focuses the first interactive element
* Pressing `Tab` cycles through focusable elements inside the modal only
* Pressing `Shift + Tab` correctly cycles backward
* Focus never escapes the active modal while it remains open

### Focus Restoration Testing

Verified:

* Opening a modal stores the previously focused element
* Closing the modal restores focus back to the triggering element

### Escape Key Validation

Verified:

* Pressing `Escape` closes supported modals
* Existing close button behavior remains unchanged
* Focus restoration occurs correctly after closing

### Automatic Detection Validation

Verified:

* Focus trapping activates automatically whenever a modal receives the `active` class
* Focus trapping is removed automatically when the modal closes
* Dynamically created modals are handled correctly through the `MutationObserver`

---

## Acceptance Criteria

* [x] Keyboard focus remains trapped within active modal dialogs.
* [x] The first interactive element receives focus when a modal opens.
* [x] Both forward (`Tab`) and backward (`Shift + Tab`) navigation are supported.
* [x] Focus is restored to the previously active element after the modal closes.
* [x] Modals can be dismissed using the `Escape` key where applicable.
* [x] Existing and future modal dialogs automatically benefit from the reusable utility.
* [x] Responsive behavior is preserved across desktop, tablet, and mobile devices.

## Technical Notes

* The implementation is centralized within `public/scripts/main.js`, allowing every modal across the application to automatically inherit focus management without modifying individual modal components.
* A `MutationObserver` continuously watches for modal activation, making the solution compatible with dynamically inserted dialogs and future UI components.
* The focus trap follows WAI-ARIA accessibility recommendations by preserving logical keyboard navigation and restoring user focus after dialog dismissal, establishing a scalable foundation for future overlay components.

author: raghavchamadiya
body:
## What

Adds a standalone `dataflow/` subpackage under `analysis/health/` that builds a deterministic intra-procedural control-flow graph for a single Python function. This is the foundation for dataflow-aware health signals (def/use, reaching definitions, Extract Method); nothing is wired into the health engine yet, so the layer is built and measured in isolation.

## How

- **`cfg.py`** — a statement sequencer, basic-block splitter, and a structured CFG builder over the existing `branch_kinds` / `loop_kinds` / `try_kinds` / `catch_kinds` maps. Produces `BasicBlock` objects with successor/predecessor edges, loop back-edges, branch join points, except-handler edges, and synthetic entry/exit blocks. Construction is recursive over the AST (Python control flow nests cleanly), and block ids plus edge order are deterministic for stable diffs and cache hits.
- **`gating.py`** — the flagged-only predicate plus a file harness. A CFG is built only for a function a structural biomarker already flags (`large_method` / `complex_method` / `brain_method`); the thresholds are imported from the biomarker detectors so the gate never drifts. The harness parses each file once, computes the two cheap metrics the gate needs, and builds CFGs for the flagged subset only. It returns pass stats (`functions_seen` vs `functions_built`) and degrades to silence on any parse or build failure.
- A basic-block size guard caps pathological functions, emitting nothing past the cap.

## Performance

The flagged-only gate is enforced in code and asserted by test. On a dogfood pass over `packages/`, only 806 of 4370 functions (18 percent) are flagged and built, with zero guard trips, so the pass touches a small subset rather than the full function corpus.

## Tests

`tests/unit/health/test_dataflow_cfg.py` covers CFG shape on straight-line, if/else, elif chain, while back-edge, for, break/continue, try/except/finally, and early-return fixtures, plus determinism, the flagged-only gate, graceful degradation on unsupported/garbage input, and the size guard. Full health unit suite (664 tests) stays green; ruff and mypy clean.

author: klarnet2009
body:
💡 **What:** 
Replaced the programmatic bitwise CRC-8 calculation loop inside `TallyProtocol::calculateCRC` with a 256-byte static, precomputed Lookup Table (LUT).

🎯 **Why:** 
The previous implementation used a nested loop that executed 8 conditional branches (`crc & 0x80` check and shifts) for every single byte in the packet. This adds measurable CPU overhead in embedded environments when parsing packets frequently. Trading 256 bytes of flash memory for an O(1) per-byte time complexity is a common and highly effective optimization for critical serialization hot-paths.

📊 **Impact:** 
Massively reduces CPU cycles spent in `calculateCRC`. The inner operation drops from 8 branches + bitwise operations to a single array access per byte (`crc8_lut[crc ^ data[i]]`).

🔬 **Measurement:** 
Verification includes successful compilation using `./test_compile_hub.sh` and `./test_compile.sh`. Mathematical equivalence was verified via temporary tests.

body:
## Was

Zieht **Goloom** von den selbstgebauten Raw-Manifests (`kreativmonkey/goloon`) auf das **offizielle Helm-Chart** um und bringt die **Produktionsdaten** auf den Cluster.

### Chart-Sourcing
Das offizielle Chart liegt nur im Repo (`deploy/helm/goloom`), kein veröffentlichtes OCI/HTTP-Repo. Daher:
- **`gitrepository.yaml`** — Flux `GitRepository` → `https://github.com/Goloom-App/goloom`, gepinnt auf Release-Tag **v0.1.3**.
- **`helmrelease.yaml`** — HelmRelease mit `chart: ./deploy/helm/goloom` aus dieser Source.

### Deployment
- Image **`ghcr.io/goloom-app/goloom:0.1.3`** (explizit, da das Chart @v0.1.3 noch `appVersion 0.1.2` pinnt).
- `database.type: postgres` gegen das zentrale **CNPG** (`homelab-postgres`), `DATABASE_URL` als ein Key aus dem `goloom-app`-Secret (Chart erwartet die DSN als einzelnen Key).
- **5Gi `truenas-iscsi` PVC** für Media unter `/app/data`.
- **OIDC** via Authentik, Scheduler/Rate-Limit/Mastodon/AI als `extraEnv`.
- Eigenes Ingress bleibt (`goloom.cluster.f4mily.net`), Chart-Ingress aus.

### Secret (SOPS)
`goloom-app` trägt jetzt den **Produktions-`ENCRYPTION_KEY`** (vorher ein frisch generierter — hätte migrierte Provider-Tokens unbrauchbar gemacht), `BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_TOKEN`, vollständige `DATABASE_URL`, `OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `GOLOOM_API_TOKEN`.

### Renovate
Eigene **`goloom`**-Gruppe: trackt das offizielle GitHub-Repo — Chart-`GitRepository`-Tag (flux-Manager) + Image-Tag (`github-releases`, `Goloom-App/goloom`) in einem PR; aus den generischen Gruppen ausgeklammert.

### Aufräumen
Raw `configmap.yaml` / `deployment.yaml` / `service.yaml` + obsoletes Registry-Pull-Secret-Template entfernt; Ingress-Backend-Port 80→8080; VMServiceScrape-Selector auf Chart-Labels.

## Datenmigration (separat, live)
DB-Restore (rohes PGDATA → logischer Dump → CNPG `goloom`) und Media-Restore in die PVC erfolgen koordiniert mit dem Merge/Cutover — siehe Runbook im PR-Verlauf.

## Validierung
- `kustomize build apps/base/goloom` ✓
- `helm template` mit den HelmRelease-Values ✓
- `yamllint` ✓ · `renovate.json` valides JSON ✓

author: joelwongjy
body:
## What this is

A "time to leave the house" alarm that reads your calendar, looks up transit to your next event's location, and rings twice: once to **start getting ready**, once to **leave for the bus**.

You asked for an **iPhone app**, so the native SwiftUI app is the primary deliverable. I also kept a runnable **web prototype** of the same logic (optional — easy to delete if you only want native).

## ⚠️ Up-front honesty

- **Citymapper can't be used.** Citymapper [shut down its public/self-serve developer API in June 2023](https://citymapper.com/news/2596/sdks-and-apis-come-to-an-end). I substituted **Apple Maps transit** (native, no API key) with **Google Routes** as an optional upgrade for line-level bus detail.
- **Not compiled here.** This build environment is Linux with no macOS/Xcode and no network to install web deps, so neither target was compiled in CI. Source is complete and reviewed; please build the iOS app in Xcode and run `next build`/`next lint` for the web part.
- **The "alarm" reality on iOS.** Only Apple's Clock app guarantees an always-on alarm at an arbitrary computed time. The app's realistic approach: **pre-schedule two local notifications** (which fire even when closed) and refresh them via background refresh / on foreground. Loud, silent-mode-bypassing rings need Apple's **Critical Alerts** entitlement (instructions in the iOS README).

## Native iOS — `ios/LeaveHouseAlarm/`

- **Calendar:** EventKit reads upcoming located events (uses the event's geo-coordinate if present, else geocodes the address).
- **Transit (pluggable `TransitProvider`):** Apple Maps `MKDirections.calculateETA` (default, no key) · Google Routes (optional key) · mock fallback.
- **Alarms:** two `UNCalendarNotificationTrigger` notifications scheduled ahead of time, `.timeSensitive`, optional `.defaultCritical` sound.
- **Background:** `BGTaskScheduler` re-plan + reschedule; also refreshes on foreground.
- **Quality:** pure `Scheduler` logic with XCTest coverage; `project.yml` (XcodeGen) + README with build steps.

## Web prototype — `/alarm` (optional)

- Installable **PWA** (`manifest.json` + service worker), full-bleed dark app shell.
- Same planning logic in `lib/leaveHouse/`; manual events + **ICS feed import**.
- Transit via `/api/journey` and ICS via `/api/calendar` so any API key stays **server-side** (set `GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY`); falls back to a built-in demo schedule with no config.
- Synthesized Web Audio alarm + Notification API; honest in-app note about background limits.

## How to try it

- **iOS:** `cd ios/LeaveHouseAlarm && xcodegen generate && open LeaveHouseAlarm.xcodeproj`, set your signing team, run on a device. See `ios/LeaveHouseAlarm/README.md`.
- **Web:** `yarn dev`, open `/alarm`, add an event with a location (works immediately with the mock provider).

## Open questions for you

1. Keep the web prototype, or **native-only**?
2. Transit provider preference — Apple Maps (zero setup) vs Google Routes (needs a key, richer bus detail)? If you have a specific city with an open feed (e.g. TfL/GTFS), I can add it behind the same interface.
3. Want me to pursue the **Critical Alerts** entitlement wiring / a Live Activity countdown next?

author: johanhaleby
body:
This is the last PR in the DCB subscription stack. It adds `@DcbSubscription`, the declarative DCB counterpart to `@StreamSubscription`, so a DCB read model is a single annotated method instead of an injected `DcbSubscriptions` DSL and a hand-rolled start position.

- `@DcbSubscription` takes `id`, `eventTypes` and `tagsAllOf` (which become the `DcbQuery`: neither gives all, types only, tags only, or both), `startAt` (BEGINNING, NOW, DEFAULT), `resumeBehavior`, and `startupMode`.
- The processor resolves the start position the same way the stream path does, over `dcbposition` instead of time. BEGINNING with the default resume replays from the start on the first run and resumes from the stored position afterwards. BEGINNING with `SAME_AS_START_AT` always replays, and disables the competing consumer and the durable position storage for that subscription, so an always-rebuilt in-memory read model sees every event and keeps no checkpoint.
- `DcbStartAt` gained a `dynamic` factory, the typed DCB counterpart to `StartAt.dynamic`, to back that resume logic.
- The DCB path routes through the `DcbSubscriptions` DSL, so it inherits the server-side filter and the in-process correctness floor. The method takes the event and, optionally, the generic `EventMetadata` or the DCB-specific `DcbEventMetadata`.
- The backend-agnostic processor helpers (parameter binding, concrete-event-type resolution) are now extracted and shared between the stream and DCB paths. The rename PR deferred this until a second consumer existed, and now it does.
- The course-enrollment `CourseDashboardSubscriber` is migrated to `@DcbSubscription`, replacing the hand-rolled subscription and the in-handler type check.

ADR 0027 records the decision.

### Verification

* `rtk mvn -pl framework/spring-boot-starter-mongodb -Dtest=DcbSubscriptionAnnotationMongoTest test`: Tests run: 1, Failures: 0, Errors: 0. A `@DcbSubscription(startAt = BEGINNING)` method replays two events appended before startup, then receives a live event, and never receives an event excluded by `eventTypes`.
* `rtk mvn -Pexamples-module -pl example/domain/course-enrollment test`: `CourseEnrollmentTest` 5 and `CourseEnrollmentWebTest` 9, with the dashboard now fed by the migrated `@DcbSubscription`.
* `rtk mvn -pl subscription/core,framework/annotations,framework/spring-boot-starter-mongodb -am test-compile`: clean.

author: desperatee
body:
## Summary

`ShouldSkipLimiter` has two bugs in the context-value branch that combine into a complete bypass of any rate limiter configured with `SetContextValue`:

### Bug 1 — `r.Header.Get` instead of `r.Context().Value` (line 160)

```go
for contextKey, contextValues := range lmtContextValues {
    for _, contextValue := range contextValues {
        if r.Header.Get(contextKey) == contextValue {   // ← wrong source
            requestContextValuesDefinedInLimiter = true
            break
        }
    }
}
```

The adjacent first-phase check on line 142 and `BuildKeys` on line 247 both correctly use `r.Context().Value(contextKey)`. This is the only site that reads from `r.Header` — almost certainly a copy-paste from a sibling function.

### Bug 2 — `fmt.Sprintf("%v", nil) != ""` is always true (line 142)

```go
reqContextValue := fmt.Sprintf("%v", r.Context().Value(contextKey))
if reqContextValue != "" {        // ← "<nil>" != "" is always true
    requestContextValuesDefinedInLimiter = true
    break
}
```

`fmt.Sprintf("%v", nil)` returns `"<nil>"` (5 chars), not `""`. The guard intended to skip when the context key is absent fires for **every** request, including those genuinely missing the key.

## Combined behavior

For a limiter configured with `lmt.SetContextValue("access-level", []string{"basic"})`:

| Request state                                | Expected            | Actual               |
|----------------------------------------------|---------------------|----------------------|
| context has `access-level=basic`             | rate limit applies  | **bypass**           |
| context has `access-level=premium`           | rate limit applies  | **bypass**           |
| context has no `access-level`                | skip                | bypass (via bug 2)   |

Effect: any `SetContextValue` limiter is a no-op rate limiter.

## Fix

- Line 160 → `fmt.Sprintf("%v", r.Context().Value(contextKey)) == contextValue`
- Line 142 → `r.Context().Value(contextKey) != nil`

## Severity

CRITICAL — silent rate-limit bypass with no log signal. Any deployment using `SetContextValue` for per-tier limits (typical SaaS pattern) is unprotected.

## Proof of Concept

`ShouldSkipLimiter` is responsible for filtering which requests should bypass the limiter based on context values configured via `SetContextValue`. Two bugs combine to make the filter unconditionally bypass the limiter for any non-empty `contextValues` list:

1. **Line 160 reads `r.Header.Get(contextKey)`** instead of the context value. The adjacent first-phase check at line 142 and `BuildKeys` at line 247 correctly call `r.Context().Value(contextKey)` — only this one site reads from the wrong source.
2. **Line 142 uses `fmt.Sprintf("%v", nil) != ""`**, which evaluates to `"<nil>" != ""` (always true), so the first-phase "absent-key skip" never fires for missing context keys.

Net effect: any limiter configured with `SetContextValue("key", []string{"some-value"})` skips rate limiting for **all** requests — including authenticated, anonymous, abusive, and trusted alike.

### Steps to Reproduce

```go
package tollbooth

import (
	"context"
	"net/http"
	"testing"

	"github.com/didip/tollbooth/v8/limiter"
)

func TestContextValueBypass(t *testing.T) {
	lmt := NewLimiter(1, nil).
		SetIPLookup(limiter.IPLookup{Name: "RemoteAddr"}).
		SetContextValue("access-level", []string{"basic"})

	req, _ := http.NewRequest("GET", "/", nil)
	req.RemoteAddr = "1.2.3.4:1234"
	//nolint:staticcheck
	req = req.WithContext(context.WithValue(req.Context(), "access-level", "basic"))

	if ShouldSkipLimiter(lmt, req) {
		t.Fatal("limiter bypassed despite matching context value")
	}
}

func TestContextKeyAbsenceShouldSkip(t *testing.T) {
	lmt := NewLimiter(1, nil).
		SetIPLookup(limiter.IPLookup{Name: "RemoteAddr"}).
		SetContextValue("tenant", []string{"premium"})

	// Request has NO 'tenant' context key
	req, _ := http.NewRequest("GET", "/", nil)
	req.RemoteAddr = "1.2.3.4:1234"

	if !ShouldSkipLimiter(lmt, req) {
		t.Fatal("limiter should skip when context key is absent")
	}
}
```

## What

When `headwaters` receives a shutdown signal, it previously logged nothing about the source — the logs jumped straight to `draining buffered writer`. This emits an info line in each arm of the `tokio::select!` in `shutdown_signal()` so the graceful-shutdown path records whether **Ctrl+C** or **SIGTERM** triggered it.

```
received SIGTERM, shutting down gracefully
draining buffered writer
stopping projection worker
```

## Why

In production the service is stopped via SIGTERM from the orchestrator; locally it's Ctrl+C. Recording which signal initiated shutdown makes the graceful-shutdown sequence visible and easier to diagnose.

author: svedova
body:
## Context

Phase 2 of the analytics hardening roadmap. The bot filter (`IsBot`, applied at `handler_forward.go` before recording analytics) relied on a hand-curated 72-entry list plus four keyword regexes, and had a latent correctness bug.

## The bug

`IsBot` short-circuited with `return false` whenever `hasSuspiciousPatterns` said a UA "looked like a browser" — *before* consulting the bot list or regexes. It only worked in practice by accident: the heuristic compared against lowercase `mozilla`/`webkit`/`gecko` while real browsers send `Mozilla`/`AppleWebKit`/`Gecko` capitalized, so the check was effectively always-true and the fall-through happened anyway. Any UA that did contain a lowercase engine token could slip past the authoritative checks.

## Changes

- **Vendored dataset** — embed `monperrus/crawler-user-agents` (MIT, 1,498 patterns) via `go:embed`, refreshable with `go generate`. All patterns are combined into a **single case-insensitive alternation** compiled once at init, so matching is one regex execution per request, not 1,498.
- **Fixed logic** — three **independent** layers (vendored dataset → supplementary list → keyword heuristics); any match wins. No more short-circuit. Grouped on a `botDetector` struct per repo conventions.
- **Trimmed the hand list** to ~24 org-specific agents the public dataset misses (uptime monitors like Pulsetic/upptime/ManicTime, niche preview/link checkers). Dropped the redundant entries and the **dangerously broad substrings** (`Google`, `Bing`, `Microsoft`, `Yahoo`, `Facebook`…) that risked false-positiving real users.
- **Dropped the bare `Viber` pattern** — it collides with real Viber in-app browsers, which we count as genuine visitors (it was the lone false positive against the real-user allow-list).
- **Added `Stormkit`** so our own domain health pinger (`StormkitBot`, see `job_domains.go`) never inflates customer analytics.

## Tests

- New `Test_IsBot_DetectsVendoredInstances`: asserts **every** example UA shipped with the dataset is detected (guards against the combined pattern silently losing coverage); skips the deliberately-excluded `Viber`.
- New `Test_IsBot_DetectsStormkitPinger`.
- Existing real-user allow-list (incl. `PostmanRuntime`, Viber webview, Dalvik, in-app browsers) and known-bot / case-insensitive suites still pass.
- `go vet` clean; `./src/ce/hosting/...` still builds.

## Notes

- Adds ~530 KB to the binary (the embedded JSON). Acceptable for a server binary; keeps a single source of truth that the tests also read for fixtures.
- Bot dropping happens at ingest unchanged — this PR only improves classification accuracy.

author: yogthos
body:
jolt maps were HAMTs with hash iteration order. Clojure keeps small maps as `PersistentArrayMap` (insertion order), converting to `PersistentHashMap` past a threshold. This was the last honeysql gap (column order in INSERT / do-update-set).

## Behavior

Insertion-ordered for ≤8 entries, matching the JVM:
- `{...}` literals, `array-map` (any size), `assoc`, `into`/transients, `merge`, `merge-with`, `zipmap`, `select-keys`, `update-keys`/`update-vals`, `frequencies`, `group-by`

Hash order (also JVM-faithful):
- `hash-map`, maps grown past the threshold, and sets

## Implementation

- `pmap` record gains an `order` field (insertion-order key list, or `#f` once hashed). The HAMT root still backs the values, so equality/hash/lookup are unchanged — only iteration order is affected.
- `pmap-fold` visits an array-mode map last-to-first, so the runtime's pervasive `(pmap-fold m (lambda (k v a) (cons … a)) '())` idiom reconstructs insertion order with no consumer edits, and hash-mode output stays byte-identical. `pmap-fold-fwd` visits in order for the few sites that build a value directly.
- Transient maps track insertion order and promote to hash past `max(8, source-count)`, matching `TransientArrayMap`.
- The `hash-map` native-op retargets to a hash-order builder so `(hash-map …)` stays hash-ordered while `{…}` literals are ordered. Syntax-quote builds maps via the hash builder (Clojure expands `` `{…} `` to `apply hash-map`).
- Core overlay map builders seed from `{}` instead of `(hash-map)` to keep order.

Threshold is 8 for any key — the `KW_HASHTABLE_THRESHOLD` in newer Clojure isn't in 1.12.5 (verified: assoc-reduce of 9 keyword keys → `PersistentHashMap`).

## Verification

- `make test` + `make shakesmoke` green; self-host fixpoint holds; 0 new divergences.
- 19 JVM-certified corpus rows added under suite `maps / insertion order`.
- honeysql **832/0/0** (was 6 map-order failures); aero 59/0/0, reitit map cases pass — no regressions.

Closes the map-order gap (bd jolt-2fl5).

author: glennjacobs
body:
Implements the **`lunarphp/demo-data`** sub-package from spec 0023 — a dev-only tool that seeds a coherent, reproducible demo store (catalogue, customers, orders) for evaluation, screenshots, and admin verification. Built as the spec's six reviewable slices (one commit each).

Depends on the accepted spec in #2522 (review that first for context).

## What it does

```bash
composer require --dev lunarphp/demo-data
php artisan lunar:demo-data                  # seed at the default (small) scale
php artisan lunar:demo-data --scale=medium   # or large
php artisan lunar:demo-data --fresh          # wipe demo-owned tables and reseed
php artisan lunar:demo-data --force          # required in a production environment
```

## Slices

1. **Scaffold** — `lunar:demo-data` command (`--scale`/`--fresh`/`--force`, `ConfirmableTrait` production guard), `DemoDataServiceProvider`, `config/demo-data.php`, `DemoContext`, `DemoDataSeeder` orchestrator over a `Generator` seam. Wired into the monorepo (autoload, provider, `replace`, test suite). Dev-only: installed under `require-dev`, omitted from a production `--no-dev` install.
2. **Foundation** — currencies (GBP default + USD/EUR), Webstore channel, Retail customer group, default Location, tax class/zone + 20% VAT. Keyed on natural handles so it reuses `lunar:install` records.
3. **Catalogue** — product type, collection group + a collection per category, products from a curated copy fixture (`products.json`); single-variant, per-currency prices, opening stock via the 0038 `adjustStock` seam (some zero/low stock), and a bundled placeholder image per product.
4. **Customers** — customers in the default group with a default billing/shipping address; ~half linked to a user account.
5. **Orders** — built from **source records** (lines, transactions, fulfilments) letting the observers settle the derived rollups. A fixed coverage set pins **every payment status** (pending → voided), **every fulfilment status** (unfulfilled → returned), **all three methods** (shipping/collection/digital), plus cancelled / closed / on-hold. Larger scales layer a natural distribution on top.
6. **Polish** — `--fresh` teardown (truncates demo-owned tables, leaves the shared foundation, `hasTable`-guarded), a double-seed guard, and per-generator faker reseeding for reproducible structure.

## Scope calls (flagged in the spec/commits)

- **Single-variant products** — option-based multi-variant (`ProductOption`/`ProductOptionValue`) is a deliberate follow-on.
- **Best-effort cosmetic determinism** — structure (catalogue, order coverage, counts) reproduces across runs; faker-derived names/addresses are not byte-identical because the framework draws from the global RNG stream mid-seed. Documented in the README.
- The `core` `DemoSeeder` is already the bare bootstrap the spec calls for, so it is unchanged.

## Verification

- `vendor/bin/pest --testsuite=demo-data` → **28 passed** (status/method/lifecycle coverage, idempotency, `--fresh`, guard, structural reproducibility).
- Pint + PHPStan clean.
- Exercised end-to-end in the host app: full coverage across both status axes, all methods, and `--fresh`/guard behaviour.

author: aignas
body:
Summary:
- Extract wheels in a repository A.
- Then parse METADATA in a repository B and C and reuse A everywhere.
- We also alias the targets for each entry point that is created in whl_library.
- The wheel repository names will be shorter in general that should help on systems
  like Windows, where path length is sometimes an issue.

Limitations:
- If users use the whl_mods API we cannot reuse the extracted whls.
- If users patch wheels, those are not reused.
- Reused only within the context of a single hub repo, we could do better with
  reuse across all of the hubs, but then we need to solve the "how to tell users
  that we need to have a single index per package? how to customize it?" problem.
- If we find the same wheel downloaded from different indexes in the same hub repo
  then we stop reuse for that particular wheel file. This should be rare?

Extra thoughts on the design:
- This is a step towards automatic cycle resolution.
- With uv.lock we can point directly to the extracted sources because
  the dep graph can be passed to the hub repo.

Once #3791 is resolved this should bring reasonable speedups, especially if there the same wheel used in multiple places.

Fixes #2948
Work towards #2530

author: davidobando
body:
## Bug

Tuple→tuple conversions were not classified element-wise. A tuple `(A, Derived)` could not convert to `(A, Base)` even though each element has an implicit conversion, and was rejected with **GS0155** (assignment/return) / **GS0154** (argument position). The same failure occurred for interface element subtyping `(A, Concrete) → (A, IFace)`, nullable-reference elements `(A, Derived?) → (A, Base?)`, and `let`-target/return positions.

```gsharp
package p
class A {}
open class Base {}
class Derived : Base {}
class C {
  func Take(t (A, Base)) {}
  func F(a A, d Derived) { Take((a, d)) }
}
```

## Root cause

`Conversion.Classify` (in `src/Core/CodeAnalysis/Binding/Conversion.cs`) treated a tuple type as a single nominal type requiring exact element identity, so any element that differed (even by a valid implicit upcast) caused the whole conversion to fail.

## Fix

- **`Conversion.Classify`** — when both sides are tuple types of the same arity, classify the conversion element-wise by recursively calling `Classify` on each element pair. If every element conversion is implicit, the tuple conversion is an implicit (non-identity) conversion; otherwise it declines and the conversion remains an error. Mirrors C# §10.2.13 and composes with every existing implicit rule (including the #1255 lifted nullable-reference upcast).
- **`ConversionClassifier.BindConversion`** — lower a non-identity implicit tuple conversion by **rebuilding** the destination `ValueTuple` from per-element converted accesses. The two `ValueTuple` instantiations differ at the CLR level, so a reinterpret is not verifiable IL. The source is evaluated exactly once (its elements reused directly when it is a tuple literal, otherwise spilled into a temp local and read by `ItemN`), and each element flows back through `BindConversion` for the correct per-element conversion.
- **`OverloadResolver`** — the user-function argument path only inserted a conversion node for value-type nullable targets and otherwise passed "implicit" arguments through unchanged (assuming a representation-preserving no-op). Tuple arguments need the rebuild, so same-arity tuple→tuple arguments are routed through `BindConversion`.

**Emit approach: binder-lowering.** The conversion is materialised by lowering the source into a tuple literal of converted elements, so the emitter reuses the existing tuple-literal construction path with **no emitter changes** and **no new Bound/Syntax node kinds**.

Guardrails preserved (still errors, as in C#): element downcast `(A, Base) → (A, Derived)`, no-conversion `(A, int32) → (A, string)`, and arity mismatch.

## Tests

- `test/Core.Tests/.../Issue1256ElementWiseTupleConversionTests.cs` — base-class, interface, 3-element mixed, and nullable-reference element conversions across argument, `let`-target, and return positions; identical-element control; negative downcast/no-conversion/arity-mismatch cases.
- `test/Compiler.Tests/Emit/Issue1256ElementWiseTupleConversionEmitTests.cs` — emit/execution tests (compile `/target:exe`, `IlVerifier.Verify`, run, compare stdout) proving identity is preserved through the rebuild and mixed (upcast + numeric widening) values are correct.

## Verification

- `dotnet build GSharp.sln -c Release -graph` → 0 errors / 0 warnings.
- `dotnet test test/Core.Tests/Core.Tests.csproj -c Release` → 4372 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed.
- Filtered emit tests + existing tuple/conversion emit suites pass.
- Minimal repro now compiles; identical-element control still compiles.

Fixes #1256

author: devasur
body:
Implements **ADR 0001** — cross-codebase linkage for `definition --at` on the existing tags engine, stateless (no index), extending the registry-dir data model.

## Step 1 — scope-aware resolution (`locals.scm`)
`definition --at` resolves a name to its nearest enclosing **local** binding before the directory-wide lookup, so a shadowing local/parameter wins over a same-named global — one binding instead of a candidate list. Driven by an optional `locals.scm` (`@local.scope`/`@local.definition`/`@local.reference`); grammars without one are unchanged.

## Step 2 — import-edge cross-file resolution (`imports.scm`)
When there's no local binding, grove follows an import statement to the **target file** and returns the definition there. Aliases resolve to the original symbol. At most one extra file is parsed — bounded by import depth, not repo size. Decision tree: **local → import → dir-wide**. Strategies: `dotted_package` (Python), `relative_path` (JS).

## Engine hardening (for hosting upstream `locals.scm`)
- Prefix-match captures (`local.definition*` etc.) so subtyped upstream files work (julia's `@local.definition.function`).
- Optional queries compile **non-fatally** — a bad registry query never breaks core tools.
- **Refuse tree-sitter supertype syntax** `(a/b)` that hard-crashes the wasm query engine at match time (found via webpack/js upstream `locals.scm`).

## Adoption (descriptions only — no tool signatures changed)
MCP `definition` description, CLI `--help`, and the `init` steering directive now tell agents `at` is the precise, scope-aware, cross-file mode.

## Evidence
Cross-file hit-rate probe vs a pyright oracle on pinned django (committed to grove-testbench): **92.6% recall on in-repo symbol imports, line-exact, zero confident-wrong answers** — every miss degrades to an ambiguous-but-correct fallback. Entire residual is the re-export tail. Verdict: the cheap wins (re-export one-hop, CommonJS `require()`) come before any stack-graphs tier.

## Companion changes (separate repos)
- `grove-registry`: hosts `locals.scm` for ruby/scala/julia/javascript (the upstream files that ship real scopes + run safely).
- `grove-testbench`: the hit-rate harness + results.

## Tests
117 unit + 17 integration, warning-clean. New: scope-aware + cross-file integration tests, non-fatal + supertype-guard tests, path-resolution unit tests.

See `docs/adr/0001-scope-aware-and-import-edge-resolution.md`.

## Résumé

Les buffs/debuffs affichent désormais leur **tooltip au survol** de la souris.

- **`CreateAuraIcon`** : les icônes d'aura activent la souris et branchent `OnEnter`/`OnLeave` qui affichent/masquent `GameTooltip` via `SetUnitAura`.

- `GameTooltip` n'étant pas protégé, ça fonctionne aussi **en combat**.

- [x] Survoler un buff/debuff sur player, target, focus, tot, pet → tooltip affiché (ancré à droite).
- [x] Avec le filtre « seulement les miennes » actif → le tooltip correspond bien à la bonne aura.
- [x] Fonctionne en combat ; le tooltip disparaît quand la souris quitte l'icône.

## Note

Activer la souris sur les icônes fait qu'un clic dessus ne ciblera plus l'unité à travers l'aura (comportement standard chez la plupart des addons d'auras).

author: shazolpersonal
body:
💡 **What:**
Extracted the static `sectionKeywords` mapping object out of the `Guide` component function body, placing it at the module scope as `SECTION_KEYWORDS`.

🎯 **Why:**
Previously, because the object was defined inside the `useMemo` block that depended on `searchQuery`, a new object was allocated in memory on every single keystroke while typing in the search bar. This caused unnecessary garbage collection pressure and main thread work during a high-frequency event.

📊 **Impact:**
Reduces memory allocations to exactly one (at module load time) rather than one per keystroke, guaranteeing smoother text input performance during search filtering on lower-end devices.

🔬 **Measurement:**
Verified that `pnpm lint` and `pnpm test` pass. The search functionality in the Guide behaves exactly as before, with no functional regressions.

author: koteine
body:
### Motivation
- The Rapunzel tarot card should guarantee the next dice roll is multiplied by 2, but previously the roll was not preserved and doubling did not apply to the next roll.  
- Bonus (lucky) cells sometimes blocked choice when the same bonus task text had been used by someone else; bonus tasks must be available per player even if the same text exists globally.

### Description
- Add `next_roll_doubled` user flag and persist it in the DB schema so the double-roll buff is stored until the next roll (`server.js`).
- Change tarot handling for `double_roll` to set `next_roll_doubled = 1` instead of executing an immediate two-dice move, and clear conflicting `next_roll_halved` when set (`server.js`).
- Apply `next_roll_doubled` on the next `/api/roll` call: compute `rawDice`, detect `next_roll_doubled`, double the raw value, pass `roll_doubled` in the move result meta, and ensure the flag is reset after the move (`server.js`).
- Ensure `next_roll_doubled` is cleared on landing (including lucky cell flows), on reset/approve flows and when creating pending submissions so the buff cannot be reused accidentally (`server.js`).
- Add `getOrCreateTaskByText` helper and use it in the lucky-choice flow so bonus task creation is robust when the same text already exists and different players can receive the same task text (`server.js`).
- Surface `next_roll_doubled` in `/api/me` responses and update client messages/UI to reflect guaranteed x2 on next roll and to show a Rapunzel toast when doubled roll occurs (`server.js`, `public/script.js`).
- Add smoke tests covering Rapunzel doubling and reused lucky choices (`test/api-smoke.test.js`).

### Testing
- Ran syntax checks: `node --check server.js` and `node --check public/script.js`, both succeeded.  
- Ran the test suite with `npm test`, all smoke tests passed (4/4).
