author: smarzban
body:
## In-file navigation — Phase 1: **Go to line** (`:`)

First half of the in-file-navigation feature (Linear project *In-file navigation*). **Staged build:** this PR ships **go-to-line only**; in-file search (`/`, `n`/`N`) follows as PR #2.

### What & why
The viewer can move *between* files (tree, and the `f` finder) but had no way to navigate *within* the open file. This adds the universal `:N` primitive: press `:`, type a line number, `Enter` jumps the content pane there.

### Behavior
- `:` opens a one-line **bottom prompt**; digits build the number, non-digits are ignored, `Backspace` edits.
- `Enter` jumps so the target source line is visible (landed near the top); **out-of-range clamps** to the last line; **empty `Enter`** closes with no jump; `Esc` cancels (scroll unchanged).
- **View-gated:** available only in the **source-mapped** (syntax/content) view, where a source line maps 1:1 to a display row. In rendered-markdown / diff / full-diff (or with nothing selected) it shows a one-line *"unavailable"* notice and opens nothing — honest about the absent line→row map (see ADR-0006).
- Fully **read-only** — pure in-memory navigation; no file/git mutation, no persistent state, no event hook (opens only on the explicit `:` key).

### Acceptance criteria covered
- **AC-1** open prompt (source-mapped) · **AC-2** digit entry · **AC-3** jump visible · **AC-4** 1-based, clamp out-of-range · **AC-5** empty-Enter no-op · **AC-6** Esc no-op · **AC-7** unavailable+notice in transformed views (incl. `FullDiff`)
- **AC-21** (go-to-line portion) prompt keys don't fire viewer intents · **AC-N6** no event/auto trigger

### Tasks → commits
| Task | Commit | Advances |
|---|---|---|
| T-1 content `scroll_to_line` | `f3e43dc` | AC-3, AC-4 |
| T-2 `OpenGoToLine` intent + `:` key + view-gated open | `f1ffce3` | AC-1, AC-7, AC-N6 |
| T-3 keystroke + confirm + cancel | `1a3aa6f` | AC-2, AC-3, AC-4, AC-5, AC-6 |
| T-4 event-loop routing + Presenter bottom prompt | `0e0a6e2` | AC-1, AC-7 |
| T-5 pty e2e | `f9f36d1` | AC-21 |
| docs (README/CHANGELOG/ARCHITECTURE) | `1a229a1` | — |

New modules: `src/infile.rs` (prompt-modal state). Reuses go-to-file's `src/prompt.rs` `PromptInput` and the `app.rs` modal raw-key routing.

### Tests
Unit (`intent`, `input`), integration (`controller` — open/gate/clamp/empty/Esc/directory-edge), Presenter (bottom-prompt render + AC-7 notice, **zero snapshot churn**), and a pty **e2e** (`:`+`j`-swallowed+`40`→jump; `:` on markdown→unavailable). **469 tests pass**; clippy `-D` / fmt / release all clean.

### Notes for the reviewer
- **No deferred shortcuts / `SHORTCUT(T-N)` ceilings** recorded by the build.
- This branch's base includes the docs-backfill #53 (go-to-file + tree-title), merged to `main` first so docs stay consistent.
- The full spec chain (Brief / AC / Design / Tech Stack / Plan / gate-report) lives in the Linear project *In-file navigation* and in `specs/in-file-navigation/` (local-only/gitignored); ADR-0006 records the search-over-displayed-content + view-gated-go-to-line decision.
- **Merge is owner-gated** — please don't auto-merge.

author: vishwabhishek
body:
## Description
When embedding text that is too short to be split further but still exceeds the context window of the embedding model, embedding engines correctly raise an `EmbeddingException`.
However, the `@retry` decorator on the `embed_text` method in `FastembedEmbeddingEngine`, `LiteLLMEmbeddingEngine`, and `OpenAICompatibleEmbeddingEngine` was catching this exception and retrying the operation with exponential backoff for up to 128 seconds. Since this error is deterministic and non-transient, retrying causes production hangs and makes unit tests take over 4 minutes to complete.

This PR adds `EmbeddingException` to the list of excluded exception types in `retry_if_not_exception_type` inside the `@retry` decorators for all three engines.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `EmbeddingException` is not retried by tenacity.
- Unit tests for context window fallbacks complete instantly rather than hanging.

## Type of Change
- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Pre-submission Checklist
- [x] **I have tested my changes thoroughly before submitting this PR** (See `CONTRIBUTING.md`)

author: tamnd
body:
The hybrid string and collection paths wrote straight to the v2 store with no bookkeeping, so used_memory stayed at zero, OBJECT FREQ returned 0 for every key, and the eviction OOM gate never fired. That left five command tests red under AKI_TEST_HYBRID=1: TestUsedMemoryTracksData, TestObjectFreq, TestLFULogFactorConfig, TestNoEvictionOOM, and TestVolatileNoVolatileKeysOOM.

The btree path keeps used_memory and the LFU access record exact by reading the previous value's size from the leaf cell it already holds. The hybrid path had no such cell, and a read-before-write to fetch the old size would add a second index probe on the hot SET path and regress the 2x string result.

The v2 store already locates the old record on every upsert and delete to confirm the key, so the displaced value's length is free there. indexPut and indexDelete now return it, shard.set/del thread it up, and new SetWithPrev / DeleteWithPrev surface it while the plain Set/Delete keep their exact signatures, so the v2 server fast path is byte-for-byte unchanged. The keyspace hybrid layer folds the delta into dataBytes and the LFU record through hlAccountStore, mirroring db.set, and the hybrid read paths (get when touch, GetUncached) call recordAccess where getProbe does. Lazy expiry in hlGet routes through hlDelete so an expired key leaves used_memory correctly.

Tests:
- AKI_TEST_HYBRID=1 go test ./command/ goes from 5 failures to green.
- New keyspace unit tests (hybrid_accounting_test.go): TestHybridUsedMemoryDelta walks a key through a fresh write, a shorter and a longer overwrite, and a delete, asserting used_memory tracks the entry cost exactly and returns to baseline; TestHybridFreqOnSetAndGet asserts a Set seeds the LFU counter, ten Gets at log factor 0 climb it one per read, and a delete forgets it.
- Default btree command suite, keyspace, and v2 store stay green under -race.

The accounting did not regress the fast path: in-process hybrid SET 167 ns/op vs btree 447 ns/op, hybrid GET 45 ns/op vs btree 140 ns/op. The added cost is one same-cache-line header read on an overwrite, a TryLock-guarded LFU bump that drops under contention, and two dataBytes atomic adds, all of which the btree path already paid.

With this the hybrid command suite is fully green, the last compat bucket on the in-place engine swap.

author: inureyes
body:
## Summary

Phase 3 M2 wires the OpenXLA backend (issue #449, ADR 0004 Track B) from the M1 scaffold and the M2 FFI gate to real, token-exact execution driven end to end from the `mlxcel` CLI.

- The C shim (proven first in `spike/iree-ffi`, then vendored to `src/lib/mlxcel-xla/csrc/xla_iree.c`) loads the #451-emitted `prefill`/`decode_step` vmfbs into one IREE session, uploads the 146 weights once as resident device buffers (bf16 to f32 via the `safetensors` crate, in the emitter's arg order), threads the KV cache across steps, and returns a token id per step. Output is read by element type, so the same shim drives both the logits graph (host argmax) and the on-device-argmax graph (a 4-byte scalar, the Phase 2b pattern). Rust drives the real Llama-3.2-1B token-exact (48/48) vs HF temp-0 on CPU.
- Real execution is behind a new `mlxcel-xla` `iree` feature, exposed at the root as `xla-iree = ["xla-backend", "mlxcel-xla/iree"]`. Without it, `--features xla-backend` still builds with no IREE distribution (CI unchanged) and `prefill`/`decode_step` return a built-without-iree error.
- The #451 emitter gains on-device argmax (`Builder::argmax`, the index-tracking two-operand reduce) behind a `sample` flag, and the prefill bucket is bumped to `MAX_SEQ` (256) so the default chat-template prompt fits one bucket; both stay token-exact. Bundled graphs (`assets/llama-3.2-1b`) compile to vmfbs at session load via the dist `iree-compile`, cached by content hash.
- `ComputeBackend::create_session` now takes the model directory path (MLX ignores it; XLA loads its own weights and config). `run_generate_once` gains a self-contained XLA branch, taken when `MLXCEL_BACKEND=xla`, that skips `load_model` (which the XLA backend rejects) and drives the session's own greedy loop, then rejoins the shared decode and print path.

## How to run (local)

```
export IREE_DIST=/path/to/iree-dist-3.12.0rc20260626-linux-aarch64
cargo build --release --features xla-iree
MLXCEL_BACKEND=xla ./target/release/mlxcel generate -m <Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct> -p "..." -n 48
```

## Build gotcha (recorded)

A dependency's `cargo:rustc-link-arg` does not propagate to the final binary link, so `mlxcel-xla/build.rs` only compiles the shim (its `rustc-link-lib` propagates) and the IREE runtime link recipe (`--whole-archive` of the unified runtime plus a `--start-group` of flatcc and libgcc/libm) lives in a new root `build.rs` gated on `CARGO_FEATURE_XLA_IREE`. No-op for default and `xla-backend` builds.

## Scope and limits (M2)

- Bundled graphs are authored for Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct (`config.json` is verified, a mismatch errors); prompts are capped at the 256-token bucket; sampling is greedy and text-only.
- The prebuilt aarch64 IREE dist registers `local`/`vulkan` HAL drivers but **not CUDA**, so M2 runs on CPU (about 2 tok/s). Phase 2b's CUDA used the pip runtime; a GPU device is a follow-up. (This corrects the earlier FINDINGS claim that the dist had a cuda driver.)

## Validation

- Spike token-exact 48/48 (bucket 64 and 256).
- `cargo build` default, `--features xla-backend`, and `--features xla-iree` (with `IREE_DIST`) all green.
- `cargo test -p mlxcel-xla` 5/5; `cargo test --features xla-backend --lib backend::` 6/6.
- `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy` (default, `xla-backend`, `xla-iree`) clean.
- `MLXCEL_BACKEND=xla mlxcel generate` end to end (raw prompt and default chat template).

Refs #449.

body:
## 🎯 Objective
This PR introduces several minor UI bug fixes and layout improvements across the frontend to improve responsiveness, user experience, and visual consistency.

## 🐛 Bugs Addressed & Changes Made

### 1. Sidebar Layout & Redundancy Fixes
- **The Bug:** On roles with fewer navigation tabs (like Accounts), the "Report a Bug" and "User Guide" buttons would float upwards rather than staying pinned to the absolute bottom of the screen. 
- **The Fix:** Added `h-full` and `md:h-full` to the sidebar container and its parent wrapper in `Layout.jsx` and `Sidebar.jsx`. This corrects flexbox height propagation, forcing the sidebar to stretch to the viewport height and correctly pushing bottom-aligned items down.
- **Cleanup:** Removed the "School Settings" tab from the Admin sidebar, resolving the redundancy since it is already accessible via the top-right profile dropdown.

### 2. Global Modal Stacking Context (Bug Reports)
- **The Bug:** When opening a full-screen image preview in the Bug Reports module, the dark background overlay was trapped under the sidebar (`z-50`) due to the main content container's isolated stacking context (`z-10`). The overlay was also an opaque dark color, breaking visual consistency.
- **The Fix:** Leveraged React's `createPortal` to mount the Image Preview Modal directly into `document.body`, breaking it out of local stacking contexts so it spans the entire screen flawlessly.
- **Visual Polish:** Updated the backdrop to `bg-gray-900/40 backdrop-blur-sm` to perfectly match the translucent blur effect of the Logout alert.
- **UI Cleanup:** Removed the redundant `X` (close) button from the preview modal, leaning on the cleaner "click anywhere outside the image to close" interaction.

### 3. Role-Based Access Control in Fee Tables
- **The Bug:** Students with no recorded fees were erroneously shown a "Create Invoice" button in the Fees transaction history (which would ultimately fail on the backend due to API security).
- **The Fix:** Updated the desktop and mobile render logic in `Fees.jsx`. The "Create Invoice" action is now strictly restricted to `ADMIN` and `ACCOUNTS` roles. For students, this action is hidden entirely on mobile and replaced with a clean dash (`-`) on the desktop table.

## 🧪 Testing Performed
- [x] Verified sidebar items correctly pin to the bottom on desktop and mobile resolutions across different roles (Admin, Accounts, Student).
- [x] Confirmed the Image Preview modal correctly overlaps the Sidebar and Navbar with a translucent blur.
- [x] Confirmed clicking outside the image preview successfully closes the modal.
- [x] Tested the Fees UI as a Student to ensure no actionable invoice creation buttons are rendered.

author: christopherchudzicki
body:
### What are the relevant issues?

Supersedes #1063 (renovate: update react-router-dom to v7.18.0). Also addresses the react-router half of #998.

### Description

The renovate PR bumped only `react-router-dom` to 7.18.0, leaving `react-router` resolved at 7.4.1 in the lockfile even though both shared the `^7.4.1` range. `react-router-dom@7.18.0` depends on `react-router@7.18.0`, so the project ended up with **two** `react-router` copies whose `Router` types had diverged (7.18 added `unstable_middleware`). That broke `main.tsx:50` with TS2322 — `createBrowserRouter` (from react-router-dom’s nested react-router) was no longer assignable to `RouterProviderProps["router"]` (from the top-level react-router@7.4.1).

Fix: bump **both** `package.json` floors to `^7.18.0` so they dedupe to a single `react-router@7.18.0`. Raising the floor (not just the lockfile) is the **durable** fix — with `^7.4.1` the manifest still permitted the exact broken split to re-resolve on any future lockfile regeneration; `^7.18.0` forecloses it. As an app, the manifest should track installed versions.

### How can this be tested?

`yarn workspace app typecheck` passes (the TS2322 at main.tsx:50 is gone); `yarn workspace app test` passes (37 files, 178 tests). Routing smoke-check covered by the e2e suite in CI.

### Additional context

Minor bump within v7. Lockfile churn limited to react-router packages and their transitive deps (drops `@types/cookie` and `turbo-stream`, which 7.18 no longer declares). The `^7.4.1` descriptor is fully gone — only a single `react-router@7.18.0` resolution remains. Closes out #1063 once merged.

body:
## 概要

`/ui/items` ライブラリ画面のアイテムカードをサイドバーのタグ要素へドラッグ&ドロップするだけで
タグを付与できるようにする（Issue #120）。既存の `POST /v1/items/bulk-tag` エンドポイントを
単一 item_id で利用し、新規 API は追加しない。タッチデバイス向けには `(pointer: coarse)` 検出
でカード上の「タグ付与」ボタンを表示する代替手段を提供する。既存の絞り込みトグル（#117）・
アクティブフィルタチップ（#115）・一括選択 UI（#118）・状態タブ（#119）への非回帰を確認済み。

## 対応 Issue

Closes #120

## 関連 PR

なし（Architect は起動せず、単一実装パス）

## 実装内容

- (Req 1.1) `templates/items_list.html` のカードに `draggable="true"` / `data-item-card` を付与し、ドラッグ可能要素として提供
- (Req 1.2 / 3.4 / 3.5) `templates/items.html` サイドバー・ボトムシート両方の `.tag-filter-option` に `data-tag-drop-target` / `data-tag-name` / `data-tag-normalized` を付与
- (Req 1.3 / 1.4 / 2.1) `static/items_drag_tag.js` — DnD + タッチ代替の実装（IIFE）。ドロップ成功時に bulk-tag POST し、`succeeded[0].tags` でチップを再描画
- (Req 3.1 / 3.2 / 3.3) `.is-dragging` / `.is-drop-target` / `.is-tag-target` クラスで視覚フィードバック（色非依存・outline/opacity）
- (Req 4.1 / 4.2 / 4.3) `matchMedia('(pointer: coarse)')` 検出時にカード上「タグ付与」ボタンを表示。tap → assignTag でドロップと同一ロジックを共有
- (Req 5.1 / 5.2 / 5.5) 通信失敗・非 200・failed[] 返却時はチップ不付与 + toast.error 通知
- (NFR 2.1) JS 非対応環境では既存編集経路を維持（プログレッシブエンハンスメント）
- (NFR 1.1 / 1.2) server / migration / extension への変更なし。API 契約変更なし
- `static/items_drag_tag.test.mjs` — 単体テスト 14 件（fake DOM + fetch stub）
- `internal/ui/render_test.go` — SSR 契約を担保する `TestDragTagSSRContract` 6 サブテスト

## 受入基準チェック

- [x] Req 1.1: カードが draggable ← `TestDragTagSSRContract`「Req 1.1」
- [x] Req 1.2 / 3.4: タグ要素がドロップ先 ← `TestDragTagSSRContract`「Req 1.2 / 3.4」
- [x] Req 1.3 / 1.4 / 2.1: ドロップで付与・チップ反映・bulk-tag URL ← drag-tag.test「Req 1.3 / 1.4 / 2.1」
- [x] Req 1.5: 対象外ドロップで no-op ← drag-tag.test「Req 1.5」
- [x] Req 1.6 / NFR 2.2 / 2.3: ドラッグ中に絞り込み等不変 ← drag-tag.test「NFR 2.2 / 2.3」
- [x] Req 2.3 / 2.4: 冪等・重複なし ← drag-tag.test「Req 2.3 / 2.4」
- [x] Req 3.1 / 3.2 / 3.3: 視覚フィードバック ← drag-tag.test「Req 3.1」「Req 3.2 / 3.3」
- [x] Req 3.5: サイドバー/ボトムシート同一挙動 ← drag-tag.test「Req 3.4 / 3.5」 + render_test
- [x] Req 4.1 / 4.2 / 4.3: タッチ代替 ← drag-tag.test「Req 4.1」「Req 4.2 / 4.3」
- [x] Req 5.1 / 5.2 / 5.5: 異常系（失敗時非反映 + 通知） ← drag-tag.test「Req 5.1 / 5.2」「Req 5.5」
- [x] NFR 2.1: JS 無効時の既存動線維持 ← SSR fallback（type=button hidden）
- [x] NFR 4.1 / 4.2: アクセシビリティ（タッチ代替 + 色非依存） ← CSS outline/opacity

## テスト結果

```
go test ./...               全 PASS（TestDragTagSSRContract 追加）
node --test static/*.test.mjs   177 pass / 0 fail（baseline 163 + 新規 14）
node --test extension/sidepanel.test.mjs  30 pass / 0 fail（拡張機能非回帰）
golangci-lint run           0 issues
go build ./...              OK
```

## 実装上の判断

- **永続化エンドポイント**: `POST /v1/items/bulk-tag` を単一 item_id で利用。additive かつ冪等で所有権チェック・タグ正規化済みのため、全置換 PUT より冪等性実装が簡潔（impl-notes.md 参照）
- **タッチ代替**: `matchMedia('(pointer: coarse)')` 検出でカード上ボタンを表示し、tap → 同一 `assignTag` でロジック共有。2-in-1 端末でも両手段が利用可能
- **視覚フィードバック**: `.is-dragging` / `.is-drop-target` / `.is-tag-target` の CSS クラスによる最小限の演出（outline + opacity）。色非依存（NFR 4.2 準拠）
- **`succeeded[0]` 前提**: 単一 item_id 送信のため `succeeded[0].tags` でチップを再描画。bulk-tag 契約変更時は追従要

## 確認事項 / レビュワーへの依頼

- design-less impl: 単一 PR で完了のため Closes を採用
- base: develop / baseRefName: develop / OK（検証済み）
- Reviewer 承認済み（RESULT: approve / `docs/specs/120-issue/review-notes.md` 参照）
- **タッチ環境判定** (`pointer: coarse`): 2-in-1 端末でも表示されるが実害なし（impl-notes.md 確認事項 1）
- **toast 文言**: 日本語直書き。i18n 方針が別途あれば調整余地あり（impl-notes.md 確認事項 2）
- **chip 再描画と #117 絞り込み状態**: 付与直後の chip は `aria-pressed="false"` 固定（impl-notes.md 確認事項 4）

body:
## Summary

- Threads joystick controller name through the axis command pipeline so two separate USB controllers can each use Up/Down independently for Pong
- Adds a "Multi-Player" control mode (controls == 4) that routes input to P1 or P2 based on the controller name
- Other games (Tetris, Snake, Breakout) strip the controller name suffix and are unaffected

Squashed and rebased onto the latest FPP10 plugin code as requested in #8.

## Changes

- **FPPArcade.h** — `axis()` gains an optional `joystickName` parameter

author: dimitri
body:
## Problem

When a SQLite TEXT column contains bytes that are not valid UTF-8, pgloader emitted a terse error and aborted the entire table load:

```
ERROR Illegal :UTF-8 character starting at position 34.
```

No table name, no row identifier, no column name — making it very difficult for users to find the offending record (see #1250).

## Fix

Catches `babel-encodings:character-decoding-error` **per column** (inside the inner column-reading loop) rather than via the outer table-level handler.  When the error fires the message now includes:

- table name
- encoding name and byte position (matching MySQL/MSSQL style)
- **primary-key value** of the offending row — when the PK column was already read before the failing column, which is the common case (id in col 0, text in col 1)
- column name

The bad column is substituted with **NULL** so the row is still inserted and the rest of the table continues loading — the same behaviour the MySQL and MSSQL sources provide via their `use-nil` restarts.

### Why handler-case instead of handler-bind + restart?

Babel defines **no restarts** for `character-decoding-error` (unlike qmynd/mssql which expose a `use-nil` restart).  `handler-case` at the column-read site gives the same outcome (substitute nil, continue) without requiring a restart.

## Sample error output (after fix)

```
ERROR While decoding text from SQLite table files:
Illegal UTF-8 character at byte position 4, pkey 2, column filename.
```

## Test artifacts

- `test/sqlite/bad-utf8.db` — SQLite database with one row containing a Windows-1252 em-dash (0x96) stored in a TEXT column; rows 1 and 3 are valid UTF-8
- `test/sqlite/create-bad-utf8.py` — script to regenerate that database
- `test/sqlite-bad-utf8.load` — pgloader load file for manual verification

The SQLite LOAD DATABASE command cannot be wired into the standard `--regress` framework (which expects a single `?tablename` in the URI), so this is provided as a manual test artifact rather than a REGRESS entry.

Closes #1250

author: st0newan9
body:
## Problem
KB auto-discovery rescans were failing on every tick with:

```
OwnerContextUnsetError: current_user_id is unset; owner-scoped reads require an owner
  load_routing_config → get_primary_plugin_id → _read_json → get_setting(require_current_user_id())
```

The scheduler's per-KB loop called `load_routing_config(db)` (which does owner-scoped settings reads) **before** any owner context was published. Only `rescan_kb` set the owner — too late for the routing-config read.

## Fix
Publish each KB's owner on the `current_user_id` ContextVar around the per-KB iteration (try/finally, mirroring `automations/in_process_runner`), so `load_routing_config` and `rescan_kb` both resolve against the KB's owner. Legacy rows with no `user_id` skip publishing (downstream default-user fallback applies).

## Verification
- `ruff` + `mypy` clean on the file.
- `pytest -k "scheduler or auto_discover or docs"` — 101 pass.

author: foxace
body:
## Erreur remontée en production (5.17.0)

```
last_called probe API TypeError (PUSH_VOLUME_CHANGE): Cannot serialize non-str key None
  File ".../alexapy/alexaapi.py", line 458, in _static_request
  File ".../aiohttp/http_writer.py", ... _serialize_headers
  TypeError: Cannot serialize non-str key None
```

### Diagnostic
- Le probe worker `last_called` appelle `AlexaAPI.get_customer_history_records` ; l'erreur survient **profondément dans alexapy/aiohttp** — un **en-tête HTTP avec une clé `None`**, qui surface sur **Python 3.14 / aiohttp récent**.
- **Cause racine côté alexapy**, pas l'intégration (les params passés — start/end/max_record_size — ne deviennent pas des clés d'en-tête).
- **Pas une régression** : ce handler a été extrait verbatim de `__init__` lors de la décomposition `setup/`.

### Le code gère déjà l'erreur
Il fait un backoff et **ré-arme le probe** → condition **auto-réparante** (la traceback indiquait « 1 occurrence », donc transitoire).

### Fix
Le souci était le **niveau de log** : `WARNING` + traceback complet (`exc_info=True`) pour un événement transitoire auto-récupéré → affiché comme une erreur alarmante. Passé en **`DEBUG`** (traceback conservée si le debug est activé). Comportement inchangé par ailleurs.

Un futur alexapy (désormais suivi par Renovate) pourra corriger la racine en amont.

### Validation
ruff clean, 63 tests `last_called` verts, suite complète OK.

author: wizarck
body:
## What
The iguanatrader half of WS-4 (WS-F). The live IBKR gateway logs the owner out of the IBKR mobile app (one live session), so it can't run continuously — it's spun up on demand to drain approved live orders and torn down right after. The **container lifecycle** (spin-up + the hard ~5-min TTL teardown + the Telegram "gateway down" notice) runs in **eligia-core's AIOps sidecar** (cross-repo, no `docker.sock` in the trading container). This PR builds the iguanatrader side of that contract.

The iguanatrader side requests a short **lease** before each live order and **refuses to place it if the gateway is not ready** — a real-money order must never be sent at a gateway we can't confirm is up (**fail-closed**). Teardown is the sidecar's job via the lease TTL, so there's no teardown choreography here.

## Pieces
- **`EligiaSidecarGatewayClient`** — HMAC-signed POST to the sidecar webhook (`X-Signature: sha256=…` over the exact body, reusing `shared/channel_dispatch/sign.py`). Any transport error degrades to **not-ready** (never raises).
- **`EphemeralGatewayCoordinator.ensure_up()`** — leases up and caches the confirmed window so a **batch** of orders reuses one gateway (one webhook per window, not per order), re-leases on expiry, returns `False` (fail-closed) when not ready.
- **`execute_on_approval_handler`** — for `mode=="live"` + an injected coordinator, `ensure_up()` runs **before any Trade/Order is created**; not-ready → `OrderRejected(reason="gateway_unavailable")` and return (nothing to orphan). Paper orders + the unwired case skip it entirely (byte-identical).
- **`build_ephemeral_gateway_coordinator_from_env()`** — `None` unless `IGUANATRADER_EPHEMERAL_GATEWAY_ENABLED` + `ELIGIA_GATEWAY_WEBHOOK_URL` + `ELIGIA_GATEWAY_HMAC_SECRET` are set. **Flag-gated OFF.**

## Contract for the eligia-core side
```
POST {webhook_url}
header  X-Signature: sha256=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of the exact body, shared secret>
body    {"action":"lease","reason":"<str>","ttl_seconds":<int>}
→ 200   {"ready": true|false, "detail": "<str>"}
```
The sidecar holds the gateway up for `ttl_seconds` and auto-tears-down on expiry (the hard 5-min cap), notifying via Telegram.

## Safety
With the flag off (default), the live path is **unchanged** — paper never consults it. Real-money LIVE activation remains the operator's deliberate, **Telegram-gated** action; this only makes the live path gateway-aware when explicitly enabled, and fails **closed**.

## Tests
Coordinator (ready / fail-closed, batch lease reuse, re-lease on expiry, no-cache-on-failure), HMAC client (exact-body signing, transport-error → not-ready), env factory (off without flag/creds, on when configured), and the execute-path gate (live not-ready → fail-closed no-order; live ready → proceeds; paper → never consulted).

author: edwin-zvs
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #489. The session canvas editor still draws its cursor slightly off from the text on **wrapped lines that contain spaces**.

`canvas_cursor_position` (after #489) wraps with **naive character division**: it counts preceding wrapped rows as `ceil(rendered_width / width)` and places the cursor within its line via `visual_col / width`. But the body renders with `Paragraph::new(...).wrap(Wrap { trim: false })`, and ratatui **word-wraps at whitespace** (hard-breaking only words longer than the width). On a line like `hello world foo` at width 8, ratatui lays out three rows (`hello` / `world` / `foo`) — it breaks at the spaces, *earlier* than char-division predicts. So:

- the cursor lands inside the wrong word on the wrapped line, and
- because the preceding-line row count is also wrong, the offset **compounds** for every line below a wrapped one.

## Fix — one word-wrap, used everywhere

Replace the char-division with a faithful port of ratatui's `WordWrapper` (`trim == false` path), `canvas_wrap_row_starts`, used as the **single source of truth** for *both* the preceding-line row count *and* the cursor's intra-line `(row, col)`.

I evaluated reusing the existing `wrap_to_width` (per the issue's suggestion) but **verified by rendering** that it does **not** match `Wrap { trim: false }` — it emits a spurious empty row after a hard break adjacent to a space, wraps overflowing trailing whitespace, and fragments leading indentation. The new port was checked cell-for-cell against ratatui's `TestBackend` for: word breaks, hard breaks, trailing whitespace, leading indent, and collapsed multi-space runs.

`canvas_rendered_line_text` reconstructs the exact glyphs the renderer paints (kept heading markers, the `  • ` list prefix, expanded smart-clip chips) so wrapping sees the same spaces ratatui sees. Chip labels come from the same `canvas_smart_clip_label` the width math already uses, keeping width and text consistent.

## Tests (TDD — written first, confirmed failing on the #489 code)

- `canvas_cursor_position_word_wraps_line_with_spaces` — cursor after a space-wrap lands at the start of the right row (old: row 1 col 4, inside `world`).
- `canvas_cursor_position_word_wrapped_line_offsets_following_line` — a normal line below a 3-row word-wrapped line lands on row 4 (old: row 3, undercounted via `ceil(15/8)=2`).
- `canvas_cursor_position_hard_break_then_space_no_phantom_row` — `abcd efgh` @ width 4 is two rows, not three (guards against the `wrap_to_width` spurious-empty-row failure mode).
- `canvas_cursor_position_matches_painted_glyph_on_wrapped_line` — renders via the same `Paragraph::wrap(Wrap{trim:false})` and asserts the computed cursor cell sits on the painted `f` (old code computed a `d`).

The existing `canvas_cursor_position_*` tests use space-free lines (where char-division and word-wrap coincide), so they pass **unchanged** — no old behavior was re-baselined.

`cargo test -p agentd-cli` (351 tests) and `cargo build --workspace --all-targets --locked` both pass. Diff is confined to `crates/cli/src/ui.rs`.

Relevant binary: this PR only touches `crates/cli` → `construct`.

author: meganechan
body:
## What

Three **human-facing** UX fixes for `maw hey` so agents don't have to memorize messaging semantics. Root cause of the recurring "ว่างแต่ message ค้าง queue" confusion was UX, not a delivery bug (proven via tmux PoC by eq3+thawanban).

**No change to delivery semantics, state machine, busy guard, or routing behavior — wording + warnings only.**

1. **Offline-persist reword (CLI).** The `⤷` line that read `target not live; persisted for receiver inbox polling` (reads like a failure) → `delivered to <name>'s inbox (not live now) — they'll read it on the next poll`. Feed-event delivery **state stays `queued`**; only the operator-visible reason changed.
2. **Federation-vs-local hint.** Sending `node:name` (e.g. `mba:nai`) while `name` also has a **live local session** → prints a hint: *"'nai' is live locally — use the bare name to inject directly…"*. **No auto-redirect** — addressing a node explicitly may be intentional, so we only surface it. New pure helper `peerLocalOverrideHint`.
3. **Unknown-node hint.** `node 'X' not in namedPeers` keeps its error/reason; the hint now also points at `maw locate <name>`.

## Risk
- **Low.** Only operator-visible strings + one new read-only `console.warn` hint.
- The API-side reason string in `sessions.ts:650` is **deliberately left unchanged** — it's regex-consumed by `queuedReceipt()` (`/not live/` → `stale_target`) and asserted by API tests, i.e. code depends on it. Touching it would be a semantic change, which is out of scope.
- The federation hint adds one extra in-memory `resolveTarget()` read on the `node:name` peer path (sync, cheap), wrapped in try/catch — never blocks the send.

## How to verify
- `maw hey <offline-or-unlocated-name> "msg"` → `⤷ delivered to <name>'s inbox (not live now) — they'll read it on the next poll` (no failure-sounding text).
- `maw hey <node>:<name> "msg"` where `<name>` is live in a local tmux session → see the `hint:` line; message still goes cross-node (not redirected).
- `maw hey <unknown-node>:<name> "msg"` → error unchanged + hint includes `maw locate <name>`.

## Tests
- `peerLocalOverrideHint`: 3 cases (node:name+local→hint, bare→null, node:name+not-local→null).
- Updated existing assertions: `00-routing-default`, `routing.fixtures.json`, `comm-send-runtime-coverage`, `comm-send-thirteenth-pass-coverage`.
- Full default-safe suite green (**2977 pass, 0 fail**); `bun build` + plugin-coverage-gate green.

author: kody-w
body:
Three Windows-compatibility fixes uncovered while reproducing failed installs. Each is independently verified on Windows 11 / PowerShell 5.1 + Python 3.11.

## 1. Dep check mangled by `Start-Process` (the `SyntaxError` users saw)

`Check-PythonDeps` ran:
```powershell
Start-Process -FilePath $py -ArgumentList "-c", "import flask, flask_cors, requests, dotenv" ...
```
`Start-Process -ArgumentList` joins array elements with spaces but does **not** re-quote an element containing spaces, so python received `-c import flask, flask_cors, requests, dotenv` and `-c` captured only `import` → `SyntaxError: invalid syntax`. It failed even with deps installed (no output redirection, so the traceback leaked) and triggered a redundant reinstall every run.

Fixed with the call operator (quotes args correctly) + local `$ErrorActionPreference='Continue'` so a missing-module stderr isn't promoted to a terminating `NativeCommandError` under the script's global `-EA Stop`. Verified: present → `True`/exit 0, missing → `False`/exit 1, no leak, no crash.

## 2. `Run-PipInstall` breaks on install paths containing a space

Same `Start-Process -ArgumentList` array problem for `-r $reqFile`: a path like `C:\Users\First Last\...` was split and pip failed with "Could not open requirements file". Pass the argument line as a single quoted string instead. Also dropped a stray `| Out-Null` that nulled `$proc` on the `--user` retry. Verified: array form fails on a spaced path, quoted single-string form installs cleanly.

## 3. `UnicodeDecodeError` on non-UTF-8 locales (GBK/Shift-JIS/...)

On a Simplified-Chinese machine the server crashed at startup:
```
File "brainstem.py", line 595, in load_soul
  _soul_cache = f.read().strip()
UnicodeDecodeError: 'gbk' codec can't decode byte 0x94 in position 14
```
`open()` with no `encoding=` uses the system ANSI codepage, but the data files are UTF-8. Added `encoding="utf-8"` to every text `open()` in `brainstem.py` (VERSION, flight-log, token, copilot cache, pending-login, soul.md) and `local_storage.py` (read/write_json, read/write_file — memory agents can hold non-ASCII content). Binary (`'wb'`) and zip (`zf.open`) opens left as-is. Verified: repo `soul.md` reproduces the exact `0x94 @ pos 14` error and decodes cleanly as UTF-8; both modules still compile.

body:
## What
Implements the **sessions subdomain** (`SessionOps`) on the SQLite backend: device authorizations, access tokens (including the single-use agent-enroll consume), refresh tokens, and the user reads.

## Semantics preserved from Postgres
- **Approve / Deny** match only a still-`pending` row (`RETURNING` + zero rows → `ErrNotFound`), so a concurrent resolve loses cleanly.
- **MarkExpired** is conditional but tolerant — a miss (already resolved / unknown id) is a no-op, not an error.
- **ConsumeAgentEnrollToken** spends only an un-consumed `agent_enroll` row and returns `false` on replay or wrong purpose (the single-use guard from issue #6).
- **MarkRefreshTokenRotated** / **RevokeRefreshTokenFamily** are the conditional `:exec` updates.

## Risk
Still **additive** — no wiring. `SessionStore`'s `Begin`/transaction control lands with `AllocationOps` in 6c (since `storage.Tx` embeds both operation sets).

## Test
Contract tests cover the device flow, token consumption, refresh rotation/revocation, and user reads against a real temp-file SQLite database (no external dep → runs in CI).

author: seluj78
body:
**Note:** Claude handled the implementation and prose via back-and-forth. Idea, decisions, and everything else are mine. — @Seluj78

## Description

When GitHub rate-limits the plugin, clicking the pane Refresh action did nothing visible: the worker deliberately degrades to stale data and arms a backoff, but never told the user, so a rate-limited refresh looked like a no-op with no reason.

This wires a user-facing notice. On a user-initiated (forced) refresh that hits an active backoff, the worker raises one `ui.notify` (a warning titled "GitHub rate limited") through a new `notifications` capability. The body shows the reset countdown ("Resets in ~Xm (HH:MM)") when the GraphQL `resetAt` is known, and a generic message for the REST path, which discards the real reset. Detection and de-duplication live in `refresh.py`: a forced `build_snapshot` attaches a one-shot `rate_limit_notice` to the snapshot, claimed at most once per backoff window. Background polls never consume it, so a rate-limited workspace is not nagged on every tick. The notification is global (no session): the rate limit is token/IP-bound, not per-session.

Closes #20

## PR Type

- [x] New Feature
- [ ] Bug Fix
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Infrastructure / CI

## How to test

- [ ] With a token set, trigger a GitHub rate limit (or seed a backoff) and click the pane Refresh action: confirm one warning notification "GitHub rate limited" appears with a "Resets in ~Xm (HH:MM)" countdown.
- [ ] Click Refresh again during the same backoff window: confirm no second notification fires.
- [ ] Let a background poll run during the backoff: confirm no notification fires from the tick.

author: ayyitskevin
body:
## What

Adds a per-symbol **Schaff Trend Cycle** screener (`STC`, aliases `SCHAFF` / `TRENDCYCLE`) — Doug Schaff's 1999 cyclical oscillator.

STC turns earlier than a plain MACD by running a stochastic over the MACD line and then a *second* smoothed stochastic over that, staying bounded in [0, 100]:

```
macd = EMA(close, fast) − EMA(close, slow)
pf   = smooth( stochastic(macd, cycle) )     // first %D
stc  = smooth( stochastic(pf,  cycle) )      // second %D = STC
```

Each `stochastic` rescales its input to 0–100 over the trailing `cycle` window; each `smooth` is an EMA-like pass with factor 0.5 (equivalent to a length-3 EMA), seeded `prev = 0`, carrying the prior raw value forward on a flat window, with a final clamp to [0, 100]. **≥ 75 and rising** flags a strengthening up-cycle, **≤ 25** a down-cycle; crosses of 25 / 75 are the common triggers.

## Verification first

Because the algorithm is doubly chained and recursive (EMA → MACD → stochastic → 0.5-smooth → stochastic → 0.5-smooth), I ran a multi-agent verification workflow **before** implementing:

1. **Derive** — confirm our convention matches the canonical (everget / shayankm Pine) STC: defaults `23/50/10`, factor `0.5` (≡ length-3 EMA), `prev=0` seeding, carry-forward on zero range, output clamp.
2. **Worked example** — an independent agent computes every intermediate (emaFast, emaSlow, macd, pf, stc) for `closes = [1..10]`, `fast=2 / slow=3 / cycle=2 / factor=0.5`.
3. **Adversarial verify** — 3 verifiers recompute from scratch.

All three landed on the same exact final value, **STC = 99.8046875** (max diff 5e-7 = display rounding). That value and the down-trend `STC = 0` are baked in as exact fixtures. The one improvement the spec surfaced — a final `clamp(stc, 0, 100)` — is included.

## How

- **`lib/stc.ts`** — `computeStc` / `stcBoard` / `sortStc`, pure and synchronous. Reuses the shared seeded `emaSeries` for the MACD. Returns `{ stc, prev, dir, zone, n }`; needs ≥ `slow + 2·cycle` closes; null on bad params.
- **`lib/stc.test.ts`** — 9 tests: the exact uptrend micro-example (`99.8046875`), a strict downtrend pinned to `0`, `[0,100]` bounds on an oscillating series, a long ramp reading bull, null guards (thin history, bad params), and board sorting (STC / slope / symbol).
- **`modules/StcModule.tsx`** — sortable board (SYMBOL / STC / Δ / ZONE), 23/50 MACD with a 10 / 23 cycle toggle, bull/bear/mid coloring, click-through navigation.
- 4-point wiring: module `meta`, lazy `registry.tsx`, command `registry.ts` (`STC` / `SCHAFF` / `TRENDCYCLE`), README table — inserted after RWI, before ALERT.

## Verification

- `pnpm -r typecheck` — clean
- `pnpm --filter web test` — 151 files, **1161 tests** pass (9 new)
- `pnpm --filter web build` — succeeds

author: rjwalters
body:
## Summary

Adds **PART 4k** to `proofs/Proofs/PascalsHexagonOQ03.lean` — the **converse** of the PART 4h incidence lemma, completing it to an *iff* that characterizes the **entire** Pascal line as a point set.

Previously the file had only the one-directional `pointOnLine_cross_of_collinear : collinear p q r → pointOnLine r (p ×₃ q)`. That identifies the three known Pascal points `P, Q, R` on the line but says nothing about any other point. This PR closes the gap.

## New theorems (0 new sorry / 0 new axiom)

- **`collinear_of_pointOnLine_cross`** — `pointOnLine r (p ×₃ q) → collinear p q r`. The incidence `r · (p ×₃ q) = 0` is monomial-for-monomial the determinant `det(p, q, r) = 0` (scalar triple product = determinant, by the cyclic symmetry of `det`), so the converse uses the *same* `linear_combination` certificate as the forward lemma — no general-position hypothesis.
- **`pointOnLine_cross_iff_collinear`** — the bundled iff `pointOnLine r (p ×₃ q) ↔ collinear p q r`.
- **`pointOnLine_pascalProjLine_iff_collinear`** — the geometric payoff: a point `r` lies on `pascalProjLine hex` **iff** it is collinear with the two spanning Pascal points `P = AB ∩ DE`, `Q = BC ∩ EF`. This pins down the Pascal line *as a point set* — exactly the locus of points collinear with `P` and `Q` — strengthening PART 4h's three-point incidence to an exhaustive characterization. (Taking `r = R` recovers `pascalR_on_pascalProjLine` via Pascal's theorem.)

## Why it matters

This is the *reasoning-backwards* direction: it lets one conclude collinearity **from** line membership. That is precisely what any future Steiner-20 / Kirkman-60 concurrence argument needs, since a Steiner/Kirkman point is *defined* by lying on several Pascal lines simultaneously (i.e. by collinearity with each line's spanning pair).

## Verification

`./proofs/scripts/docker-build.sh Proofs.PascalsHexagonOQ03` → **Build succeeded (3070 jobs)**. The only remaining `sorry`s are the pre-existing open `steiner_count_eq_20` / `kirkman_count_eq_60` (OQ-03-OQ-03/04). Entry stays `axiomatized` via the parent `conic_implies_pascal_constraint` (used only by `pascalR_on_pascalProjLine`; the PART 4k lemmas are themselves axiom-free).

author: brucearctor
body:
## Summary

Fix JetBrains AI Assistant failing with "unexpected EOF" and HTTP 422 when using the LM Studio provider mode through Candela.

> **Note**: Reapplies #451 which was merged prematurely without CI reviews.

## Root Cause

Two issues in how JetBrains ktor HTTP client interacts with Go net/http:

### 1. Ktor SSE EOF Bug (unexpected EOF)

Go net/http uses chunked transfer encoding for streaming responses. When the handler returns, Go writes the chunked terminator (`0\r\n\r\n`). Ktor SSE parser treats this as "unexpected EOF" even though the stream already sent `data: [DONE]`.

- **Gemini worked accidentally** — Google Frontend keeps the response body open indefinitely, so Go never writes the terminator
- **Claude, Qwen, Mistral all failed** — their upstreams close promptly

**Fix**: Detect ktor via `User-Agent` and hijack the TCP connection (`http.Hijacker`) after the proxy finishes writing. This prevents Go from ever writing the chunked terminator. The connection is held until ktor disconnects or a 30s safety timeout fires. Other clients (curl, Continue, Cursor) are unaffected.

### 2. Request Body Sanitization (HTTP 422)

JetBrains sends extra fields that strict backends reject:
- Empty `tool_calls:[]` on every message (Mistral: "Extra inputs are not permitted")
- LM Studio/Ollama fields: `format`, `keep_alive`, `options`

**Fix**: Strip these fields in `serveChat` before forwarding to the upstream.

## Changes

- **`cmd/candela/lm_handler.go`**: TCP hijack for ktor clients, request body sanitization
- **`cmd/candela/main.go`**: `ModifyResponse` on remoteProxy for SSE header normalization
- **`cmd/candela/sse_normalizer_test.go`**: Tests for renamed `sseLiteNormalizer`
- **`docs/candela.md`**: JetBrains compat details + troubleshooting entries

## Testing

- All pre-commit hooks pass (gofmt, golangci-lint, go-test)
- Manually verified Claude, Qwen, Gemini Flash, Mistral via JetBrains AI Assistant
- curl (non-ktor) clients unaffected

body:
## What

A clean-room pipeline that streams **live battle state out of a running game into a VRChat world**, for a live battle-diorama feature. Built transport-free first, then layered, so the same event source can also feed the spectator-viewport idea. **No Sony bytes** — wire-protocol structure, tooling, and docs only; the actual VRChat world content stays out of the repo.

Three parts:

**Extraction (shared event source)**
- `scripts/pcsx-redux/lib/probe/battle_state.lua` — a transport-free typed `BattleState` reader over the pinned battle globals (actor table, battle ctx, per-monster-id array, render mode), with an `in_battle` presence gate that rejects stale field-state pointers.
- `autorun_battle_state_stream.lua` — a no-breakpoint VSync poll that diffs state and emits newline-delimited JSON (delta on change + periodic and battle-enter full sweeps). Live-validated on a real battle save (resolved the enemy as Gobu Gobu at correct HP).

**MIDI transport**
- `scripts/vrc-diorama/register_schema.toml` — single source of truth; `codegen.py` emits the Lua encoder table + UdonSharp constants, with a `--check` drift gate wired into the pre-commit hook.
- `midi_encoder.lua` — `BattleState` to MSB-first, commit-latched Control-Change messages (delta + full sweep). `midi_sink.lua` — an ALSA `snd-virmidi` device sink (plain write, no FFI) chosen via `LEGAIA_MIDI_DEVICE`.
- `setup-virmidi.sh` / `verify-virmidi.sh` — one-time virtual-port setup and a no-VRChat end-to-end loopback check (sink to virmidi to `aseqdump`), which passes locally.

**Decoder scaffold (VRChat side)**
- `scripts/vrc-diorama/world-project/` — drop-in Unity assets: the UdonSharp `MidiDebugMonitor` (M0 raw monitor) + schema-driven `BattleStateDecoder` + generated `Registers.cs`, with deterministic `.meta` GUIDs and a Windows VCC setup guide.

## Verified

- Offline `luajit` tests: encoder, sink, extraction, and the **encode to decode round-trip** (lossless, including 14-bit wide values and late-joiner reconstruction from a single full sweep).
- The Linux transport loopback (encoder + sink to ALSA seq port) is confirmed with `aseqdump`.
- Codegen drift gate, doc-density gate, and all Lua suites pass. No Rust touched.

## Out of scope / next

The only unproven hop is Wine/Proton to the VRChat client — that requires a Windows host (this dev box is ARM64, which can't run the Unity Editor or the VRChat client). The Unity world build + the live MIDI hop will be a **separate branch of work** done on Windows from the `world-project/` scaffold; the third-party world package and any built Unity project are intentionally **not** committed.

author: mohasarc
body:
## Why

Phase 3 of the stage-1 plan. Provides the visual constants and canvas geometry that the SVG renderer (phase 4) depends on.

## Output preview

`measure()` is not user-facing directly — it is called by the renderer internally. This phase's user-visible output is the `LayoutMetrics` it returns.

Input:
```
.
├── ** src/palette.ts
└── ** src/layout.ts
```
Parsed and passed to `measure(lines, {})`:
```json
{
  "lineHeight": 27,
  "charWidth": 10.8,
  "hPadding": 21,
  "vPadding": 19,
  "canvasWidth": 269,
  "canvasHeight": 173,
  "legendGap": 27
}
```

Full artifact: [`examples/phase-3/measure-output.json`](examples/phase-3/measure-output.json)

Error cases:
- All-blank input → `RenderError('empty tree')`
- Line exceeds `maxLineWidth` → `RenderError('line too wide to render at the current maximum width')`

## Where it lives

```
.
├── ++ src/palette.ts          <-- font/spacing constants + LIGHT/DARK Primer tokens
├── ++ src/layout.ts           <-- measure() function
├── ++ src/layout.test.ts      <-- 7 tests covering all plan-specified cases
└── ++ examples/phase-3/
    └── ++ measure-output.json <-- representative measure() call and result
```

## Public surface

Added:
```typescript
// src/palette.ts
export const FONT_SIZE: number;
export const CHAR_WIDTH: number;
export const LINE_HEIGHT: number;
export const H_PADDING: number;
export const V_PADDING: number;
export const LEGEND_GAP: number;
export const DEFAULT_MAX_LINE_WIDTH: number;
export const LIGHT: { containerFill, pathText, muted, markerAdded, markerChanged, markerMoved, markerRemoved }
export const DARK:  { containerFill, pathText, muted, markerAdded, markerChanged, markerMoved, markerRemoved }

// src/layout.ts
export function measure(lines: ParsedLine[], options: RenderOptions): LayoutMetrics;
```

## Decisions

Chose filtering non-empty lines only for the max-width check (blank lines still count toward `canvasHeight`) over excluding blank lines from height too, because blank lines represent real visual rows in the tree.

author: grhohertz
body:
## Summary

Addresses the three review recommendations for the memory store in `~/.aish/aish.db`: **token usage**, **duration/growth**, and **recall accuracy**.

### 1. Token usage — offloads can't blow up a tool result
- History-compaction transcripts now live in a dedicated `offloads` table instead of co-mingling with curated `memories`, so a routine `recall` can never drag an MB-scale transcript in front of real facts.
- Every `recall` hit is truncated to a ~2 KB cap with an elision marker — a rehydrated transcript can no longer dump a six-figure-token blob into a single tool result.
- Legacy `context-offload` rows are migrated out of `memories` on open (idempotent).

### 2. Duration — the store stays bounded
- Offload transcripts are bounded by a keep-recent (20) + max-age (7-day) reaper run on each write.
- Curated dedup (`organize_memories`) no longer scans transcript bytes (they live in their own table).
- A new FTS5 index backs keyword recall instead of a raw `LIKE` scan.

### 3. Accuracy — most relevant fact leads, not merely the newest
- The long-dormant `embedding` column / `vec_memories` index are now populated (dependency-free local lexical embedder, pluggable for a learned model later) on every `remember`, and backfilled for existing rows on open.
- `recall` generates keyword candidates via FTS5, then re-ranks them by embedding cosine similarity.
- Falls back to a substring scan + recency when FTS5/embeddings are unavailable.

## Recall ergonomics
- New `tag`/query path: `recall(tag="context-offload")` (or query `"context-offload"`) retrieves compacted-conversation transcripts, which are now kept out of normal curated recall.

## Implementation
- New `src/memory.rs` holds the pure, tested helpers (hit truncation, FTS query builder, lexical embedder, retention planning).
- 17 new unit tests.

## Testing
`cargo test --bin aish`: **473 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored**. `cargo clippy` clean for the touched code.

body:
## What is the current behavior?

Tailwind class changes in route files do not properly (hmr) update the tailwind styles.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8513956a-3eb1-4479-af7a-cd943a3e815a

## What is the new behavior?

Tailwind class changes are applied correctly via hmr.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f0b4a52d-5bc8-42a3-850a-51e285d13c34

## What did the removed code do?

Since this PR only removes code, it's fair to ask, what that removed code actually did:

The removed code included a cache optimization for route tree-shake babel transforms. Based on the logic, the cache however didn't reduce the actual amount of babel transforms, it only was used to silence/mute HMR events for unchanged mods via https://github.com/solidjs/solid-start/pull/2171/changes#diff-a43f34f42abb75b93b0894fd3cb7fe15a353a8f62b25d2f03b3dd52c506330ceL329. This logic however resulted in the silencing of HMR events necessary for tailwind to function properly.

Verdict: This three years old logic was introduced in Vinxi via https://github.com/nksaraf/vinxi/commit/975a185b4af08f6a137a339f9fa49b9923caa605#diff-9c9fee025366fdf03d3645a11a19d4444d9afb53a27a4d29fd72bf4f1c2c9309R8 and doesn't seem to provide any advantage these days, that's why I removed it completely. Maybe it was needed for older Vite versions.. I'd love to hear other opinions, especially from @nksaraf / @Brendonovich 😅.

author: martinkrakowski
body:
## What

Revives the three `it.skip`'d tests in `ImportProjectSpecPage.test.tsx` that drive the cloud generation / loose-spec conversion flows.

## The real cause (not what the skip comment claimed)

They were skipped on the premise that **jsdom exposes no readable `body`** ("Response body is empty"). I probed it directly — under **Vitest 4 that's no longer true**: `response.body` is a real `ReadableStream` and `getReader()` works (undici-backed, even in the jsdom env).

The actual blocker is **provider gating**. The page's hooks call `resolveExecutionStrategy(hasLocalLLM, hasCloudKeys)`, which returns `"none"` when no local WebLLM model is loaded **and** no cloud key is present — so the flow errors out (`"No LLM provider available."`) **before any fetch**, and the msw mocks are never reached. `hasServerLLMAccessKey()` reads the build-time `NEXT_PUBLIC_LLM_AVAILABLE` flag (unset in tests).

## How

- **Stub `NEXT_PUBLIC_LLM_AVAILABLE="true"`** in `beforeAll` (unstubbed in `afterAll`) so `"auto"` resolves to `"cloud"` and the existing msw NDJSON stream mocks are exercised. This alone revives 2 of the 3.
- **Delay the `/spec/convert` mock by 60ms** in the loose-spec test so the transient `CONVERTING_LOOSE_SPEC` screen is observable — an instant mock races straight to `SPEC_REVIEW` before `waitFor` can catch it.
- **Replace the stale comment** with the real diagnosis.

No production code changes — this is a test-only fix. (The task was scoped as a possible "node-env integration test"; that split proved unnecessary since streaming already works under jsdom in Vitest 4, so the tests stay as full-page component tests in the existing suite — strictly better coverage.)

## Verification

- `ImportProjectSpecPage.test.tsx`: **12/12** (the 3 were skipped).
- Full `features/manifest-generation` suite: **226/226** across 24 files — confirms the env stub is scoped (`afterAll` unstubs; no cross-file leakage).

author: grovesswg-cloud
body:
## Summary

The Editorial Calibration Sprint hit its first engine bug: the outline stage failed with `Expecting ',' delimiter (char 5355)`, but every stage's failure handler only logged `raw[:400]` — so the actual break point (char 5355) was never visible. Per GPT's directive, the fix is **observability, not a retry mask**: capture the full evidence so the cause becomes inspectable, then fix the confirmed cause with evidence in hand.

## What changed

**`automation/engine_debug.py` (new)** — `parse_stage_json()` replaces the duplicated `try/except → log raw[:400] → raise` boilerplate in all five JSON stages. On a parse failure it writes a self-contained evidence folder:
- `stage.txt`, `prompt.txt` — the stage and the exact prompt sent
- `raw_response.txt` — the model's untouched output
- `repaired.txt` — the exact bytes `json.loads()` choked on (after fence-strip + repair)
- `error.txt` — the parse error and the text around the break point, marked `>><<`

Location is controlled by `ENGINE_DEBUG_DIR` (default `calibration/_failures`; `off` disables). Writing evidence never masks the original error — fail-closed is preserved.

**`automation/json_utils.py`** — `parse_writer_json` now raises `WriterJSONError` (a `ValueError`, fully backward compatible) carrying the raw response, the repaired text, and the `JSONDecodeError` with its exact position. New `repair_json()` exposes the parser's real input.

**`automation/reasoning/llm.py`, `automation/revision/llm.py`** — capture `stop_reason`. A `max_tokens` stop guarantees truncated, invalid JSON, so it warns loudly and names that cause — it must never be mistaken for a malformed-quote bug.

**`automation/generate.py`** — `_make_run_dir` points `ENGINE_DEBUG_DIR` at each run's own `failures/` folder, so a failed generation leaves its evidence beside its other artifacts; the error handler tells the operator where to look.

## Diagnosis (evidence-based, to be confirmed by the next captured artifact)

The first hypothesis — unescaped quotes — was **wrong**: the repair pass already handles those (it sometimes corrupts silently, but does not raise this error). The reproduced cause of this exact `Expecting ',' delimiter` error is a **missing structural comma between objects in an array**, which the repair deliberately never touches. Truncation produces `Unterminated string` instead, so it is ruled out for the reported case. All three reproductions are pinned as tests so they are never re-confused.

The next failed run will now capture the real `raw_response.txt` + `repaired.txt`, which will confirm the cause definitively before any parser change is made.

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest automation/tests/test_engine_debug.py` — 9 tests (evidence capture, disable switch, extra context, the three reproductions)
- [x] Full suite green: 176 passed, 5 subtests
- [x] All engine + revision modules import cleanly (no circular import via `engine_debug`)
- [x] `generate.py` routes `ENGINE_DEBUG_DIR` into the per-run `failures/` folder
- [ ] Re-run the failing calibration generation and inspect the captured `failures/<stage>/` folder

body:
## Summary

Full implementation of Phase 2 — the features that enforce financial discipline. Balance checks, reconciliation math, recurring deductions, per-category budget alerts, cron endpoints, and GitHub Actions workflows are all wired up.

## DB changes (applied to Supabase `nudge` project)

| Change | Detail |
|---|---|
| New table `balance_snapshots` | Stores periodic balance readings with `recorded_at` timestamp |
| New table `recurring_items` | SIP/rent/salary config: `day_of_month`, `direction`, `last_applied_on` |
| New table `reconciliations` | Period-level reconciliation records with discrepancy |
| `users.balance_prompt_sent_at` | Idempotency guard — cron sends at most one prompt per 24 h |
| `categories.budget_80_sent_month` | Deduplication for 80% budget alerts (stored as `"YYYY-MM"`) |
| `categories.budget_100_sent_month` | Deduplication for 100% budget alerts |

## New Python code

### Bot commands
- **`/balance <amount>`** — accepts `48200`, `48k`, `₹48,200`; records snapshot and runs reconciliation against prior snapshot; clears `awaiting_balance`
- **`/budget`** — shows all budgeted categories with MTD spend, a progress bar, and 🚨/⚠️/✅ status

### Balance & reconciliation (`services/balance.py`, `utils/reconciliation.py`)
- `expected_close = opening − logged_expenses − recurring_debits + recurring_credits`
- `discrepancy = expected_close − actual_closing_balance`
- Reports sent via bot: opening, logged total, recurring breakdown, gap or ✅ within ₹100

### Text router (`bot/handlers/text_router.py`)
- Replaces direct `expense_handler` registration; if `awaiting_balance=true` and message is a valid number → balance capture; otherwise → expense classification

### Budget alerts (`bot/handlers/expense.py`)
- After each expense is logged: computes MTD spend vs `monthly_budget`
- Fires ⚠️ at ≥80%, 🚨 at ≥100%; each alert sent at most once per category per calendar month (IST)

### Recurring items (`services/recurring.py`)
- `get_recurring_items_due_today`: matches `day_of_month == today(IST)`, guards via `last_applied_on` month
- Creates `expenses` rows with `source='recurring_debit'` or `'recurring_credit'`
- Bot notifies per applied item

### Cron endpoints (`routers/cron.py`) — `Authorization: Bearer <CRON_SECRET>`
| Endpoint | Schedule |
|---|---|
| `POST /cron/apply-recurring` | Daily 00:05 IST |
| `POST /cron/balance-prompt` | Biweekly (1st & 15th), idempotent |
| `POST /cron/weekly-summary` | Sun 19:00 IST (stub) |
| `POST /cron/monthly-summary` | 1st 09:00 IST (stub) |

### Dashboard API (`routers/dashboard.py`)
- `GET /dashboard/analytics` — stub
- Full CRUD `/dashboard/recurring`
- `GET/PATCH /dashboard/categories` — read categories, set `monthly_budget`

## GitHub Actions workflows

| Workflow | Schedule |
|---|---|
| `keep-warm.yml` | Every 10 min — prevents Render/Supabase sleep |
| `cron-apply-recurring.yml` | `35 18 * * *` UTC (00:05 IST) |
| `cron-balance-prompt.yml` | `30 4 1,15 * *` UTC |
| `cron-weekly-summary.yml` | `30 13 * * 0` UTC |
| `cron-monthly-summary.yml` | `30 3 1 * *` UTC |

Requires GitHub secrets: `APP_URL`, `CRON_SECRET`

## Tests — 20 passing

body:
The sender-/audience-facing messaging surfaces deferred since PR2/PR3b, plus the **agent-primary multicast keying** (operator direction: agent_id is the canonical key; conv-id stays an accepted selector).

## What changed
- **Send receipt → agent_id**: the `recipient` struct gains `AgentID`, populated at all five construction sites (`fanOutToGroup` ×2, `handleMultiRecipient` ×3). The CLI multicast / multi-recipient receipt names each recipient by its short stable agent_id, falling back to the conv-id prefix for a non-agent recipient.
- **Multi-recipient To:/CC inbox list → agent_id**: `recipientLine` (daemon + CLI) gains `AgentID`; `decorateRecipients` / `mailboxDecorator.recipients` resolve it; `formatRecipientList` leads with `name <agt_xxxxxxxx>`.

Shrink-only (never widens reach); an all-blank `members` list reaches nobody (no whole-group fallback); the sender is excluded even if listed; a member named by a now-superseded conv-id still reaches the live successor.

Display resolves conv→agent at render; the receipt resolves in-handler; the durable `from_agent`/`to_agent` columns (PR3a/PR4) already record which generation each send landed on.

## Tests
agent_id-keyed subset; **agent_id survives reincarnation** (the rotation-immune headline); mixed agent_id+conv_id list; receipt carries agent_id; `formatRecipientList` agent_id + conv-fallback cases. Existing subset invariants retested. build / test / lint / gofmt clean.

**Cold review** (fresh agent, diff-only): SHIP — no blockers. Addressed its findings (two stale doc comments, two test-gap fills, one redundant-lookup short-circuit); skipped one cosmetic JSON-tag nit with reason.

## Scope
This is the **CLI/backend** half. The **dashboard Messages-tab + group-message modal** display cutover (and switching the modal to send agent_ids in `members`) lands next as **PR3b-2-web**, mirroring the PR3c/PR3c-web split. author: chubes4
body:
## Summary
The WordPress build extension's theme structure validation (`wordpress/scripts/build/build.sh`) decided block-vs-classic by the **presence of `theme.json`**, then required `templates/index.html` for the "block" branch. That misdetects classic themes that ship a `theme.json`.

A `theme.json` does **not** make a theme a block theme — classic themes legitimately ship one for global styles, color palettes, and font registration (`wp_theme_json_data_theme`) while still rendering via `index.php`. Those classic-themes-with-theme.json got flagged `Essential theme files missing: templates/index.html` and failed the build (exit 1), blocking release — and since the failure is inside the build script, `--skip-build-validation` couldn't rescue it.

## The fix
Detect by the canonical block-theme signal — presence of `templates/index.html` (what WP core's `wp_is_block_theme()` checks) — not `theme.json`:
```bash
if [ -f "$staging_dir/templates/index.html" ]; then
    required_files+=("templates/index.html")
else
    required_files+=("index.php")
fi
```

## Repro (real)
The `extrachill` theme is classic (`index.php`, no `templates/` dir) but its build generates a `theme.json` from design tokens (`cp node_modules/@extrachill/tokens/css/theme.json theme.json`). Staging dir then has `theme.json` → old logic assumes block theme → requires `templates/index.html` → fail. It released fine as v2.6.3 before this validation tightened; now it blocks every release of the theme (and any classic-theme-with-theme.json on the fleet).

## Verify
- `bash -n build.sh` clean.
- A classic theme (index.php + theme.json, no templates/) now validates via the index.php branch.
- A block theme (templates/index.html) still validates via that branch.

Closes Extra-Chill/homeboy#6730

author: miracle778
body: Closes #3836 ## Summary This PR persists security-relevant `GuardrailMiddleware` outcomes as run events. When guardrail intervenes, it writes a `middleware:guardrail` event through the existing `RunJournal.record_middleware()` path. The recorded scope is intentionally narrow: - provider deny; - provider error + fail-closed; - provider error + fail-open; - normal allow decisions are not recorded. The implementation follows the optional-Journal pattern already used by `SkillActivationMiddleware` and `SafetyFinishReasonMiddleware`: read the run-scoped journal from `runtime.context["__run_journal"]`, skip when it is absent, and treat recording failures as non-fatal debug-only errors. ## Motivation `GuardrailMiddleware` changes the actual execution path of tool calls, but these decisions were previously only written to the logger. After a run completes, structured run events could not explain whether a tool call was denied by guardrail or failed during execution, nor whether a provider error resulted in fail-open or fail-closed behavior. By persisting these interventions as run events, operators and developers can use `RunEventStore` to review: - which tool call was denied by guardrail; - which policy / reason code was involved; - whether the provider failed; - whether provider failure allowed or blocked the tool call. Explicit policy denial and fail-closed handling after a provider error both use `action="deny_tool_call"` to represent the same final execution action. `provider_error`, `fail_closed`, `reason_codes`, and `policy_id` distinguish the causes. ## Surface Area - [ ] **Frontend UI** - [ ] **Backend API** - [x] **Agents / LangGraph** - [ ] **Sandbox** - [ ] **Skills** - [ ] **Dependencies** - [ ] **Default behavior change** - [ ] **Docs / tests / CI only** ## Changes ### `GuardrailMiddleware` Adds a private helper: ```python _record_guardrail_event(...) ``` The helper: - reads `__run_journal` from `ToolCallRequest.runtime.context`; - builds a bounded `changes` payload; - calls `journal.record_middleware(tag="guardrail", ...)`; - catches recording failures and logs them at debug level without changing execution behavior. The `changes` payload includes: - `tool_name` - `tool_call_id` - `agent_id` - `is_subagent` - `user_role` - `allow` - `policy_id` - `reason_codes` - `reason_messages` - `fail_closed` - `provider_error` It does not record: - `tool_input` - raw tool arguments - `user_id` - `oauth_provider` - `oauth_id` Each reason message is truncated to 500 characters. ### Applicability Boundary Recording follows the existing `SkillActivationMiddleware` and `SafetyFinishReasonMiddleware` boundary: an event is written only when `runtime.context["__run_journal"]` already exists. - Frontend/API and Message Channel runs execute through Gateway `run_agent()` and are covered. - Embedded `DeerFlowClient`, TUI, and direct `agent.invoke()` execution do not create a `RunJournal` and are not recorded. - Subagents do not inherit the parent run's `__run_journal`; this PR does not add a cross-thread Journal bridge or claim persistence for decisions made inside subagents. `is_subagent` remains an attribution field so the event accurately preserves `GuardrailRequest` context and remains compatible with custom runtimes or a future Journal bridge. Its presence does not imply native subagent Journal propagation. This is not a Guardrail-specific limitation. Lead-agent and subagent executions currently have independent runtime contexts, so any middleware that relies on the lead run's Journal has the same boundary. Defining Journal ownership, lifecycle, cross-thread propagation, and event ordering for subagents is a shared runtime concern that should be designed by the project maintainers rather than solved locally inside `GuardrailMiddleware`. It is explicitly out of scope for this PR. ### Tests Extends `test_guardrail_middleware.py` to cover: - deny records `middleware:guardrail`; - provider error + fail-closed records and denies; - provider error + fail-open records and allows the handler; - normal allow does not record; - payload excludes tool args and user identity fields; - `record_middleware()` failure does not affect denial behavior; - sync and async paths remain aligned. ## Verification Ran: ```bash uv run pytest tests/test_guardrail_middleware.py tests/test_sandbox_audit_middleware.py -q ``` Result: **189 passed.** ## Manual Runtime Validation The implementation is also intended to be exercised against a locally running DeerFlow instance with persistent run-event storage enabled. Validation procedure: 1. Start the DeerFlow Gateway and frontend using the project-supported setup, with a persistent run-event backend configured. 2. Configure a guardrail provider to deny a known tool call such as `bash`. 3. Trigger that tool call from the DeerFlow UI. 4. Confirm that the tool is not executed and that the run contains a `middleware:guardrail` event. 5. Inspect the persisted event and verify `action`, `tool_name`, `is_subagent`, `provider_error`, and `fail_closed`. config.yaml: ``` run_events: backend: db max_trace_content: 10240 track_token_usage: true guardrails: enabled: true fail_closed: true provider: use: deerflow.guardrails.builtin:AllowlistProvider config: denied_tools: - bash ``` Example query when using the DB-backed event store: ```sql sqlite3 -json backend/.deer-flow/data/deerflow.db " SELECT run_id, seq, event_type, content FROM run_events WHERE event_type = 'middleware:guardrail' ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 10;" ``` ### Runtime Behavior ### Persisted Run Event The observed values and screenshots will be added after the local runtime validation and before this PR is submitted. ## Security and Privacy Notes This PR does not persist tool input or raw args, avoiding storage of sensitive content that the guardrail may have blocked. It also does not duplicate `user_id` in middleware content; the event continues to use existing `thread_id` / `run_id` correlation and DeerFlow's ownership/access-control paths. This PR does not change identity semantics across run-event backends. Recording is best-effort and does not change guardrail allow/deny behavior. ## Non-Goals - Do not record every allow decision; - do not add a new `RunJournal` API; - do not change the `RunEventStore` schema; - do not create a new audit subsystem; - do not change guardrail provider decision semantics. - do not add Journal lifecycle or propagation for Embedded/TUI or subagent execution. ## AI Assistance **Tool(s) used:** Claude Code and Codex **How they were used:** The implementation was produced from a reviewed design with Claude Code, then reviewed and refined with Codex. Tests and repository behavior were inspected as part of that review. - [x] I've read and understand every line of this change and take responsibility for it; it is not unreviewed AI output.

author: nightohl
body:
## 요약

1회차만이던 booking 을 **N회차 진행·완료**로. 학생이 회차를 순차로 잡고(직전 회차 **done** 후 다음 열림), 강사가 **일정변경요청**으로 **완전한 대안 슬롯(날짜+이용권+블록)**을 제안→학생이 골라 **사전수락(곧장 결제대기)**, 회차는 강사 마킹/자동(+24h)으로 **완료(done)**. 전체 테스트 green.

## 무엇이 바뀜

**2회차+ 진행**
- `POST /enrollments/{id}/rounds` + `GET .../next-options`. `RoundGate.nextSchedulable` 순차 게이트 — **직전 정규회차 done** 이면 열림, 정규 끝나면 EXTRA. 2회차+는 수강료 없음(부대만).

**강사 일정변경요청 (완전한 슬롯 → 사전수락)**
- `POST /instructor/enrollments/{rid}/propose-slots` — 날짜만 바꾸면 요일(평일↔주말)이 바뀌며 daypart(이용권·입장료·블록)가 달라지므로, 강사가 **이용권·블록까지 정해** 제안(서버 bookable 검증). 위치는 회차 고정(장비 재사용).
- `POST /enrollments/rounds/{rid}/pick-slot` — 학생 선택 → **사전수락 곧장 PAYMENT_PENDING**(입장료 그 daypart 로 재산정).
- 거절은 **1회차만**(진행 중은 일정변경요청).

**회차 완료(done)**
- `doneAt`: 강사 `complete`(회차)·`sessions/{id}/complete`(세션 일괄) + **세션일+24h 자동 sweep**(미마킹 fallback). CONFIRMED 만.

author: axelavl
body:
## Contexto

Problemas reportados desde capturas de la oferta del Banco Central (Especialista en Integraciones de Sistemas SAP) y del sitio en general:

1. **Faltan los títulos profesionales** en Requisitos (solo aparecía *"O carrera profesional afín…"*).
2. **"Cómo postular" no se ajusta al PDF**: mostraba la frase del *llamado* ("Se llama a postulación, hasta el 28 de junio…") en vez de los pasos reales.
3. **Logos institucionales no aparecen** (Banco Central, Codelco, ENAP… caen al ícono genérico).

## Cambios

### Banco Central — títulos profesionales
`pdfplumber` parte un requisito en dos renglones; `extract_requirements` los tomaba como ítems separados y la parte de los títulos se perdía. Nuevo `_unir_lineas_envueltas()` reúne renglones de continuación al bullet al que pertenecen (conservador: solo continúa si el renglón previo no cierra como oración y el actual arranca en minúscula, o el previo terminó en coma).

### Banco Central — "Cómo postular"
- Nuevo `_extraer_pasos_postulacion()`: saca del recuadro de bases los pasos concretos (Formulario de Postulación Online, recepción de antecedentes, adjuntar CV en PDF, expectativas de renta líquida, correo de dudas).
- `construir_oferta` arma la descripción con **saltos de línea** (antes `" | "`) y agrega un bloque `Cómo postular:` con viñetas, para que el front detecte los encabezados y clasifique cada sección.
- **Front (rich-text):** la frase de *llamado a concurso* deja de clasificarse como "Cómo postular" (va a residual); `Cómo postular` / `proceso de postulación` se reconocen como encabezados.

### Logos institucionales
`logo.clearbit.com` fue discontinuado por HubSpot (dic-2025) y era la fuente primaria, por eso casi ningún logo cargaba. Cadena reordenada a fuentes estables: **DuckDuckGo ip3** → **Google s2** → apple-touch-icon/favicon del dominio. Alineado en `shared-shell.js`, `app.js` y `og_image.py` (imágenes de compartir). Caché de logos del cliente invalidado (`v1`→`v2`).

> Nota sobre las flechas de contraer del detalle: ya están implementadas y verificadas en #280 (mergeado). En las capturas se ve "Cómo postular" expandido, que es justamente el estado *previo* a #280 — es propagación de deploy / caché del navegador, no un bug de código.

## Verificación
- `pytest` (bcentral, extraction, og_image) → **123 passed**.
- `node tests/test_rich_text_parser.js` → **64 passed** (incluye llamado→residual y pasos→postulacion).
- End-to-end (scraper → `buildSemanticSections`): "Cómo postular" muestra los 4 pasos reales, separados y sin contaminar Condiciones.
- Proveedores de logos no probables por red (política del entorno bloquea esos hosts con 403); el cambio se apoya en el sunset conocido de Clearbit y en que el repo ya usa DuckDuckGo para logos de cursos.

author: mikemcdougall
body:
## Summary

Pre-release S2 hardening of on-device storage and session handling (#106): SQLite concurrency, token-refresh stampede, the DB-key get-or-create race, and the copy-pasted encryption/connection boilerplate. No merge — a separate agent merges.

## Changes

### SQLITE_BUSY / WAL (AUD-252)
Every connection now sets `PRAGMA busy_timeout=5000` and `journal_mode=WAL`, so a concurrent write (sync vs UI) waits briefly for the lock instead of throwing `SQLITE_BUSY` immediately, and a writer no longer blocks readers. Applied to all stores via the new base (below) plus the HTTP outbox store in its own `OpenAsync`.

### SqliteStoreBase — DRY the encryption/connection boilerplate (AUD-257)
Eight of the nine SQLite stores (`SqliteRecordStore`, `SqliteAssignmentStore`, `SqliteRecordHistoryStore`, `SqliteRelatedRecordStore`, `SqliteLocaleStore`, `SqliteAnswerMemoryStore`, `SqliteAuditStore`, `SqliteSelectiveSyncStore`) now derive from `SqliteStoreBase`, which owns connection-string building, opening, the **fail-closed at-rest-encryption guard**, the concurrency pragmas, and the lazy one-time schema gate. Each store overrides only `CreateSchemaAsync` (its tables/migrations) and `StoreDescription`. This removes ~840 lines of duplicated boilerplate and the risk that one store omits the cipher guard and silently writes plaintext.

> The 9th store (`SqliteHttpOutboxStore`) is intentionally **not** folded into the base in this PR, because its file is already being changed by the open #105 PR (the outbox `LoadDueAsync`/purge work) and rewriting its structure here would collide. It still gets the same `busy_timeout`/WAL pragmas and keeps its existing fail-closed cipher guard; folding it into `SqliteStoreBase` is a trivial follow-up once #105 lands.

### Token-refresh single-flight (AUD-255)
`AuthSessionManager` serializes refresh behind a `SemaphoreSlim` with a double-check: a burst of near-expiry requests triggers exactly one refresh and the waiters reuse the freshly stored session, instead of stampeding the token endpoint and rotating refresh tokens that mutually invalidate into 401s.

### DB-key get-or-create race (AUD-295)
`DbKeyProvider.GetOrCreateKeyAsync` serializes creation behind a static `SemaphoreSlim` and re-checks inside the lock, so two first-launch callers can no longer each generate a key and have the second `SetAsync` overwrite the first — which would orphan the database the first key encrypted and force a silent data-loss reset of unsynced records.

## Tests

- Core **1061 passed / 9 skipped** (warnings-as-errors clean). New coverage: DB opens in WAL mode; 24 concurrent writes don't throw `SQLITE_BUSY`; a burst of concurrent `EnsureValidAsync` calls triggers exactly one refresh. The existing encryption/schema/round-trip suites still pass against the refactored stores, confirming the base-class extraction is behavior-preserving.
- `DbKeyProvider` lives in the MAUI **App** project (`net10.0-android`), which cannot be compiled in this WSL/CI environment (no Android SDK); that change is a localized `SemaphoreSlim` + re-check and needs a build agent with the MAUI workload to compile.

Closes #106

author: santoshakil
body:
when you long press and drag to select, the selection used to stop the moment the grid started auto scrolling, so you could only ever grab about one screen worth.

three separate things broke it. the selection range was only applied when it was fully inside the sliding buffer, so once the buffer moved past the anchor every later tick failed silently. the auto scroll animation makes flutter ignore pointers on the whole grid, so nothing under the moving rows could be hit tested. and the selection sheet swallows the hit test at the bottom edge, which is exactly where the finger sits while holding to scroll.

now each tick asks the service for just the missing chunk of the range (old and new ranges always overlap at the anchor, so its at most one chunk in and one out per tick). the asset under the finger is no longer found with a hit test, it comes from the scroll offset and the segment geometry, with the column read from the laid out row, so it resolves the same during auto scroll and while the finger sits on the sheet or the app bar. the selection also writes once per tick instead of once per asset, which removes the flicker on big selections.

tested with seven widget tests, five fail on main and two pin behavior main already had, and by hand on a pixel 5: edge hold selects through the whole library, holding on the sheet keeps counting in realtime, a day with a single photo gets picked up from any column, direction flip deselects, and scroll feel checked on a release build.

closes #20855
