author: prasrvenkat
body:
First incremental slice of **Ditty** — the project's quality gates, then the determinism foundation the whole engine builds on.

## Toolchain
- pnpm + `mise` (pinned Node/pnpm/just) + `just` as the command surface; ESLint flat config + Prettier; Vitest.
- `tsup` build → **ESM + `.d.ts`** for `@simpllyf/ditty` and `@simpllyf/ditty/core`, plus a minified **IIFE global** (`window.Ditty`) for `<script>` use.
- Strict TS (`noUncheckedIndexedAccess`, `exactOptionalPropertyTypes`, `verbatimModuleSyntax`), `sideEffects: false`, **zero runtime dependencies**.
- CI runs a single `just check`: format-check, lint, typecheck, test, build, zero-dependency guard, and a **<10 KB gzip size budget** (currently **536 B**).
- ESLint blocks `Math.random()` repo-wide — all randomness flows through the seeded `Rng` so output stays reproducible (spec §10).

## `rng.ts`
- mulberry32 `makeRng(seed)` → `next` / `int` / `pick` / `weighted` / `fork`. Same seed → identical stream byte-for-byte; `fork()` derives uncorrelated sub-streams (melody / rhythm / stingers) from one seed.
- **28 tests**: determinism (exact known-answer sequence + seed coercion incl. negative), bounds, `weighted` distribution + invariants (incl. NaN rejection & zero-weight exclusion), `fork` independence + exact one-step consumption, distribution sanity.

## Review
Passed a parallel review panel (correctness/packaging + test-thoroughness). The mulberry32 port was verified faithful to the canonical reference; five determinism-hardening test cases were added from the review before commit.

author: wayuno
body:
The PayPal panel used data-reveal, which defaults to opacity:0 until useReveal's observer adds `.in`. For this panel — mounted dynamically after the "starting checkout" loading state — the observer never fired, so on a normal (non-reduced-motion) browser the whole panel stayed invisible and the page looked blank below the product card.

Drop data-reveal and give the panel its own fade-up entrance animation, so its base opacity is 1 and it can never get stuck hidden (same fix already applied to the manual-verify card).

Reproduced with a harness: an initial-pass [data-reveal] element gets `.in`, but one swapped in after a loading state does not. The fixed panel renders at opacity:1 regardless.

author: cagataycali
body:
## What

The `use_rtps` action-dispatch tests stub `_backend.writer` / `_backend.reader`, so the real get-or-create factories on `_RtpsBackend` (`_participant_obj`, `writer`, `reader`) were never exercised - they sat at 82% with the entire participant/writer/reader construction path uncovered.

This adds four behavioral tests that drive those factories directly by injecting fake `cyclonedds` submodules (`cyclonedds.domain`/`.pub`/`.sub`/`.topic`) into `sys.modules` - cyclonedds is not installed in CI, mirroring the existing injected-fake approach in this suite - and pinning the IDL resolver + topic mangler from the real modules.

## Contract under test

The tests assert the documented backend contract (verbatim from the class docstring): "A single DomainParticipant is shared ... Writers and readers are cached per (topic, type) so repeated publish/echo calls reuse the same DDS entities":

- `_participant_obj()` constructs one `DomainParticipant` and returns the same instance on repeat calls.
- `writer(topic, type)` / `reader(topic, type)` get-or-create and cache per `(topic, type)` - same key reuses the cached entity, a new key builds a new one.
- The `Topic` is built with the ROS-mangled name and the resolved IDL class.
- Writer and reader share the single participant (one presence on the graph).

These are output/identity assertions on the public factory surface, not implementation internals.

## Coverage

`strands_robots/tools/use_rtps.py`: **82% -> 99%** (only the `ImportError` re-raise line remains). No production code changed - test-only.

## Gate

`ruff check` + `ruff format --check` + `mypy strands_robots tests tests_integ` all clean; `tests/tools/test_use_rtps.py` 27 passed.

author: levezze
body:
## Problem

The Stop-hook poll reconciler (shipped 0.14.x) was actively breaking live
worktree agents:
- **143 (SIGTERM)** killed a worker's healthy `--as` poll.
- **400 "not a participant"** on the relaunch, because it omitted `--as` and
  defaulted to `pid-{PID}` ≠ the registered handle.

## Root cause

A legacy worker state file (written by a session that loaded the pre-
`connections:`-block skill) has no `connections:` block, so `declared_connections`
falls through to `parse_worker`. That function **already reads the `poll-label`
line — which already contains `cbc poll <room> --as <handle> --model <m>` — and
threw the flags away**, returning `identity: None`. With identity `None`:
- `poll_command` emits no `--as` → relaunch 400s.
- the reconciler can't distinguish the worker's own poll from the orchestrator's
  poll on the same shared report room → reaps the healthy one (143).

## Fix (code)

`parse_worker` now extracts `--as`/`--model` from the `poll-label` it already
reads, via a shared `flag_value` helper (also used by `parse_connections`).
Identity threads into the `DeclaredConnection`, so:
- relaunch carries `--as <handle>` (no 400), and
- the stale-poll kill is identity-scoped (no 143 friendly-fire).

Both hook entry points heal: the Stop path (`run_stop` → `declared_connections`)
and the SessionStart/compaction path (`run_session_start` → `emit_relaunch` →
`id_of` → `scan_declared`). Per-turn, **no session restart needed** once the
rebuilt binary is installed.

## Fix (skills)

`cbc-worker` and `cbc-orchestrator` SKILL.md:
- **Backfill-on-resume**: if a state file predates the `connections:` block, add
  one before relaunching any poll. This is the only heal path for legacy
  *orchestrator* files (code can't recover their identity).
- **Name the false signals**: exit 144 = SIGURG (process survives); exit 143 on a
  poll task-wrapper is a harness reap, not poll death. Neither warrants a hand-
  relaunch — panic-relaunching on them stacks orphan polls.

## Scope honesty

Heals legacy **worker** files whose `poll-label` carries the full `cbc poll …`
command (e.g. the live mvp-api worker). Does **not** heal:
- **orchestrator** files — `agents:` block has no `--as` to extract (skill nudge
  + fresh session only);
- **bare-label** worker files — need a `connections:` block.

Out of scope: harness reaping all `run_in_background` tasks at turn boundaries
(separate handoff). The reconciler is designed to compensate via per-turn
relaunch and now does so correctly once relaunch carries identity.

## Tests

`cargo test -p cbc` green (137 unit incl. new identity-recovery tests across both
hook paths; 30 + 8 integration). `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and
`cargo clippy -p cbc --all-targets` clean.

Activation after merge: rebuild + `cbc install-skills` to ship the binary and the
updated bundled skills.

author: trialblazer23
body:
## What this fixes

The **"spaCy unavailable (ModuleNotFoundError)"** line you can see on a fresh Codespace, which quietly drops the Archivist to its (smaller) rule-based knowledge graph even though spaCy installed fine.

**Root cause:** spaCy's command-line piece pulls in transitive dependencies (`click`, via `typer`) that some pre-baked container images don't include. So `import spacy` raises `ModuleNotFoundError`, and the Archivist degrades gracefully — but you lose the full graph for no good reason.

## The fix

- New **`.devcontainer/setup.sh`**: installs the package with the `dev,graph,web` extras, then **verifies spaCy can actually `spacy.load('en_core_web_sm')`** — and if it can't, installs `click`/`typer` and re-fetches the model. It prints which graph mode ended up active.
- `devcontainer.json`'s `postCreateCommand` now just runs that script.

If the model genuinely can't be obtained, the system still runs on the rule-based extractor exactly as before — it never fails, it just prefers the full graph when it can.

## Result

A Codespace **created after this merges** gets the full spaCy knowledge graph automatically — no yellow warning, no manual `pip install`. (For an existing Codespace, `pip install click typer` once, or just rebuild the container.)

Verified by running `setup.sh` end-to-end: it reports **"✅ Aletheia is ready — full spaCy knowledge graph active."** Tooling only — no package or test changes.

author: danielsimonjr
body:
💡 What: Replaced expensive `Array.from` usage with manual pre-allocated nested `for` loops in hot numerical paths (`src/numerical/curvature-lowering-helpers.ts` and `src/numerical/weyl-lowering.ts`).

🎯 Why: In V8 (Node.js), converting a TypedArray (like `Float64Array`) to a standard Array using `Array.from()` carries massive allocation overhead. This can significantly degrade performance when used inside tight numerical integration or curvature lowering loops. Pre-allocating manual `for` loops bypasses this overhead entirely.

📊 Impact: Significantly accelerates array shaping and numerical integrations in hot mathematical pathways. Microbenchmarks showed that converting `Float64Array(16)` into nested `number[][]` with a `for` loop is >35x faster than using `Array.from()`.

🔬 Measurement: Run `npm run bench`. Observe improved or steady execution times in operations like the Kretschmann scalar benchmarks, PG metric closures, and GL4 operations. Tests can also be successfully validated via `npm run test`.

## Summary

This fixes how RemoteTerm tells the radio to send messages without a flood scope.

The problem showed up while testing with OpenHop Core, formerly pyMC Core, and is related to openhop-dev/openhop_core#91. body:
Closes #979

Plan: #979

<details><summary>Plan #979</summary>

# Add a `/pr-review-local` command that opens plannotator code review on the active PR

## Summary

Add a warm in-session command, `/pr-review-local`, that opens the plannotator browser
code-review UI on the active worktree's PR — with the GitHub PR URL filled in **implicitly** (no
copy-paste). The end result is identical to running plannotator's `/plannotator-review <pr-url>`.

Because pi exposes **no API for one extension to invoke another extension's slash command**
(`sendUserMessage` sends text to the model; `steer`/`followUp` explicitly *error* on slash
commands), perk cannot literally call `/plannotator-review`. Instead it speaks plannotator's
**published `pi.events` API** — `plannotator:request` with `action: "code-review"` and a `prUrl`
payload — which opens the *exact same* browser UI. This is the same in-process event bus perk
already uses for plan review (`createPlannotatorBridge` in `extension/adapters/planAdapterPlannotator.ts`).

A tiny read-only `perk pr url --json` cold door resolves the active PR's URL from the worktree's
plan-ref branch (GitHub resolution stays canonical in Python).

This is deliberately minimal and forward-looking: when the planned first-party `diffs`-based local
review lands, the same `/pr-review-local` command name can front it.

## Key changes

### Python — new read-only cold door `perk pr url`

- **New file `perk/cli/commands/pr/url_cmd.py`**, mirroring the structure of the sibling
  `perk/cli/commands/pr/review_context_cmd.py`:
  - A `@click.command("url")` named `url_pr` with the `--json` flag and the standard
    `@click.pass_context`, supervisor-surface docstring, and exit codes (`0` ok · `1`
    invalid/no-plan/no-PR/op-failure · `2` not-a-repo).
  - An `_impl(*, repo_root)` that reuses the **exact** active-PR resolution path the existing PR
    workers use: `cache.read_plan_ref(repo_root)` → `launch.resolve_plan_worktree_name(plan_ref)`
    → `github.find_pr_for_branch(branch=..., repo_root=repo_root)`.
  - Error arms via `UserFacingCliError` with the same messages/`error_type` values as
    `review_context_cmd.py`: `no_plan_ref` ("No saved plan in this worktree…") and `no_pr`
    ("No PR found for branch … / Run /submit first.").
  - `--json` success payload: `{"success": true, "error_type": null, "message": null,
    "pr": {"number": <int>, "url": <str>}}`. Failures go through the shared
    `perk.cli.commands.pr.shared.fail(...)` helper (same as the siblings).
  - Human (non-`--json`) render: one `user_output` line like
    `PR url #<n> (<branch>): <url>` via `perk.substrate.output.user_output`.
  - Catch `GitHubError` (→ `error_type="github_error"`) and `UserFacingCliError` exactly as
    `review_context_cmd.py` does.
- **Register it in `perk/cli/commands/pr/__init__.py`:** add `from
  perk.cli.commands.pr.url_cmd import url_pr`, `mark_kind(url_pr, "worker")`, and
  `pr_group.add_command(url_pr)`. Add `url` to the **Workers** list in the module docstring
  (the prose that enumerates `check` / `feedback` / `ready` / … / `review-post`).
- **Parity smoke `tests/test_cli_parity_smoke.py`:** add `("url", ())` to the `"pr"` entry of the
  `EXPECTED_SURFACE` map. The list is alphabetically sorted; `url` sorts **after** `submit`, so it
  is appended at the end of the `"pr"` list.
- **New test `tests/test_pr_url_cmd.py`**, mirroring `tests/test_pr_review_context_cmd.py`:
  invoke the command via Click's `CliRunner` with monkeypatched `cache.read_plan_ref`,
  `launch.resolve_plan_worktree_name`, and `github.find_pr_for_branch`; assert (a) the `--json`
  success shape (`pr.number`/`pr.url`), (b) the `no_plan_ref` arm (exit 1, `error_type`), and
  (c) the `no_pr` arm (exit 1, `error_type`).

### TypeScript — the warm `/pr-review-local` command

- **New file `extension/doors/prReviewLocal.ts`:**
  - `export const PLANNOTATOR_REVIEW_COMMAND = "plannotator-review";`
  - `export function plannotatorPresent(pi: ExtensionAPI): boolean` — returns
    `pi.getCommands().some((c) => c.name === PLANNOTATOR_REVIEW_COMMAND)`. (`getCommands()` returns
    `SlashCommandInfo[]` whose `name` field is the bare command name; this detects that the
    `@plannotator/pi-extension` extension is loaded, independent of the selected plan provider.)
  - A pure, offline-testable bridge:
    `export async function requestPlannotatorCodeReview(bus: PlannotatorBus, opts: { prUrl: string; cwd: string; signal?: AbortSignal }): Promise<CodeReviewOutcome>`.
    Import the **already-exported** `PlannotatorBus` interface from
    `../adapters/planAdapterPlannotator.ts`. It emits **one** `plannotator:request` with
    `{ requestId: randomUUID(), action: "code-review", payload: { prUrl, cwd }, respond }` and
    resolves when plannotator calls `respond(...)`. Unlike the plan-review bridge there is **no
    fast handshake / no `reviewId` channel and no timeout** — for `code-review` plannotator
    `await openCodeReview(...)` and then responds **once with the final result**. Map:
    - `{ status: "handled", result }` → `{ status: "handled", approved: result.approved === true,
      feedback: <trimmed string|undefined>, annotationCount: Array.isArray(result.annotations) ? result.annotations.length : 0 }`
    - `{ status: "unavailable" | "error", error? }` → `{ status: "unavailable"|"error", warning }`
    - honors `signal?.aborted` / `addEventListener("abort", …)` → `{ status: "aborted" }`, mirroring
      the existing bridge.
    Type `CodeReviewOutcome` is a small local discriminated union declared in this file.
  - `function decodePrUrl(payload: ColdJson): { number: number; url: string } | null` using the
    `coldDoor.ts` field helpers (`objectField` + `numberField` + `stringField`), same shape as
    `decodeReady` in `extension/doors/ready.ts`.
  - `export function registerPrReviewLocal(pi: ExtensionAPI): void` registering command
    `pr-review-local` with this handler `(args, ctx)`:
    1. `if (!ctx.hasUI)` → `report(ctx, "pr-review-local", "info", "…requires an interactive
       session (the plannotator browser review needs UI).")` and return.
    2. `if (!plannotatorPresent(pi))` → `report(ctx, "pr-review-local", "info", "…requires the
       @plannotator/pi-extension package (its /plannotator-review command was not found).")` and
       return.
    3. `const r = await runColdDoor<{number; url}>(pi, ctx, ["pr","url","--json"], { label: "perk
       pr url", decode: decodePrUrl })`; on `!r.ok` → `failFor(ctx, "pr-review-local")(r.message,
       r.errorType)` and return (loud-but-soft; the existing error surface).
    4. `report(ctx, "pr-review-local", "info", "Opening plannotator code review for PR #<n> …")`.
    5. Kick the long-running review **in the background** (do not block the session for the whole
       review): `void (async () => { const out = await requestPlannotatorCodeReview(pi.events, {
       prUrl: r.data.url, cwd: ctx.cwd, signal: ctx.signal }); routePrReviewOutcome(pi, ctx, out);
       })();` — mirrors how plannotator's own command handles the decision in a background `.then`.
  - `function routePrReviewOutcome(pi, ctx, out)` — mirror plannotator's slash-command routing:
    - `unavailable` / `error` → `report(ctx, "pr-review-local", "error", out.warning, { alsoLog:
      true })`.
    - `aborted` → no-op (the turn was interrupted).
    - `handled` with `approved` and no `feedback` → `report(ctx, "pr-review-local", "info",
      "Code review approved — no changes requested.")`.
    - `handled` with `feedback` → build `message = feedback + (annotationCount > 0 ? <triage

## Problem

`wrangler pages dev --local` (without `--port`) auto-increments the port when 8787 is already occupied — e.g., from a leftover wrangler process. The deploy script hardcoded port 8787 and timed out waiting for it, causing a `wrangler_dev_timeout` error.

## Changes

1. **`web/package.json`** — Pin dev port: added `--port 8787` to the `npm run dev` script so wrangler consistently binds to the expected port.

2. **`scripts/deploy.py`** — Added `_detect_wrangler_port()` that reads wrangler's stdout/stderr for the `Ready on http://localhost:<port>` line. The deploy script now adapts to whatever port wrangler actually bound to instead of hardcoding 8787. Falls back to a socket check on 8787 if the output pattern isn't found.

## Testing

- `python3 -m py_compile scripts/deploy.py` — syntax OK
- Local deploy now succeeds even if 8787 is occupied

author: shepherdjerred
body:
## What

The **GitHub-native PR babysitter**: comment `@temporal-worker help me get this green` on a PR and a durable bot drives it to *ready to merge* — CI green (ignoring soft Buildkite failures), no merge conflicts (real local merge-tree, never the gh API), no unresolved P3+ review comments — by editing → committing → pushing, escalating to you only on intent conflicts. Owner-only; never merges/closes.

This PR lands **all code phases (0–3) in one PR, dormant** behind `PR_BABYSIT_ENABLED` (default off). Design: `packages/docs/plans/2026-06-27_pr-babysit-bot.md`.

| Phase | What |
|---|---|
| **0** | Pure reusable core (DoD classifiers + loop policy) + I/O activities (deterministic DoD via gh checks + required-check gate, local merge-tree, GraphQL review threads, persistent workdir, mutating `claude -p` iteration, non-force push) + local PoC driver. |
| **1** | Durable `prBabysitWorkflow` on a dedicated `PR_BABYSIT` queue — event-driven (signals: ci/branch/review/main/guidance/stop), reuses the SAME `decideNextAction` as the PoC, human-in-the-loop guidance blocking, budget + stuck guards, `continueAsNew`. 5th worker. |
| **2** | `issue_comment` ingress + owner-only authz + command parser (start/stop/status) + start=`signalWithStart`, stop/status=signal/query, plain reply=guidance; 👍 ack + single marker status comment. Kill switch `PR_BABYSIT_ENABLED` (off). |
| **3** | tofu subscribes `pr_bot` to `issue_comment`; worker env adds the kill switch (off) + handle/login + concurrency cap. |
| 4–5 | **Operational, post-merge** (not PR content): live test on a throwaway PR, then flip `PR_BABYSIT_ENABLED=true`. |

## Dogfood validation
The babysitter was run against **this PR**: it autonomously fixed two Greptile P1s (forked-PR handling, missing-checks-look-green) *and resolved its own review threads*. The run surfaced 8 real issues across the loop (clone retry, askpass ordering, fork handling, missing/partial/fail-open required-check gating, turn budget, workdir refresh) — all fixed.

## Verification
- temporal: `bun run typecheck` ✅, `bun run test` → **655 pass** ✅, `bunx eslint .` ✅, workflow-bundle smoke ✅ (the workflow pulls no I/O imports).
- homelab: typecheck ✅, eslint ✅, 1Password reference linter ✅, `tofu fmt` ✅.

## Safety
Everything is off by default: `PR_BABYSIT_ENABLED=false`, owner-only authz, per-PR concurrency 1 + worker cap, budget (iterations/wall-clock/cost/stuck), graceful + force stop. Merging it activates nothing.

author: mohamedyousalama-ctrl
body:
Adds a **real out-of-band** critical-alert channel — a WhatsApp message to the Kivo admin — so a live failure is seen even with no manager watching the console. The in-console `system_alerts` banner + email scaffold are unchanged; this **adds** a channel.

## Verified state in main (cited)
- `lib/alerts/record.ts` — `recordCriticalAlert` inserts the `system_alerts` row (banner) then calls the email scaffold; result swallowed.
- `lib/alerts/email.ts` — no-op (`provider_not_configured`), no provider wired.
- `lib/messaging/outbound.ts:56` — `sendWhatsAppText({to,text,lastInboundAtMs?,retries?})`: env-gated (`isWhatsAppConfigured`), retry via `retrySend`, and a **24h-window pre-check that is skipped when `lastInboundAtMs` is omitted** (line 72). Returns `sent`/`skipped`(test mode)/`failed`(window or 4xx).
- `lib/messaging/config.ts:52` + `creds-context.ts` — the sender (phone_number_id/token) comes from `readWhatsAppEnv()`: a **per-request override** (webhook sets it per-tenant by inbound phone_number_id) else the **env vars** (`WHATSAPP_PHONE_NUMBER_ID`). `runWithWhatsAppCreds(null, …)` forces the env (no override).

## Proposed send path + recommendation
**(1) Which number SENDS.** There is **no platform/Kivo sender distinct from the tenant number** — a single env-configured WhatsApp number exists (for the pilot, Wesaya's business number). Some alert call-sites run inside a webhook where a per-tenant creds override is active. **Recommendation (implemented):** pin the alert to the **platform/env-configured number** via `runWithWhatsAppCreds(null, …)`, so an alert never sends from whatever tenant override happens to be active. For the pilot this env number is Wesaya's number.
**Flagged tradeoff:** this mixes ops-alerts with the customer business number. The clean post-pilot fix is a **dedicated Kivo platform WhatsApp number** (separate Meta number/app) — provisioning, not pilot-blocking.

**(2) Which number RECEIVES.** `ALERT_WHATSAPP_TO` env var (E.164, no `+`/spaces) — configurable, **not hardcoded**. Unset → clean no-op.

**(3) Template vs session — WhatsApp-window finding.** An alert is **business-initiated** to the admin, so **outside the admin's 24h window Meta rejects free-form text and requires an approved template.** For the pilot this is **NOT a hard blocker**: the admin keeps a thread open by messaging the number (each inbound resets the 24h window), and free-form alerts deliver while it's open. We omit our window pre-check (`lastInboundAtMs` not passed) and let Meta gate the send; a rejection is surfaced to the loud log + the console banner still shows. **Robust follow-up:** an approved alert **template** (Meta approval needed) removes the window dependency — proposed, not built.

## Build
- **`lib/alerts/whatsapp.ts`** — `sendAlertWhatsApp()` reuses `sendWhatsAppText` (existing retry sender; no new dependency). Message: type, restaurant name, detail, conversation id + console link (`NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL`) when present. Gated on `ALERT_WHATSAPP_TO` (no-op `reason:"no_recipient"` when unset).
- **`lib/alerts/record.ts`** — calls it AFTER the unchanged `system_alerts` insert + email scaffold, with a best-effort restaurant-name lookup. **Logs loudly** on a real send failure (per Audit-7 Q3); silent only on the unset no-op. Wrapped so it can never throw into the request path.

## Boundaries (confirmed)
Alert delivery only. No change to what triggers alerts (that's Q2), the `system_alerts` insert/banner, allergen gate, money/COD, or the agent. The alert send is non-blocking and cannot throw into the caller. No new HTTP/provider dependency.

## Verify
- In **this environment** WhatsApp is in test mode (no live creds) → `sendWhatsAppText` returns `status:"skipped"`, so `sendAlertWhatsApp` returns `{sent:false, reason:"skipped:…"}` — logged loudly, request unaffected. A real delivery requires: `ALERT_WHATSAPP_TO` set, live WhatsApp creds, and an open admin window (or a template). Reported exactly as needed — couldn't deliver a live message headlessly here.
- Alert-send failure logs loudly and never breaks the request (try/catch, best-effort).
- `system_alerts` insert + banner unchanged (additive only).
- `tsc` clean; `next build` clean.
- `git merge-base --is-ancestor main HEAD` → TRUE; scope: `record.ts` (+29, 0 deletions) + new `whatsapp.ts`; zero unexpected deletions.

## Env vars to set (launch checklist — Vercel)
- **`ALERT_WHATSAPP_TO`** — admin recipient (Mohamed), E.164 digits (e.g. `2010…`). **Required** to enable the channel.
- **`NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL`** — console base URL (for the conversation link in the message). Optional.
- (Plus the existing live `WHATSAPP_ACCESS_TOKEN`/`WHATSAPP_PHONE_NUMBER_ID`, and keep an admin↔business thread open, or add an approved template.)

Do NOT merge — for review.

body:
## Lever 1, step 2: turn VIX data into edge context for the learned meta-filter

Builds on #20 (VIX internals). Adds a **volatility-regime feature** and threads it into the meta-filter — *without* hand-tuning the deterministic rules (principled: new features go to the OOS-validated learned layer).

### Changes
- **`features/volatility.py`** — causal **as-of (backward) join** of `VIX/VIX9D/VIX3M` onto bars (each bar sees only the most recent VIX print ≤ its timestamp; no lookahead). Produces:
  - `vix_level` — VIX spot
  - `vix_roc` — 1h rate-of-change (rising fear)
  - `vix_term_slope` — `VIX9D/VIX3M − 1`; **> 0 = backwardation = acute near-term stress** (classic high-probability reversal context)
  - Missing series → column omitted (no fabrication).
- **`build_features(internals=…)`** gated on `INTERNALS_VOLATILITY`; new keys added to `SIGNAL_SNAPSHOT_FEATURES` so the meta-filter auto-consumes them (default 0.0 when absent).
- **Threaded the VIX fetch through every runtime path**: scan / chart / backtest service entrypoints, the **meta-filter training** path, and the **live WS poller** (`LiveMonitor.process(internals=…)`).

### Discipline
- Deterministic signal generation is **unchanged** — this is context for the learned, walk-forward-validated layer, not a hand-tuned rule.
- Default `internals=None` everywhere → existing callers/behaviour untouched.

### Verification
- New `tests/unit/test_volatility_features.py` (as-of correctness, term-slope sign, no-fabrication); updated 2 stub engines for the new `scan(internals=…)` kwarg.
- **Full suite green**; ruff clean; **zero new mypy errors** (13 pre-existing).
- **Live**: `vix_level=18.53`, `vix_roc=-0.03`, `vix_term_slope=-0.17` flowing into the AAPL feature frame; `data_completeness=0.65`.

### Next: measure the OOS lift
With VIX now in the meta-filter's feature space, the honest test is a walk-forward Deflated-Sharpe / expectancy before-vs-after. On thin single-symbol intraday data that may be inconclusive — which we'll report truthfully rather than overclaim.

author: brandonscollins
body:
## Why
Very long notes froze or crashed the browser on open (e.g. **ECC Insurance**, 955K chars; the biggest body is 2.4M). Measured against prod data, the cause is entirely **client-side**: the body always mounts the Tiptap/ProseMirror WYSIWYG, which is one `contenteditable` tree of tens of thousands of nodes plus a full markdown re-serialize on every keystroke. Postgres/Neon, Vercel, and the FTS tsvector (~13% of its 1 MiB ceiling even for the 2.4M-char outlier) are all fine.

Brandon wants long read-only notes (PDFs-as-text) as a permanent use, so this builds the long-intended **source/preview toggle** and lets a size gate select it.

## What
- **`BodyEditor`** owns rich/source/preview mode; `ItemEditor` renders it, so every canvas inherits the behavior.
- **`RawMarkdownEditor`** — a plain `<textarea>` of raw markdown (no contenteditable, holds megabytes), available on any note, the only editor for a large body.
- **`MarkdownPreview`** — read-only rendered HTML via new **`POST /api/render-markdown`** (markdown-it stays server-only).
- **Size gate** `LARGE_BODY_THRESHOLD = 100_000` chars (`isLargeBody`, `body.ts`): at/above it the rich editor is **never mounted** — opens in Preview with a banner, Source is the edit path; below it, rich default + a quiet Rich/Source toggle.
- **Size-aware revisions** (`snapshotRevision`): large bodies throttle to 60min/10 snapshots (vs 5min/50) so a multi-MB doc can't balloon Neon storage.

Additive, **no migration**, fully reversible. **CORE** (type+canvas model, body contract) → **Tyler agreed before build**. Full design: **ADR-125** (decisions.md).

## Verification
- `tsc` + `eslint` clean; `next build` clean.
- `scripts/verify-body-modes.mts` **ALL PASS** (threshold/`isLargeBody` boundaries + the markdownToHtml preview path: title-shift, tab-marker flatten, anchor strip, ~520K render).
- Live `/api/render-markdown` exercised in dev-auth preview: 200, tabs flattened, anchors stripped, a 200K-char doc renders.
- **Not yet eyeballed:** the `/items/[id]` canvas UI in-browser — the headless preview won't swap in this route's Suspense content (server returns 200 + 2.1MB; a Next-dev streaming quirk upstream of the change). Needs a real-browser check on this deploy: open ECC Insurance → reading mode banner + "Edit as text"; confirm a normal note still rich with a Rich/Source toggle.

## Follow-ups (out of scope)
- MCP `get_item` still returns full bodies (a 2.4M-char note floods Claude context) — truncate/section there.
- In-app Preview doesn't carry sermon highlight-color CSS (`mark.hl-*`); highlights show browser-default in preview (rich mode unaffected).

author: cdowell-swtr
body:
Prep for the framework repo's default-branch rename **master → main**, closing the last inconsistency with the generated-project template (which already targets `main`).

## What this changes (5 surfaces)
- `ci.yml` / `review.yml` / `docs.yml` / `render-matrix.yml`: `push: branches: [master]` → `[main]`
- `docs.yml`: gh-pages deploy `if: github.ref == refs/heads/master` → `refs/heads/main`
- `CLAUDE.md`: "merge to `master`" → "merge to `main`"

## Why no deadlock
All four workflows trigger on an **unfiltered `pull_request:`** event, so the required checks (`gate`/`build`/`render-complete`) fire on PRs to **any** base — this PR is mergeable, and PRs to `main` post-rename will be too. The `push:` filters + the docs `if` only gate post-merge / gh-pages runs, which would otherwise silently stop firing on `main`. Chose `[main]` (not `[main, master]`) for a clean end state, safe precisely because `pull_request` is unfiltered.

## Sequence (this PR is step 1 of 4)
1. **This PR** — teach workflows/docs about `main` *(here)*
2. Native rename `gh api -X POST .../branches/master/rename -f new_name=main` (auto-retargets open PRs; rewrites ruleset 17579429 — re-verified to resolve to `main`)
3. Local `git branch -m master main` + re-point tracking
4. Operator: dir relocation for git-worktrees + laptop-parity-clone local rename

author: alexdermohr
chaliy
body:
### Motivation

- Production gRPC-backed workers were inheriting a default `None` for the outbound tool-call limiter, allowing outbound tool calls to bypass the per-org rate limit (TM-TOOL-009) that was only enforced for in-process/direct workers.

### Description

- Add a `CheckOutboundToolRateLimit` RPC to the internal worker protocol (`crates/internal-protocol/proto/worker.proto`) to let external workers consult the control-plane rate limiter before executing tools.
- Expose and store the central `OrgRateLimiter` on the gRPC service (`WorkerServiceImpl`) and add a setter `set_org_rate_limiter` so the server startup path can inject the limiter in non-dev mode (`crates/server/src/grpc_service/mod.rs`, `crates/server/src/app_builder.rs`).
- Implement the server-side handler `check_outbound_tool_rate_limit` that delegates to `OrgRateLimiter::check_outbound_tool_call` and fails closed (deny) if the limiter is not configured (`crates/server/src/grpc_service/worker_service_impl.rs`).
- Add `GrpcOutboundToolRateLimiter` on the worker side which calls the new gRPC endpoint and returns `false` on RPC errors, and return that limiter from `GrpcWorkerAdapters::outbound_tool_rate_limiter` so production gRPC workers are gated (`crates/worker/src/grpc_adapters.rs`, `crates/worker/src/grpc_worker_adapters.rs`).

### Testing

- Ran `cargo check -p everruns-worker -p everruns-server` and compilation/checks completed successfully.

- Ran `git diff --check` (style/diff checks) and there were no issues reported.

body:
## Resumo

Três melhorias pedidas: ícones sociais corretos, banner de cookies funcional (LGPD) com registro no painel, e escolha do método de envio de e-mail (SMTP ou Resend).

## 1. Ícones TikTok e Kwai
O lucide-react não tem esses ícones, então o rodapé usava um "fogo" genérico para ambos. Adicionei **SVGs próprios** (`src/components/icons/BrandIcons.tsx`) — TikTok com o logo real e Kwai com o mark de smiley — usados no `Footer`.

## 2. Consentimento de cookies (LGPD) — funcional
Substitui o banner que aparecia **sempre** por um fluxo real:
- Banner com **Aceitar todos**, **Recusar** e **Personalizar**.
- Modal de preferências com categorias: **Necessários** (sempre ativo), **Análise & Desempenho**, **Marketing & Personalização**.
- A escolha é **salva no `localStorage`** (não reaparece a cada carregamento) e **registrada no servidor**.

These 8 are the genuine **verdict bugs**: the vuln_id itself is wrong, so the emitted FrameworkRef points at an unrelated control.

| Rule | was | now | evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ssh-banner` | V-258014 (GUI automount) | **V-257981** | its own stig_id RHEL-09-255025 + CCI-000048 already pointed here (SSH DoD banner) |
| `audit-delete` | V-257869 (mount /var) | **V-258187** | rename/unlink, `-k delete` |
| `audit-xattr-changes` | V-257860 (mount /boot) | **V-258179** | setxattr — 5-syscall exact match |

| `audit-perm-mod` | V-257852 (prevent code exec) | **V-258177** | chmod/fchmod, `-k perm_mod` |

| `etc-shadow-permissions` rhel8 | V-230256 (not in source) | **removed** | RHEL 8 STIG V2R7 has no /etc/shadow perm control |

Correct controls now covered; the wrong mount/DoS/automount controls these rules falsely claimed are released. Re-baselined; drift gate green. Consistency sweep 122→114.

author: criztiano
body:
Follow-ups to the Curve Composer (PR #4), in the requested priority order: direction-aware triggers first, then tests, a shared-core refactor, and the Svelte/Solid/Vue ports.

## What changed
- **Direction-symmetric triggers** (priority): `triggersCrossed` now reads the value sequence direction-agnostically — interior levels fire whichever way the value travels, and a flyback (segment/loop boundary) fires the far endpoint the walk flew back from (top on a forward reset, floor on a reverse one). Works under `direction: forward | mirror | reverse`; the old forward-only caveat is gone.
- **Core unit tests** (vitest): 39 tests over the pure core — direction-symmetric triggers (ascending/descending/flyback, no edge double-fire, overshoot clamp, on-level convention), and **through the real read/trigger pipeline**: multi-segment forward, reverse (count-equality), **mirror** (both legs, no spurious endpoint at the smooth peak), **spring** (no phantom from overshoot), and a **non-linear driver** re-pacing trigger timing. Plus deriveEase/steepness/energy, spring overshoot, the per-segment walk, geometry, weight redistribution, and state transitions.
- **Shared interaction core + barrel trim**: lifted pointer resolution + drag math out of the React wrapper into `curve-composer-core` (`pointerTarget`, `applySegmentBodyDrag`, `applyDriverBodyDrag`, `toLocalCoords`, gains) so the ports don't triplicate it; dropped the internal-only `directionPhase` export.
- **Svelte / Solid / Vue ports**: each renders the same SVG, runs the rAF playhead with direct per-frame DOM writes, and wires the full pointer pipeline by consuming the shared core. Behaviour mirrors React, including the direction-symmetric triggers and the phantom-trigger re-arm guard. Exported from each framework barrel with matching prop/type surface.

## Review-and-fix
Ran a 6-agent review (simplicity, TypeScript, architecture, performance, frontend-races, test-quality) focused on the ports. Fixed:
- **Vue**: replaced an async `watch`-based trigger re-arm with an inline geometry-snapshot check in the rAF tick (atomic with the read; matches the other ports) — closes a window where a mid-playback geometry change could phantom-fire a trigger.
- **Solid**: memoized `mainRect`/`driverRect` so the loop reads a cached object instead of allocating a `Rect` every frame.
- **Tests**: added the mirror/spring/driver pipeline cases above and the on-level convention; tightened the reverse case.
- A flagged Svelte "stale props" race was investigated and **dismissed as a false positive** — Svelte 5 prop reads inside closures are live (verified against the shipped `WaveformVisualization` getter pattern).

## How to verify
- `npm test` (48 pass), `npm run typecheck` (React/Solid/Vue + svelte-check — only the pre-existing `DialRoot` error), `npm run build`.
- React showcase: `npm --prefix example run dev` → http://localhost:3000/library §09 (energy/steepness drag, Trigger mode with a non-linear curve, driver, Direction — try **mirror/reverse** in Trigger mode now).

## Verification gap (please note)
The React changes are live-verified. The **three ports are typecheck + build + unit-contract verified and adversarially reviewed, but NOT visually/live-verified** — there's no non-React example harness in the repo. They're faithful translations of the live-verified React reference over the unit-tested shared core. Standing up minimal per-framework example pages for visual QA is a sensible follow-up.

## Deferred (non-blocking, from the review)
- **Lift the duplicated geometry/layout/`curvePath`/cursor layer** from all four wrappers into the core — a real DRY win, but a large multi-file refactor better done as its own focused change.
- **Core-helper re-export asymmetry**: the root barrel re-exports the composition helpers; the ports don't (mirrors the existing WaveformVisualization precedent). An API call to make deliberately — unify one way or the other.
- Minor: a11y parity (only the Svelte port sets `role`/`aria-label`), Vue prop JSDoc depth, two unused `CompositionRead` fields.

## Risks / rollback
- Additive: one new component per framework + core helpers + tests. The `triggersCrossed` rewrite is the one behavior change to existing React, covered by the new tests and live-verified. Rollback: revert the merge; no data/schema/migration involved.

author: aisraelov
body:
## Summary

Diagnosed from incident `123e9171-b09d-4d00-8c21-9902dec82b4e` (Recorder local miniapp, `com.mentra.recorder`). Three symptoms were reported; this PR fixes the two that are genuine code bugs and documents the third (which is working as designed).

### ✅ Fix 1 — shared recording had no file extension (host-side)
`BlobStore` stores each blob on disk under a generated, **extension-less** id (the `name`/`mimeType` live only in metadata). `react-native-share` derives the shared file's name from the `file://` URL's path — its `filename` option only applies to base64/`data:` payloads, not file URLs — so the recipient got an extension-less file (`recording…` with no `.wav`).

`handleShare` now copies the blob into a short-lived cache file that carries the real display name **with extension** (derived from the `mimeType` when the stored name lacks one), shares that, then deletes it in `finally`. Fixes the symptom for **every** blob type. Ships with the app build — no miniapp bundle rebuild needed.

### ✅ Fix 2 — `speaker.play()` / `speak()` timed out mid-playback (bundled SDK)
The miniapp `play()` promise rejected with `ACTION_TIMEOUT` ~60s into a long clip:
```
[com.mentra.recorder] "Recorder: playback failed", {"code":"ACTION_TIMEOUT", ...}
```
The host only sends its `REQUEST_RESULT` when playback **finishes or is interrupted**, but `sendRequest` applied the default 60s ceiling. These inherently long-running requests now opt out (`sendRequest` gains an optional `timeoutMs`; `0` disables the timer). They still settle via the host result, `stop()`, or disconnect (`failAllPending`). Applied to `play()` and `speak()`.

This code lives in `@mentra/miniapp`, which is **bundled into each local miniapp**, so the Recorder bundle is rebuilt + re-embedded for it to take effect (see Rollout).

### ℹ️ Symptom 3 — "playback is silent" → working as designed (not changed)
The logs show playback **loaded and played** for the full clip (11s / 13s / 4.5s runs, zero decode errors — never the `player went idle` failure path), and the visualizer bars are computed from the exact bytes written to the blob, so the WAV genuinely contains audio. With Mentra Live connected, iOS routes `.playback`-category audio to the **glasses A2DP speaker** (every play reads/manages glasses media volume; see `BLOCK_AUDIO_DUPLEX` in `MentraLive.swift`). So the audio came out of the glasses, not the phone. **Confirm:** disconnect Mentra Live and replay → audio plays from the phone.

Forcing phone-speaker output isn't reachable from expo-audio's JS API and needs native `AVAudioSession` changes that entangle with the LC3 mic path and re-route audio for **all** miniapp audio/TTS — a deliberate product decision proposed as an opt-in (`PlayAudioOptions.output`) follow-up rather than bundled here.

## Rollout — Recorder bundle rebuilt
Because Fix 2 is bundled into the miniapp, I rebuilt the Recorder against the patched SDK and re-embedded it:
- `miniapp.json` `1.0.0 → 1.0.1` — `MantleManager.installBundledMiniapps()` skips a bundle when that exact version is already installed (`MantleManager.ts:435`), so the version **must** change for existing installs to pick up the new bundle.
- Repacked `mobile/assets/miniapps/com.mentra.recorder-1.0.1.zip` (replaces `-1.0.0.zip`), verified the packed `background/index.js` contains the `timeoutMs` fix.
- Regenerated `mobile/src/generated/bundledMiniapps.ts`.

Other local miniapps that bundle the SDK (captions, translation, navigation, teleprompter, merge) will pick up the timeout fix on their next routine rebuild; none was in this incident and none does long-running `speaker.play`, so they're intentionally left as-is here.

## Changes
- `miniapp/session.ts` — `sendRequest` accepts `{timeoutMs?}`; `0` disables the timeout.
- `miniapp/modules/speaker.ts` — `play()`/`speak()` pass `timeoutMs: 0`.
- `island/services/BlobStore.ts` — `handleShare` shares a properly-named temp copy.
- `island/services/blobPaths.ts` — new pure `shareFileName` / `extForMime` helpers.
- `island/services/blobPaths.test.ts` — unit coverage.
- `miniapps/recorder/miniapp.json` + `mobile/assets/miniapps/*` + `bundledMiniapps.ts` — rebuilt/re-embedded bundle.

## Test
`bun test src/services/blobPaths.test.ts` → 11 pass; Recorder `wav.test.ts` still green. SDK + Recorder bundles built clean; packed zip verified to contain the fix. Full mobile typecheck/tests run in CI.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes blob share I/O and SDK request-timeout semantics for audio; scoped helpers and tests limit blast radius, but other miniapps only get the timeout fix on their next rebuild.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes two Recorder-related bugs: **shared blobs arrived without a file extension**, and **long `speaker.play()` / `speak()` calls failed with `ACTION_TIMEOUT`**.
> 
> **Blob sharing (host):** `BlobStore.handleShare` no longer shares the internal extension-less blob path directly. It builds a display filename via new `shareFileName` / `extForMime` helpers in `blobPaths.ts`, copies the blob into a unique cache subdir under that name, opens the OS share sheet on the copy, and deletes the temp dir in `finally`. This works around `react-native-share` ignoring the `filename` option for `file://` URLs.
> 
> **Miniapp SDK:** `MiniappSession.sendRequest` accepts optional `{ timeoutMs }`; `0` skips the 60s timer so promises that only resolve when playback finishes do not reject mid-clip. `SpeakerModule.play()` and `speak()` pass `timeoutMs: 0`.
> 
> **Rollout:** Recorder is bumped to **1.0.1** and the embedded bundle in `bundledMiniapps.ts` is updated so installs pick up the SDK change.
>

author: amiller68
body:
## Problem

`confit run`/`show` take a **single** section, but a working dev env spans several (secrets in `credentials.app`, datastore URLs in `accessories.*`, plus literals). And an agent's shell tool runs each command in a fresh process — env vars don't persist and interactive 1Password approval can't be driven per-call. So an agent can't realistically chain `migrate → seed → server` without re-unlocking each time.

## What this adds

**`confit export`** — a first-class verb that materializes a complete env **once** (one provider/1Password unlock) into a safe file you can source repeatedly:

```
confit export [--profile <name> | <SECTION>...] [OPTIONS]
```

- Composes **multiple sections** (later wins on conflict) or a named **`[env.<name>]` profile**, drawing from sections/providers/**sources**/literals.
- `-o/--out` writes **`0600`**, **atomically** (temp+rename), and **refuses non-gitignored paths** (checked via `git check-ignore`) unless `--force`; warns and proceeds outside a git repo.
- `--format dotenv|shell|json` — all shell-safe single-quoted.
- `--reveal` **required** to emit secret values (refuses rather than write masked junk). With `--out`, secrets go **only to the file**; a keys-only summary prints to stderr — nothing secret in the agent transcript.
- **Fails closed**: nonzero exit and no file written if any value can't resolve.
- `--upper` / `--prefix` / `--no-eval` carried over from `show`.

**`[env.<name>]` profiles** — declare a named env once in config. Profiles can pin their own vars with dotted keys (`vars.stage = "development"`), with precedence `[vars] < profile vars < CONFIT_VAR_* < --set`.

## Composes with `[sources]` (not a duplicate)

Built on top of v0.3.0's sources feature: a profile key can reference `bag://FIELD`, and `export` shares a single `SourceCache` across all sections, so a bulk source bag **loads once** for the whole export — exactly what sources are for. `secret = true` sources flow through the `--reveal` gate correctly.

## Example (agent workflow)

```bash
# once — human approves the single unlock
confit --set stage=development export --profile dev --reveal --out web/py/.env.dev
# thereafter — any fresh shell, no re-auth
set -a; . web/py/.env.dev; set +a
```

## Tests / checks

- 70 CLI integration tests (16 new, incl. profile↔sources composition, gitignore guard, 0600/atomic write, reveal gating, dotenv/shell/json, pinned-vars precedence).
- `cargo test` (core + cli), `clippy --all-targets`, `cargo fmt --check` all clean.
- Wiki builds clean; new **Env Profiles** page + `export` docs.

## Notes

- Pure addition — no changes to existing `resolve`/`show`/`run`/`sources` behavior; no naming collisions with upstream.
- The optional session-cache idea from the original ticket (part C) was intentionally **dropped** — the materialized file serves that role.

author: rhoulihan
body:
## Phase 1 — Core routing proxy + CLI

Implements Phase 1 of the [design spec](docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-27-agentfactory-design.md): the core that proves the whole mechanism end-to-end. A Claude Code orchestrator (Anthropic) dispatches local-model subagents that do grunt-work code generation; the Anthropic parent orchestrates and reviews.

### How it works
All model traffic flows through one Anthropic-Messages-API proxy that **routes by the request's `model` field**:
- `claude-*` → passthrough to `api.anthropic.com` (orchestrator + reviewers stay frontier)
- `local/*` → translate Anthropic↔OpenAI and forward to a local vLLM (OpenAI-compatible) backend, then translate back — including SSE streaming.

A "local subagent" is therefore just an ordinary `.claude/agents/*.md` whose `model:` is a registered `local/*` alias. **Core invariant:** local models only generate; all review/verification stays on the Anthropic parent.

### What's included
- **Routing proxy** (`proxy.py`): `/v1/messages` (streaming + non-streaming), `/v1/models` discovery, `/healthz`.
- **Hand-rolled translation** (`translate.py`, `streaming.py`): Anthropic↔OpenAI request/response mapping and an SSE re-framer, including the load-bearing `tool_use`↔`tool_calls` round trip with streamed tool-argument deltas.
- **Backends** (`backends.py`): the only outbound-HTTP module — passthrough + OpenAI backend, streaming + non-streaming.
- **Config registry** (`config.py`, `factory.example.yaml`): `local/*` aliases → backends; local NVIDIA box and remote Ubuntu host are the same abstraction.
- **CLI** (`cli.py`): `factory up/down/status/doctor`, with a live tool-call smoke test.
- **`local-coder` template** + worktree-review docs.

### Quality
- Built with TDD, **13 tasks**, each adversarially reviewed (independent suite re-run + spec check) — all passed first try.
- Whole-branch review surfaced one binding-constraint gap (guided-decoding `tool_choice` enforcement); fixed with a covering test (commit `a8bcf02`).
- **37 tests passing.** Deferred Minors tracked in [`docs/phase2-backlog.md`](docs/phase2-backlog.md).

### Not in this PR (later phases)
`factory install`/`models`/`report`, worktree merge helper, tool-call repair, observability/cost split (Phase 2); docker-compose, LM Studio native path, reviewer-subagent panel, ReAct fallback (Phase 3).

## Why

The Gemini pipeline is now live and healthy (answers flowing, backlog dropping). But a URL-quality check on freshly-written answers found **~179 of 290 still carried opaque `vertexaisearch…/grounding-api-redirect` stubs** — `resolveRedirectUrl` was failing in the edge runtime because Gemini's grounding redirect **403s a bare HEAD request**, so the stub was kept as-is.

Gemini's own *stated* source URLs are exactly the deep links we want (specific bills, league scorecards, even PDFs with `#:~:text=` anchors to the precise line). The unresolved redirect stubs were pure noise.

## What changed (`_shared/gemini-research.ts` only)

- **`resolveRedirectUrl`** — now uses **GET + a browser User-Agent** (and a longer timeout); if the HTTP redirect chain still doesn't resolve, it parses the destination from a meta-refresh/anchor in the response body.

author: seanbuckley
body:
## Summary

Security response headers for **both** hosts, a CSP designed not to break as the site grows, and two drift guards.

> **Stacked on #462.** This PR targets the `claude/fix-prettier-config` branch so its diff is security-only. The formatting/config fix lives in **#462** and should merge first; GitHub will retarget this PR to `master` automatically once #462 merges.

### Security headers — Cloudflare + Vercel
- **`public/_headers`** (Cloudflare Pages) and **`vercel.json`** (Vercel) carry the same set: `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `Referrer-Policy`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, a restrictive `Permissions-Policy`, conservative `HSTS`, and a **Content-Security-Policy**.
- The CSP is **forward-compatible** (pages + JS frameworks are planned):
  - `script-src 'self'` stays strict — the real XSS surface. Astro bundles React/Svelte/etc. islands as same-origin module scripts, so `'self'` covers them; a *third-party* script would need its origin added (the guard below catches that).
  - `img-src`/`style-src`/`font-src` allow `https:`/`data:` so new images, web fonts, and inline styles don't silently break.
  - `connect-src 'self'`, `form-action 'self' https://formspree.io`, plus `frame-ancestors`/`base-uri`/`object-src` lockdowns.

### Drift guards (Playwright)
- **CSP guard** — applies the real policy from `_headers` to each page and fails if the browser reports any violation. *Verified it fails on a real violation.*
- **Host parity guard** — asserts `vercel.json` and `public/_headers` carry identical security headers. *Verified it fails on a deliberate drift.*

## Verification

- `astro check` → 0 / 0 / 0
- `prettier --check .` → clean
- `astro build` → `dist/_headers` emitted; `vercel.json` at root
- Playwright → 18/18 (15 prior + CSP guard ×2 + host-parity); both guards confirmed to fail on real drift

## Notes

- **HSTS** is conservative (`max-age=31536000`, no `includeSubDomains`/`preload`) — strengthen once every `*.buckley.ca` subdomain is confirmed HTTPS-only.
- Couldn't live-verify headers on the previews (the agent proxy blocks outbound to `pages.dev`/`vercel.app`); validated by auditing built resources + the automated guards.

author: yeremivr
body:
## Problema
El workflow `Frontend CI/CD` (`frontend-cicd.yml`) rompía en cada push a `develop`:

```
Run curl -X POST
curl: (2) no URL specified
Error: Process completed with exit code 2.
```

El job `deploy-dev` hacía `curl -X POST ${{ secrets.RENDER_FRONTEND_DEV_HOOK }}` con el secret **vacío** (Render hook no configurado) → curl sin URL → exit 2 → pipeline rojo. A diferencia de `deploy.yml` (que se dispara por `workflow_run` desde la rama por defecto `main`, donde no existe), este workflow despliega en el **push directo a develop**, así que sí se ejecutaba.

## Fix
- Nuevo job `config` que expone `has_dev_hook`/`has_prod_hook` desde los secrets (no se pueden usar secrets en `if:` de job).
- `deploy-dev` / `deploy-prod` corren **solo si su hook existe**. Si no, se **saltan** (y como `smoke-test`/`deploy-prod` dependen de ellos, también se saltan) → pipeline en **verde** sin hooks, y plenamente funcional el día que configures los deploy-hooks en Render.
- `curl` endurecido (`-fsS`, URL citada).

No cambia comportamiento cuando los hooks SÍ estén configurados.

author: randileeharper
body:
## Summary

Closes #45.

The adaptive-session worker start/stop logic was duplicated across transports: the A2A HTTP lifespan, the standalone MCP lifespan, and a dedicated `_embedded_mcp_lifespan` whose only purpose was to *not* stop the worker when MCP was mounted under the parent HTTP app. This made it easy to leak a worker, stop it too early, or leave it off entirely.

## Changes

- Introduce an `Application` object in `vesper/app.py` that owns the worker lifecycle in exactly one place via `worker_lifespan()`.
- Both the HTTP app lifespan (used by `cli serve` for A2A-only, MCP-only, and combined) and the standalone MCP stdio lifespan now compose this single context manager instead of calling `service.start/stop_background_session_worker` directly.
- The `_embedded_mcp_lifespan` workaround is retained but its comment now points to `Application.worker_lifespan` as the single owner of the lifecycle.
- One-shot CLI commands remain unchanged: they never start the worker, and `service.close()` drains it as a teardown safety net.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Worker start/stop logic exists in exactly one place (`Application.worker_lifespan`).
- [x] All three transports (CLI serve, A2A, MCP) behave consistently — they compose the same lifespan.
- [x] Tests verify worker does not run after shutdown in all modes (parametrized over HTTP transport combinations + standalone MCP).

author: kraulerson
body:
## Summary

Fixes audit finding `specs-plans-bl029-bl030-5` on `scripts/hooks/record-claude-commit.sh`. Same defect class as BL-020 on the sister hook `scripts/pre-commit-gate.sh` (fixed in PR #53).

**Defect 1 — naive substring match (line ~37):**

```sh
case "$CMD" in *"git commit"*) ;; *) exit 0 ;; esac
```

False-positives on innocuous commands whose argv contains the literal string `git commit`: `echo "see git commit later"`, `cat scripts/pre-commit-gate.sh | grep "git commit"`, `rg "git commit" docs/`. Each false-positive polluted `.claude/claude-commits.jsonl` with a spurious entry mapped to whatever HEAD happened to be — which the out-of-band detector then trusted as a Claude-issued commit.

**Fix — verbatim copy of `scripts/pre-commit-gate.sh:81-93` (the BL-020 precedent):**

```sh
_is_git_commit() {
  echo "$1" | grep -qE '(^|[^"'"'"'])git[[:space:]]+commit\b'
}
```

`commit` must come immediately after `git` (whitespace-separated); `git` must NOT be preceded by a quote. Start-of-line is allowed; chained `cd /foo && git commit ...` still matches because `git` is preceded by whitespace.

**Defect 2 — `git commit --amend` not handled (line ~44):**

`SHA=$(... && git rev-parse HEAD)` captures HEAD after-the-fact. After `--amend`, HEAD has a new SHA, leaving the original ledger entry pointing at a now-orphan SHA while the new SHA is unrecorded — the out-of-band detector then flags the amended SHA as user-terminal.

**Fix — option C (record amended commits as a fresh entry):**

No special-casing in the hook. The normal flow records the amended commit under its new HEAD SHA. The pre-amend entry persists harmlessly as an orphan SHA in the append-only ledger. The out-of-band detector matches against ledger membership, so the amended SHA is correctly classified as Claude-issued. Options A (skip the hook on --amend, leaves the amended SHA undetected) and B (rewrite the prior entry, requires fragile commit-message matching) were rejected.

## Test plan

- [x] `bash tests/test-record-claude-commit.sh` — **9/9** (T1-T5 unchanged; T6-T9 new)
  - T6: `cat ... | grep "git commit"` (quote-preceded false-positive) — NOT recorded
  - T7: `rg "git commit" docs/` (search-string false-positive) — NOT recorded
  - T8: `cd $TMP && git commit ...` (chained happy path) — recorded
  - T9: `git commit --amend --no-edit` (option C semantics) — recorded as fresh entry, original entry preserved
- [x] `bash tests/test-pre-commit-gate-classifier.sh` — **6/6** (sister suite, unaffected)
- [x] `bash tests/test-out-of-band-detector.sh` — **8/8** (ledger consumer, unaffected by entry shape)
- [x] `bash tests/test-bl030-calibration-replay.sh` — **4/4** (calibration replay)

## Backlog

Closure note added to `solo-orchestrator-backlog.md` under the BL-030 section's existing "Audit follow-up" pattern (parallel to the `specs-plans-bl029-bl030-3` closure).

## Summary

The deploy-confidence core of #573: `npm run qa:dev` drives the **real** Haven money-movement path on **Base Sepolia** against the shared dev backend, using the seeded QA identity (#574), and asserts the #420 invariants — no LLM, fixed inputs, asserted outputs, non-zero exit on failure. | Scenario | #420 invariant | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `over-budget-queue` | over-allowance payment is queued (`pending_approval`), never auto-executed | ✅ **PASS live** |

body:
More audited fixes across reported areas.

**Content Calendar** — "doesn't show today vs tomorrow." Root cause was a timezone bug: items were bucketed by their **UTC** date but Today/Tomorrow was judged in **local** time, so posts near midnight landed on the wrong day. Now bucketed by local day to match the labels.

**CRM** — the Add-contact form silently forced **every** manual contact to `kind="recruiter"` (no selector, recruiter default). Now defaults to `contact` and has a **kind selector** (contact/recruiter/partner/advisor/client) so people aren't mislabeled.

**Jobs** — "LinkedIn/Indeed not showing; list empty." Two fixes:
- The list could go **silently empty** because free-board roles often score below the 75% bar and were dropped. It now falls back to the **best-scoring roles** so the list always populates when sources return jobs.
- **LinkedIn/Indeed/Glassdoor** require a JSearch key — that (and **Twilio** for SMS) can now be **connected in-app** on *Connect Email & Data*, and `/setup` reports their status. No key → free remote boards still populate the list.

(Connector key-naming audit: most inconsistencies are load-bearing keys read by integrations + stored in connections — renaming would break existing connections — so deferred; it's cosmetic.)

body: ## Summary This draft PR collects surgical memory-safety fixes in netdata and closely related C code. Each fix is intended to be one verified issue per commit, with no intended functional change beyond avoiding undefined behavior or invalid memory access. The branch will continue to receive small commits as additional scout findings are independently verified, externally reviewed, validated locally, and accepted as deterministic zero-functional-impact fixes. ## Validation Validation is recorded per commit/finding. Current local validation includes focused builds for affected targets and same-pattern scans where applicable. ## Review Scope This is intentionally draft while the remaining scout findings are triaged. Findings that require design, behavior, or risk-acceptance decisions will not be silently changed; they will be collected for discussion. --- ## Summary by cubic Harden memory safety, file I/O, time arithmetic, and concurrency across the Agent with no behavior changes. Fixes racy ACLK/streaming/MCP state, validates persistence paths, prevents overflows, and corrects OpenAPI/docs. - **Bug Fixes** - ACLK: make runtime‑ban, disconnect mailbox (atomic exchange), session generation, diagnostic scalars, and node‑send timestamps atomic; publish new claim state before reconnect; release OpenSSL private‑key decoder/BIO state on retry. - Persistence/I/O: validate regular files and predictable temps for Status/Dedup and Registry DB/log; MCP API key opens are nonblocking; DynCfg rejects short/error payloads; bearer tokens publish complete immutable entries and check fwrite/ferror/fclose; spawn popen callers handle NULL streams. - MCP: take the function‑registry entry read‑lock before TTL checks to avoid refresh races. - Queries/Health/Time: overflow‑safe window/resampling with correct relative‑cache flag; reject negative evaluation frequencies; bound delay‑multiplier casts; saturate uint32 durations; time32‑safe scheduling and elapsed‑time helpers; guard weights point‑limit shifts; release compiled alert‑filter patterns. - Streaming: accept exact‑size gzip/Brotli frames (+1 byte ring capacity); add monotonic‑fallback/rebase helpers; clamp negative initial gaps; validate REPLAY endpoints as bounded base‑10 time_t values and normalize invalid pairs; atomically mark/clear receiver TID ownership. Add a regression test target for replay endpoints. - SQLite: quote migration identifiers with sqlite3_mprintf (%Q/%w); make time32 deadlines safe; restore unit‑test DB handle ownership. - RRDDIM/RRDSET: safe INT32_MIN magnitude checks; normalize zero divisors on update; define collected max at LLONG_MIN; define signed‑boundary deltas; fix homogeneity baseline magnitude. - Registry: order delete‑before‑compaction; enforce machine‑name length/trim policy; add regular‑file open helper and validate predictable temp files. - Gorilla: remove unused unbounded unpatched disk‑chain walkers. - Status: validate temp files via lstat/open/fstat/ftruncate and enforce lock‑free atomics in deadly‑signal paths. - **Docs/OpenAPI** - Quote boolean‑like enum values to avoid YAML 1.1 coercion and align v1 allmetrics aliases; keep v2/v3 bearer true/false as strings for type parity and sync JSON parity members. - Remove stale web‑file owner/group settings and document that static content under `[directories].web` is served using the Agent process’s filesystem permissions. - Add Windows corruption‑signature how‑to; ignore local `/.agents/scout`; note CodeQL dismissal 280‑character limit. Written for commit 07455614d54ebd81b8c5796311e0477d14fd63dd. Summary will update on new commits.

author: werkamsus
body:
## Problem
The desktop app supports workspace sidebar groups through renderer-local `v2SidebarSections` and `v2WorkspaceLocalState`, but the public CLI only exposed workspace create/list/open/update/delete commands. Users had to use the app context menu for `New group from workspace` and `Move to group`.

## Design
- Adds `superset workspaces groups` command family:
  - `list`
  - `create --name <name> [workspace-id...]`
  - `create --name <name> --project <project-id>` for empty groups
  - `move <group-id> <workspace-id...>`
  - `remove <workspace-id...>`
  - `rename <group-id> --name <name>`
  - `delete <group-id>`
- Keeps sidebar groups desktop-local. The CLI reads/writes a per-organization bridge file under Superset Home and does not introduce cloud-side workspace group state.
- Desktop renderer remains the source of truth for sidebar collections. It writes current snapshots to the bridge file and consumes queued CLI operations into `v2SidebarSections` / `v2WorkspaceLocalState`.
- CLI commands optimistically update the bridge snapshot so `groups list` reflects queued changes before the desktop app consumes them.
- State mutations use one lock-protected transaction for validation + queueing + optimistic snapshot updates.

## Review fixes included
- Renderer waits for sidebar project, section, workspace, and local main workspace hydration before publishing snapshots or consuming queued operations.
- Auto-included local main workspaces are materialized into `v2WorkspaceLocalState` before CLI group/move operations apply.
- Queue consumption now claims one operation, applies it, then acknowledges it; failed/not-yet-hydrated operations are released for retry instead of being dropped.
- Ack retry is tracked per organization to avoid replay after lock contention or organization switches.
- Shared state writes validate schema before replacing the file and use atomic temp-file rename.
- File locking now only treats `EEXIST` as contention and removes stale lock directories after timeout-safe expiry.
- CLI delete/remove/move rewrites recalculate top-level tab ordering to avoid duplicate ordering after ungrouping.
- Helper tests use non-alphabetical names to prove `tabOrder` sorting.

## Verification
- `bun test packages/shared/src/sidebar-groups-cli.test.ts packages/cli/src/lib/sidebar-groups.test.ts` — passed, 8 tests / 15 assertions.
- `bun run --cwd packages/shared typecheck` — passed.
- `bun run --cwd packages/cli typecheck` — passed.
- `bun run --cwd apps/desktop typecheck` — passed.
- `bun run lint` — passed, checked 4754 files.

## Branch
- Base: `main`
- Head: `werkamsus:nick/sidebar-group-cli`
- Current commit: `f5bcdf49 Add CLI support for sidebar workspace groups`

Rank 贡献者弹窗点进归属于旧 `docs/community/*` 的文章报 404（#359）。issue 原话：

author: dzhuneyt
body:
## What
Adds `begin`, a local CLI that finds a project under the current directory and drops you into a durable Claude Code tmux session inside it.

- **Fuzzy resolution** — searches downward from the CWD (pruning `node_modules`/`.git`/…); 0 matches → zoxide fallback, 1 → use it, 2+ → picker (`fzf`, else numbered list).
- **Persistent sessions** — runs `claude; exec "$SHELL"` so the session survives Claude exiting (a shell remains in the project dir).
- **Collision-safe naming** — each session is tagged with its absolute project path (`@begin_path`); re-running reattaches the *same* project, and same-basename projects get a parent-qualified name instead of silently attaching to the wrong one.
- **Guards** — bails if already inside tmux; clear errors if `tmux`/`claude` are missing.
- **Install** — clone + symlink `begin/begin` onto `PATH`; the entrypoint self-resolves its symlink (portable, no `readlink -f`) to find `lib/`.

## Why
Across a multi-box dev setup (laptop, NAS, remote Mac Mini), git clones live in different layouts and Claude Code sessions die on disconnect. `begin` gives one muscle-memory command, identical on every box, to land in a durable session in the right project.

## Notes for review
- **Purely local by design** — no ssh/mosh/transport. You get onto a box yourself, then run `begin` there.
- **Decomposed, not a monolith** — a thin entrypoint composes small single-responsibility `lib/` units; pure logic (matching, naming, disambiguation) is split from the tmux/filesystem seams so it's unit-testable.
- **Tests** — 48 bats-core tests run inside the official `bats/bats` Docker image via `begin/tests/run.sh` (no host install, no submodules; a small self-contained assertion shim replaces `bats-assert`/`bats-support`). CI runs them, path-filtered to `begin/**`.
- **Two acceptance checks deferred** (need a real terminal): detach/reattach idempotency and Claude-exit survival. The underlying decisions are asserted via a fake-tmux test.
- Includes the OpenSpec change (`openspec/changes/add-begin-tmux-wrapper/`) that drove the work.

author: roblourens
body:
Fix #323305

Client-provided tool calls running in a session's default chat were being silently dropped: the SDK handler's deferred never resolved, so the agent could hang waiting on a tool result that already came back.

## Why

`ChatToolCallComplete` envelopes are emitted on the chat channel URI, which is formatted as `ahp-chat://<chatId>/<base64(sessionUri)>`. Both call sites in `agentSideEffects.ts` forwarded that chat URI straight to `agent.onClientToolCallComplete(...)`. But every agent keys its `_sessions` map by the raw session id, resolved via `AgentSession.id(uri)` = `uri.path.substring(1)`. For a chat URI the path is the base64 blob, not the session GUID, so the default-chat lookup never matched and the completion was discarded.

## Fix

Forward the resolved session URI (`sessionChannel`, which both sites already computed) for the default chat so `AgentSession.id` yields the GUID. Peer (non-default) chats are tracked separately in `_chatSessions` keyed by the chat URI, so those keep being forwarded as-is via `isDefaultChatUri` check.

This is a call-site translation only; the agent `onClientToolCallComplete` implementations are unchanged. It fixes the copilot, claude, and codex agents at once.

## Note

I could not run the type-checker or tests in this worktree because `node_modules` is not installed. The change is small, reuses the already-imported `isDefaultChatUri` helper and in-scope `sessionChannel`, and the pre-commit hygiene hook passed.

(Written by Copilot)

author: stxkxs
body:
First piece of the portal force-unwedge break-glass (M3). When a vend wedges (provider-opentofu's `external-create-pending` blocks create *and* delete), the half-built cluster's resources are stranded. This is the bounded, delete-only teardown role portal's owner-only force-unwedge action assumes.

## Why a dedicated role (not the vend role)

The vend role *can* already delete a cluster's orphans, but reusing it would mean widening its trust to portal. Instead:
- **Trusted by portal's management-account role**, not the hub — vending stays the hub's, the vend role's trust never widens, and an unwedge is unambiguous in CloudTrail.
- **Delete-only** — separation of duties; it can never create.

## Scoping (condition keys AWS-docs-verified, not guessed)

Every cluster-stack resource carries `ProvisionedBy=eks-fleet` (provider `default_tags`), so destructive actions are tag-conditioned to fleet-provisioned resources — an untagged resource is denied (a stuck teardown, never a wider blast radius). I verified each destructive action's `aws:ResourceTag` support against the AWS service-authorization reference; that drove the statements:

| Statement | Scope |
|---|---|
| `TeardownTagged` | required-resource-type deletes (EC2/EKS/Logs/KMS-key/SQS/EventBridge/ASG/ELBv2) — `Resource:"*"` + tag condition (required type forces the tag to evaluate) |
| `TeardownTaggedElasticIP` / `TeardownTaggedEventRules` | optional-type actions — Resource pinned to the typed ARN so `"*"` can't bypass the tag gate |
| `TeardownKmsAlias` | aliases are untaggable → eks-fleet alias-name prefix |
| `TeardownClusterIAM` / `…Policies` | `/eks-fleet/` path-scoped (the gate fleet-vend uses) |
| `TeardownOIDCProvider` | no path/tag → `oidc-provider/*` under the boundary (small fleet-owned set) |

Carries an escalation boundary mirroring fleet-vend (no principals/org/account/boundary-strip/self-modify) and publishes its ARN to SSM.

## Verification
`tofu fmt`, `tofu init -backend=false && tofu validate`, `tflint`, and the zero-placeholder gate all pass locally. No hardcoded account ids/regions (all from `aws_caller_identity` / vars). Per-account live wiring + a real wedged-vend teardown are the deploy-time (🔒) validation.

Next: the portal `FleetUnwedgeService` (idempotent ordered teardown via this role) + the owner-only UI.

author: illia1f
body:
## Summary

Field-selected reads let callers fetch only the metadata they need, and Google Workspace MIME-type knowledge now lives on `MimeType`.

## What changed

- `DriveFields`: an immutable, composable field selector. It starts from `Default` (the core `id`, `name`, `mimeType`) and you chain `With*` calls. `WithRaw` keeps verbatim nested selectors.
- Field-selected overloads of `ListAsync`, `ListAllAsync`, and `FindByIdAsync` take a `DriveFields` and return the raw `Google.Apis.Drive.v3.Data.File`, so an unset property means the field was not requested rather than absent.
- `GetRequestExtensions.WithDefaultOnNotFound` wraps a `Files.Get` so a `404` returns `null`. A `403` and other errors still propagate.
- `MimeType` now owns the constants that used to live in `GDriveMimeTypes`, plus `IsGoogleWorkspace` and `GetExportMimeType()` for Workspace export formats.
- Docs, samples, and unit tests updated to the new model.

## Breaking changes

- `GDriveMimeTypes` is removed. Use the `MimeType` constants such as `MimeType.Folder`.
- `DriveItem.ParentIds` is removed. Request parents with `DriveFields.WithParents()`.

Engine-side support for two TP-Combat features.

The upgrade ring reused the item-explain widget but fed it **raw strings** via `openExplainText`, bypassing the JMessage tag pipeline — so it could not show button glyphs, colored runs, or bullets like the vanilla item box.
